## Bug fix: editor "+" tooltips never showed (hitTest shields panel-level tooltips)

The reworded "+" tooltips still didn't appear: `emitEditorPlusCell` carried
the tooltip on the `nine_slice_panel`, with the spriteless interactive
button emitted on top covering the exact same rect. `hitTest` (element.zig)
walks top-to-bottom and HALTS at the first blocking element that fails the
predicate — the button (no tooltip, blocks input) shielded the panel's
tooltip underneath, so it could never spawn. The tooltip now rides the
BUTTON (the convention every working tooltip already used — tool cells,
level tabs, group headers), pinned by the add-level test asserting the
button's header text "Add Level" and the panel carrying none.

Swept the tree for other victims of the same pattern: none (the
entity-inspect skill grid's image-carried tooltip sits topmost; slot
tooltips are on the interactive slot itself). The doc comment on
`emitEditorPlusCell` records the rule: a tooltip on an element drawn under
a blocking element never shows.

## Editor palette: an expanded EMPTY group's header rises to the strip too

Expanding a tool group with no tools left its header + "+" pinned flush
against the bottom of the screen — the placement condition was
`collapsed or size == 0`, so "empty" read as "collapsed" for placement.
Now `header_y` keys off `collapsed` only: an expanded group rises to the
strip above the bar whether or not it has cells to label. The footprint
math KEEPS its `or size == 0` (an empty group's row extent is still just
the header + "+", so the neighboring group's header can't overlap it) —
the two conditions are now intentionally different, noted in the comment.
Test: the collapsed/expanded placement test gains an empty-Decorations
expanded build asserting header + "+" both sit at the hovering y.

## Editor palette: adding a tool expands its group + scrolls to the new cell

The palette "+" (add-new type) left the accordion alone — a new tool could
land in a collapsed group (invisible until expanded) or beyond the group's
8-cell window (invisible until scrolled). The `.add_editor_palette_type`
input arm now, after a successful add (post load_error revert gate):
expands the target group with the header-toggle accordion discipline (the
others collapse), and scrolls the group's window to
`size -| editor_palette_max_tools` — the new type (always appended last by
the handler) becomes the window's last visible cell, which is also the
MINIMAL scroll that shows it. View-side display state, off the undo
timeline (the toggle branch's class); a failed/reverted add touches
nothing.

Tests: the add-path test now drives all-groups-expanded going in and
asserts the accordion after each of the three "+" clicks (one group open,
the other two collapsed); a new test with 9 preset enemy types asserts
offset 10 -| 8 = 2 with the accordion.

## Mission browser: the Your Missions tab sorts newest first (max file mtime)

The local tab had NO explicit sort — entries rendered in `Dir.iterate`
order (filesystem-implementation-defined; looked alphabetical on the
author's machine by coincidence). Now `listMissions` sorts NEWEST FIRST,
keyed by `MissionEntry.mtime_ns` = the MAX mtime across the mission
folder's files — the settled semantics: ANY file change is an update
(editor save, custom png drop, zip import, validation-replay write all
count), matching the load-save browser's proven ordering + tiebreak
discipline (mtime descending, name ascending). Considered and rejected:
a persisted `last_modified` stamp in mission.txt (travels through zips
but needs an mtime fallback for every non-editor-authored mission
anyway, and starts the mission file-format-version clock TODO defers).

`hasMissionCustomAssets` folded into `scanMissionFolder` returning both
flags + the stamp (the custom-asset check already enumerates the folder's
files platform-safely — the stat pass rides it; web stats each file
through the persistent dir, the `listSaveFilesWeb`-proven pattern).
Official entries keep `mtime_ns = 0` (embedded, no filesystem) and the
Official tab keeps its comptime order. Web branch verified by compile
(`scripts/web.sh` — emrun spot-check unnecessary: the per-file stat
pattern is the save-listing's, already running on the mount).

Tests: the populated scan test now asserts the defined order + mtime
sanity (sleep between missions per the save-test tie discipline); a new
recency test (png dropped into the OLDER mission bumps it to the front —
max-across-files, not mission.txt-only); a comparator unit test pinning
the name tiebreak + mtime-0-last.

## Entity inspect: Momentum row + dead-target handling (view-gated, corpse shadowing fixed)

Three pieces:

- **Momentum stat row** (panels.zig): the inspect stat column's live-
  combat lead is now Current Health, **Momentum**, Aggro Range (raw
  `entity.momentum` — no effect modifier exists for momentum itself, it
  feeds `getEffectiveOutgoingDamage`). Both inspect-panel tests pin the
  sequence (adjacency, not just presence; count 9→10).

- **Dead target renders no panel** (view.zig): the `.entity_inspect` arm
  + `buildInspectedAggroOutline` skip when the target's
  `current_health == 0` — the mission-fail-overlay precedent (death
  derivable from health, no flag or event), so close-on-death needed no
  handler change and undo reopens the panel for free. Chosen over the
  handler-close variant because NO handler in the codebase writes
  `ui_state` (exclusively the input layer's) — the handler-close would
  have been the first exception. Known quirk accepted: while the target
  is dead the panel's open slot lingers invisibly (heals on the next
  inspect).

- **Corpse shadowing fixed at the press site** (input_gestures.zig): the
  right-press loop took the FIRST entity on the tile with no health
  check — but corpses keep their tile (death removes nothing) and living
  entities can stand on one (dead entities don't block movement), so a
  lower-index corpse shadowed the living entity standing on it. The loop
  now skips the dead and keeps scanning: first LIVING entity wins; a
  tile holding only corpses inspects nothing (and can never open the
  panel on a dead target, keeping the view-gate coherent). Test: shared
  tile with lower-index corpse + living entity → the living one; lone
  corpse tile → pending cleared.

## Input: binding contexts (slice 1 — the context model)

Settled design: DESIGN → Input (Binding contexts + Action↔context validity
+ New keybind wiring sites). What landed:

- **`BindingContext` + `BindingContextSet`** (types.zig): `anytime` / `game`
  (level+hub) / `editor` / `menu` (main menu) / `error_popup`. Named
  `error_popup` because `error` is a Zig keyword (can't be a bare enum
  value). `menu` was added beyond the initially-agreed
  anytime/game/editor/error set: the exhaustive classification switch needs
  SOME context for main-menu-only actions (continue_game, load-save browser,
  open_editor, …) — button-only today, classified for honesty + the future
  binding UI; zero behavioral effect (no menu-context bindings ship).
- **`InputBinding.context`** — a REQUIRED field (no default), so every
  construction site states it and the compiler surfaces them all.
- **`actionBindingContexts`** — the exhaustive no-else switch over Action
  classifying each action into its valid contexts (the "where does this
  action fire" single declaration). Multi-screen actions carry multiple
  flags: `exit_to_menu` + `continue_after_mission` {game, editor} (the
  editor's options menu / the validation stats overlay over the editor);
  `open_settings` + `change_setting` {menu, game}. `overwrite_validation_
  replay` + `validate_editor_mission` are editor (the stats screen renders
  over the editor).
- **Gating** — `frame()` computes the active set (pending_error →
  `{error_popup}` ONLY, mirroring/preceding the handler-side modal gate;
  else screen context + anytime) and threads it into `translateInput`;
  `checkAction`/`isActionHeld`/`isSuppressed` skip inactive-context bindings
  (an inactive binding is not a precedence competitor). Editor
  playtest/validation runs are `.level` screens → game set active, editor
  set dormant — free, no special cases. Button clicks (`applyAction`)
  bypass the gate; buttons only render in their context.
- **Load-time validation** — `loadSettings` gained a `warnings` out-param
  (null on the shipped-defaults path via `loadSettingsWrapped` — the file is
  round-trip-tested; real warnings on the user-file overlay path). Warn +
  drop: missing/unknown `context`, unknown action, or an action bound in a
  context it never fires in. A dropped entry counts as unmentioned → its
  default (context included) is injected — the one existing context-less
  user install self-heals: one boot of warnings, then the next debounced
  full-format write persists the context lines. `settings_file_format_
  version` deliberately NOT bumped (old files parse + migrate rather than
  being rejected wholesale — scalars survive).
- **`save_game` editor-run gate** (input_handlers options_action arm):
  no-op while `editor.mode != .edit` — the run's player_data is throwaway,
  same reasoning as the view hiding Export Save mid-run. Button-only action
  today, so the gate is the defensive half for a future keybind (the
  user-requested "saving player disabled when testing/validating").
- **Files**: parser whitelist += `context`; `writeSettings` emits it;
  `data/default_settings.txt` — all 38 bindings carry explicit context
  lines (author decision: explicit everywhere, no implicit anytime).
- **Tests**: context-gated firing (ArrowUp game/error_popup pair — exactly
  one fires per active set; Digit1 skill-slot/select-tool pair), the
  rewritten ctrl+S dispatch test (editor set), warn+drop+inject for
  context-less entries, warn+drop for invalid action-context pairs +
  unknown actions, writeSettings context round-trip. The old
  "equal-specificity ties co-fire" test was REPLACED — its premise (the
  ArrowUp dual-bind co-firing) is exactly what contexts removed.

Why contexts over the old implicit co-fire: the shipped ArrowUp pattern
relied on handler ordering (the popup branch consuming scroll + returning
first) — undocumented at the binding sites and unscalable to the editor's
1–5 keybinds (slice 2, see TODO). Contexts make the disambiguation
declarative (the binding file states where a combo fires), give load-time
validation a real rule (same combo + same context is the only collision
class left, and the remaining un-validated case is documented), and the
future binding-UI gets its grouping for free.

## Input: editor tool/palette keybinds (slice 2 — Digit1–5)

Settled design: DESIGN → Input (Binding contexts) + DESIGN → Level Editor →
Editor UI layout (tool palette). The five keybinds the context model was
built for:

- **Bindings** (`data/default_settings.txt`, all `context editor`):
  Digit1 → `editor_select_tool`, Digit2 → `editor_tile_tool`, Digit3/4/5 →
  `toggle_editor_enemy/decoration/item_group`. Digit1–8 remain the in-game
  skill slots (`context game`) — the first shipped same-combo
  cross-context pair; the context gate resolves it upstream, so pressing 1
  in-game never touches the editor tool and vice versa (pinned by tests
  both directions). No backend key-table edit (Digit1–8 were already
  mapped for the skill slots — the usual missing-site trap didn't apply).

- **The bridge, not new handler arms.** The five are payload-less
  keybind-only Actions (no button carries them — `applyAction` has an
  explicit no-op case). `translateInput` maps each onto the EXACT
  `options_action` + payload pair the button-release dispatch produces for
  the equivalent click (`.select_editor_tool` + `clicked_editor_tool` /
  `.toggle_editor_palette_group` + `clicked_editor_group`), so the existing
  consumption sites serve both input paths with zero new handler code and
  identical semantics: the tool switch pushes `player_set_editor_tool`
  (undo timeline, same-value no-op, editor-gated), the group toggle is the
  accordion UiState write. Same-frame keypress + button release on the
  same action is degenerate (the button's payload lands last and wins).
  Consumption choice: `handleAnytimeInput`'s options_action path (the
  tool-cell click path), not `handleIdleInput`'s editor arm — tool
  switching is a palette interaction and the editor has no waits, so
  stack-state gating would add nothing.

- **Tests**: the bridge end-to-end through `translateInput` on the editor
  set (all five payloads correct, skill slots silent) and on the game set
  (skill slots fire, no editor bridge) — the ctrl+S dispatch-test pattern
  (pin the dispatch, not just checkAction).

- Digit6–8 have no editor binding yet — free for future editor shortcuts
  if wanted; nothing reserves them.

## Bug fix: error popup scrolling (built day one, broken until first real use)

Surface: the user booted with the new binding-context settings and the
startup warning popup finally got scrolled for real — revealing three
compounding bugs in the one scroller that predated every other scroller in
the game (built with the error-handling slice 1, never exercised until
now; the other scrollers that later defined the conventions — skills
panel, inspector, browsers, palette — were all built correct).

- **Wheel direction flipped**: the gate ADDED `scroll_delta` to the offset
  (positive delta = wheel up = should scroll toward the top = offset
  decreases; every other scroll site does `offset -= delta`). Fixed: the
  game-wide sign convention.
- **Window drawn at its unscrolled position**: the view emitted the
  window's lines but placed them at `body_top + first_visible_line ×
  line_height` — blank space above, bottom lines overflowing the panel
  ("renders the wrong text, cuts it off weirdly"). Fixed: the window's
  first line renders AT the body region's top.
- **Step unit out of sync with the view**: the input stepped in pixels
  using a hardcoded `error_scroll_line_height` (56) while the view's line
  height is `lineHeight(56) = 67` — offsets were never line-aligned, so
  the window math (`@divTrunc(offset, line_height)`) was garbage on every
  scrolled frame.

The fix aligns the popup with the settled game-wide scroll convention
instead of patching the pixel model: `error_scroll_offset` is now the
index of the first visible body LINE (rows, not pixels); wheel = one line
per notch (wheel-up = earlier lines, offset decreases, lower clamp at the
input site); arrows = 3 lines per press; the view clamps the upper bound
in place (authoritative — only it knows the wrapped line count) and emits
exactly the visible window drawn from the body top, whole lines only (the
region height is a multiple of the line height, so placement is identical
at every offset). The hardcoded `error_scroll_line_height` constant is
DELETED (the view derives everything from `lineHeight`; the input steps in
lines, so no pixel constant exists to drift).

Also discovered while writing tests: `wrapRow` does NOT treat `\n` as a
line break (width-only breaking at spaces and '/') — the old tests'
"60 lines" comments were wrong (their messages flowed into ~25 wrapped
lines); the new tests use width-deterministic 40-char tokens so the
wrapped line count is exact (60 lines, 23 visible, max_scroll 37) and the
scrolled window is assertable by content ("line 10 renders at the body
top") and position, not just counts.

Tests: window content + placement + exact clamp (screens.zig), wheel sign
+ line steps + lower clamp + dismiss (input_handlers.zig, direct
handleAnytimeInput through the pending_error gate). Design: DESIGN →
Error Handling → Recoverable error surface (scrolling paragraph).

## Bug fix: wrapRow must break on '\n' (overlapping lines in the error popup)

Follow-up to the scroll fix above, same popup, same first real use. Symptom:
with the multi-warning startup message, "lines overlap each other, layout
weird — I think we're dropping linebreaks."

Root cause — a measurement/rendering disagreement over the newline:

- The startup warnings are joined with `\n` (session_setup, one warning per
  line).
- `wrapRow` (the layout authority) treated `\n` as an ordinary character:
  it isn't a space or '/', so the token-run loop consumed straight past it —
  `\n` rode INSIDE a word token ("dropped\nInputBindings"), measured as one
  line on one visual row.
- raylib's `DrawTextEx` (verified in the vendored rtext.c) treats `'\n'` as
  a line break: `textOffsetY += fontSize + textLineSpacing`, x reset. So
  the label drew a SECOND, unmeasured line at y+71 (at 56px font) while the
  next visual row's labels sat at y+67 — the two text bodies drew on top of
  each other, and the internal line restarted at the span's x, scrambling
  placement. Every symptom matched.

The fix is at the layout authority, not the renderer: `wrapRow` now treats
`\n` (and `\r`, tolerating Windows endings) as a HARD line break — flush the
current line, drop the pending space, drop the character. No emitted span
ever contains a raw newline, so measurement and rendering agree by
construction (stripping `\n` in drawTextLabel instead would have thrown away
the intended line structure). Consecutive breaks collapse (no blank lines —
the warning list wants one entry per line, no gap noise, and a trailing
break must not add a trailing blank row). First fix attempt missed that the
check must ALSO end the token-run loop — a check at the loop top alone never
sees a `\n` the run loop consumed past (caught immediately by the new test).

Also fixed in passing: wrapRow's doc claimed a too-wide word "sits alone on
its line and is allowed to overflow" — stale; the code (and the doc now)
says it character-wraps into fitting chunks.

Tests: wrapRow hard-break semantics (break, char dropped, `\r\n` collapsed,
no newline in any span, interior spaces kept); buildErrorPopup end-to-end
(two `\n`-joined warnings → two visual lines exactly one lineHeight apart,
no label carries a newline). Sweep: no other UI text source emits `\n`
(authored strings only; the renderer-side break was never something anyone
relied on). Design: the wrapRow contract is its doc comment in
element.zig; DESIGN → Error Handling → Recoverable error surface notes the
newline join + the contract.

## Skills: focus-fire AI target selection (weakestTarget)

The AI target-selection convention for attack skills, set before the Tier A
skill-design batch lands (~20 new skills — the convention had to be settled
first so they're all born consistent). Decision: focus-fire —
`selectTarget` picks the hostile with the LOWEST current health; ties break
by Chebyshev distance to the caster, then entity index (total, deterministic
order). Rationale: concentrating damage on nearly-dead enemies kills them
sooner than nearest-first; strictly more effective in practice.

- `helpers.weakestTarget` (skills/helpers.zig) implements the ordering once;
  resolves each valid-target position back to its entity via
  `hostileEntityAt` (skips a stale position defensively rather than
  panicking — lists come from getValidTargets, so a miss means a crafted
  input, and selectTarget is advisory for the AI).
- 13 single-target offensive skills switched (slice, stab, chop, cleave,
  throw, toss, impale, skewer, bash, retreating_swipe, vampiric_strike,
  spark, daze). Daze included deliberately: one uniform rule for every
  hostile-targeting single-target skill (control skills too) beats
  special-casing; revisit only if control targeting ever wants threat
  awareness instead.
- `nearestTarget` KEEPT for Swap (not an attack; swapping with the nearest
  enemy is the sensible tactical read). Not dead code.
- Barely observable live today: enemy casters usually see exactly one
  hostile (the player, entity 0), so weakest == nearest in practice. The
  convention matters for the new skills + future multi-entity teams.
- Tests: `src/skill_tests.zig` (new file — direct contract tests on the
  pure Skill-interface fns, the convention the Tier A skills follow):
  health-beats-proximity, health-tie → distance, full-tie → entity index
  (target list reversed to prove list order can't decide), null/empty,
  and nearestTarget's still-nearest behavior.
- Convention recorded in DESIGN → Determinism & Tiebreaking (it owns the
  explicit tiebreak conventions); TODO → Skill Logic now carries the full
  Tier A/B/C triage of the remaining designs (the open design questions —
  drain's heal scope, chain lightning's connection rule, diamond form vs
  collision counterplay, etc. — live inline there).

## Skill: crossbow Shoot (Tier A slice 1)

First of the Tier A batch (the unimplemented Unity skill designs that need
no engine changes). Shoot: the crossbow's first skill (main hand, no
cooldown) — attack target for 1x main-hand damage + retreat 1 tile, range 3.
Exactly RetreatingSwipe's shape at range, with plain 1x damage.

- src/skills/shoot.zig — standard 5-fn Skill; priority flat 2 (the
  always-available basic rating, toss precedent; the 1-tile retreat doesn't
  earn a 3); selectTarget on weakestTarget (the new focus-fire convention).
- src/skill_tests.zig grows the per-skill contract-test convention: useSkill
  emits attack+retreat with main-hand damage (asserting the LIFO order —
  ownedEvents returns execution order reversed), useSkill no-ops on an empty
  target tile, priority 0/2 by range + the cooldown map (a swap can leave a
  cooldown on a no-cooldown skill — that's why priority still checks it),
  getValidTargets filters team/dead/range.
- Not yet equippable in-game: WeaponType enum + weapon-type data wiring is
  the separate tracked TODO (crossbow + idol).

## Skills: knockback target selection (knockbackTarget) + crossbow Powerful Shot (Tier A slice 2)

Second convention interjection of the Tier A batch, landed with Powerful
Shot because the skill motivated it. Knockback skills now select targets by:
would-collide FIRST (the collision adds damage), then the focus-fire tail
(lowest health, then distance to caster, then entity index).

- `helpers.knockbackWouldCollide` — the push-collision prediction extracted
  from bash's priority so prediction and the knockback handler can't drift
  (same rule: per-axis sign direction away from the caster; missing tile or
  living occupant = collision; the defender itself and dead entities are not
  obstacles). Takes the caster's EFFECTIVE push distance.
- `helpers.knockbackTarget` — the 4-key selection (collide, health,
  distance, entity index). selectTarget has no allocator param, so it's a
  min-scan over a candidate key rather than a filter + weakestTarget
  compose; the tail keys match weakestTarget by doc contract.
- Bash REFACTORED onto both: priority is now the flat any-collide bump (3 if
  ANY in-range target's push collides, else 2 — was nearest-target-only,
  which under-reported when the nearest target stood in the open but a
  second adjacent one was walled), selectTarget on knockbackTarget. The
  bump and the selection now agree by construction.
- Powerful Shot (crossbow skill 2, main hand, cd 2): attack + knockback,
  +0.5x effective outgoing as collision damage, range 3, distance 2 —
  bash's shape at range, on both new helpers.
- Tests: knockbackWouldCollide (edge / occupant / clear path / dead
  occupant), knockbackTarget (collide beats weaker open-field target; no
  collisions → weakest), bash priority any-collide (the scan-first-open +
  second-walled case that distinguishes any from nearest), powerful shot
  useSkill (half collision damage 7→3, distance 2) + priority.

## Skill: crossbow Head Shot (Tier A slice 3)

Crossbow complete (3/3 skills). Head Shot: skill 3 (off hand, cd 4) — attack
target for 1x off-hand damage + stun 1, range 3. Cleave's shape at range
with off-hand damage; conventions identical: flat priority 3 (the stun
rating — durations stack via the handler's `+=`, so an already-stunned
target is not a wasted pick), weakestTarget selection, outgoing stun
modifier applied at the skill site. Tests: useSkill (off-hand damage,
stun payload, LIFO order) + priority 0/3/cooldown.

## Skill: idol Heal (Tier A slice 4)

Idol 1/3. Heal: skill 1 (main hand, no cooldown, turn-ending weapon skill)
— self-heal for 20% of max health, no targeting (the replenish template:
getValidTargets/selectTarget/playerPrepareSkill all null, useSkill ignores
the target param).

Priority decision worth recording: 3 only BELOW half health, 0 at/above
(the replenish threshold logic). The tempting alternative — rate whenever
below full — would tie the attack skills at 2, and ties resolve by slot
order, so the idol would spend EVERY turn topping off instead of attacking.
The half threshold means it heals only when meaningfully wounded (and being
a 20% heal, it climbs back over half in a couple of turns, not forever).
Heal amount getEffectiveMaxHealth()/5 (the stone-form end-of-turn precedent
for "20% of max"). Tests: heal amount truncation on an awkward value
(23/5 → 4), null targeting surface, priority at full/exactly-half/below-
half + the swap-inherited cooldown case.

## Bug fix: stun takes the max, not the sum (anti-stunlock) + stun-aware AI

The stun handler did `stun_duration += effective_duration` — consecutive
stuns STACKED. Intent (surfaced while porting Head Shot): a player facing
multiple stunning enemies must not be mega-stunlocked, so a new stun takes
the MAX of current vs incoming; a shorter stun on an already-stunned target
changes nothing, a longer one replaces it. (This also invalidated the
reasoning recorded in the Head Shot entry above — "stun durations stack, so
an already-stunned target is not a wasted pick" — written hours before the
rule was caught.)

The AI mirrors the rule so it doesn't waste stuns:
- `helpers.stunTarget` — new selection for single-target stun skills:
  unstunned first, then the focus-fire tail. Restructured the selection
  family while adding it: a shared `TargetCandidate` + `focusFireTailLessThan`
  (health → distance → entity index, the convention in ONE place) +
  `preferredThenTailLessThan`; weakestTarget now scans via the shared tail
  comparator, knockbackTarget via the preferred-then-tail one (its local
  Candidate/anytype comparator removed). No signature changes.
- cleave + head_shot: priority 3 with any unstunned target in range, 2 when
  only stunned targets remain (the attack still pays), 0 otherwise;
  selection on stunTarget.
- daze (no damage): 3 unstunned; 2 stunned-with-momentum (the drain still
  pays); 0 stunned-and-momentumless (nothing to gain). Selection on
  stunTarget — note the residual seam: among all-stunned targets the tail
  is health-based, so daze can pick a momentumless target while its 2
  rating was earned by a different one; rare, one wasted turn at most,
  accepted rather than growing a momentum key into the helper.
- slam/blitz (AoE stunners) untouched: no target choice, and their damage
  component pays regardless of stun state.
- Rule recorded in DESIGN → Architecture (the stun-rule paragraph on the
  events bullet); the Determinism focus-fire bullet now describes the
  selection FAMILY (tail + preference keys).

Tests: handler regression (pre-stunned 2 → new 1 stays 2, new 3 → rises
to 3), stunTarget (unstunned beats weaker stunned; all-stunned → weakest),
priority tiers for cleave (3/2), head_shot (2 stunned-only), daze (3/2/0).

## Skills: AI threat model (deals_damage + threat.zig) + idol Absorb (Tier A slice 5)

Idol 2/3, landed with the threat-model interjection it motivated. Absorb:
skill 2 (main hand, cd 5, turn-ending) — self-cast create_effect for one
round; the effect is an interceptor (reflect's shape) that zeroes incoming
ATTACK damage and heals the receiver for the pre-defense amount (attack-
only by the interceptor rule — collision damage still lands, the deliberate
Reflect counterplay). effect_sprite null until art ships (only
reflect.png/stun.png exist).

The threat model (design in DESIGN → Architecture, "AI threat model"):
- `Skill.deals_damage` — required field (no default; a forgotten flag on a
  future damaging skill would silently under-report threat). 19 true / 10
  false across the 29 existing skills.
- `priority_fn` widened to receive `weapon_type_definitions` (new alias
  `types.WeaponTypeDefinitions`): slot resolution needs the session's
  weapon-type → skills mapping — the same GameStateHistory constraint that
  forced Focus to be an orchestrator. One production call site
  (enemy_turn_attack, which has history in scope); 30 fns gained a mostly-
  ignored param.
- `skills/threat.zig` (excluded from the SkillId scan; imports
  generated_lookups directly — imports no skill file, so no cycle):
  computeMinRange MOVED here from handlers/level.zig, new
  computeMaxDamageRange (damaging-only max of effective range ?? radius),
  new hostileCanAttackNextTurn (alive + active + unstunned + within
  effective speed + max damaging reach, Chebyshev). Deliberate design call
  kept from the discussion: computeMinRange still counts ALL usable skills
  — min answers "when can I act" (a Daze-only enemy should cast from 3),
  max answers "how far can I hurt".
- Absorb + Reflect priorities on the predicate: 0 unthreatened (absorbing
  into the void wastes the cooldown), 2 threatened, 4 threatened + below
  half (4 must beat Heal's 3 on the idol bar). Reflect's old heuristic —
  flat 4 on ANY hostile within 2 tiles — ignored speed, range, cooldowns,
  stun, and aggro; an idle unaggroed enemy could bait the cooldown.

Tests: computeMaxDamageRange (main-only 1, +off-hand 3, cooldown fallback,
unarmed null), hostileCanAttackNextTurn (reach geometry, stun, aggro,
unarmed), absorb useSkill/priority tiers + the interceptor unit contract,
reflect priority tiers incl. the unaggroed-bait regression, and a handler-
level integration test (attack into absorb → 10+5=15; a 999-damage hit
heals to max instead of killing).

## Skills: AoE priority bump + idol Drain (Tier A slice 6)

Idol complete (3/3). New AI convention, motivated by Drain: every radius
skill's priority bumps +1 when two or more hostiles would be hit — an AoE's
value scales with hit count.

- `helpers.aoePriority(target_count, base)` — the convention as ONE
  function (0 / base / base+1) so callers can't drift;
  `helpers.hostileCountWithinRadius(caster, state, center, radius)` —
  allocation-free (priority fns have no allocator), center-parameterized
  so a skill can count around an arbitrary point, not just itself.
- Retrofits: spinblade + slam (3 → 4 on two targets), blitz (4 → 5), howl
  (1 → 2; it counts INACTIVE entities of any team — aggro_in_radius
  rallies same-team entities too — but shares the bump arithmetic).
- flash_strike: the interesting one. Its AoE centers on the LANDING tile,
  so "targets that would be hit" = max over candidate empty tiles in range
  of hostileCountWithinRadius(tile, radius). This also fixed a latent flaw:
  its old rating was a flat 3 whenever off cooldown — no target check at
  all, so an enemy could flash into empty space; a cast with no reachable
  hit now rates 0. Residual seam (accepted, daze-momentum-shaped):
  selectTarget still picks the tile NEAREST a hostile, not the max-hit
  tile, so a 4 rating earned by one landing spot can land on another.
- Drain: idol skill 3 (off hand, cd 5) — spinblade's shape with off-hand
  damage, every attack carrying heals_attacker. Settles the triage's open
  question: PER-TARGET lifesteal (the flag heals the post-defense applied
  damage, which the skill can't know ahead of the handler); a "heal for
  the total" reading would need post-batch accumulation machinery and
  leave Tier A. Priority 3/4 on the bump — the lifesteal is a rider, not a
  tier: threatened + below half, Absorb's 4 wins (ties resolve to Absorb
  by slot order anyway) — prevention first.

Tests: aoePriority table, hostileCountWithinRadius (incl. the
diagonal-counts-as-1 case that caught my own wrong expectation), spinblade
bump, flash_strike best-landing-tile max + the no-target regression,
drain useSkill (per-hit heals_attacker, off-hand damage) + priority 3/4,
howl bump.

## Skills: unified AI options (priority + selectTarget → ai_options_fn)

The double-work fix, landed before porting the remaining ~14 Tier A skills
(so they're born on the unified interface). Old shape: priority fn = a
SUMMARY over targets ("3 if any collides", "count in radius"), selectTarget
fn = a separate argmax over a different key — the seams we kept documenting
(bash, daze-momentum, flash-strike landing, stab any-healthy). New shape:
ONE fn, `ai_options_fn`, enumerating the skill's meaningful casts as
(target, rating) pairs, best-first; the skill-side rating and the target are
a single decision. The handler (enemy_turn_attack) collects options across
equipped off-cooldown skills, keeps the ending/non-ending pools, picks
(priority desc, option order, slot order) — options arrive best-first, so
the ordering conventions (focus-fire tail, collide/unstunned keys, AoE bump)
live in emission order. Player path untouched (getValidTargets /
player_prepare_skill / use_skill / legality validation all unchanged).

- `skill.zig`: `AiOption{target, priority}` + `ai_options_fn` (+ `aiOptions`
  convenience); `priority_fn`/`select_target_fn` and their convenience
  methods removed; PORTING NOTE rewritten for options (Unity -1 = emit
  nothing). `helpers.singleOption` added (the one-best-cast emitter; helpers
  now imports skill.zig for AiOption — no cycle, skill.zig imports no skill
  files).
- 31 skills migrated via a one-shot script (asserted every transformation).
  Most emit one option built from the existing helpers at the existing
  ratings. Deliberate behavior changes — the seams closing:
  - **stab** rates its actual pick (wounded weakest + healthy bystander → 2,
    not the old any-healthy 3) — regression-tested.
  - **daze** emits two target classes (unstunned at 3, stunned-with-momentum
    at 2, focus-fire order within each) instead of rating "any" and picking
    weakest — a stunned momentumless weakest can no longer waste the cast.
  - **flash strike** option target IS the max-hit landing tile (old
    selectTarget picked the tile nearest a hostile) — asserted.
  - **blink** offers nothing when no empty tile helps (old pair could choose
    it and cast a no-op); **howl/blink/etc.** all keep their ratings.
- Handler: `SkillOption` struct, single pass over options, drop the
  definition-tracking vars + the now-unused `Skill` import; computeMinRange
  unchanged (already in threat.zig).
- Tests: 39 rating assertions mechanically converted to option-list form;
  bash/flash-strike/daze upgraded to also assert the option TARGET (the
  unified decision made visible); new stab seam-fix regression test.
- Docs: DESIGN → Architecture gains the "AI options" bullet (the unified
  decision surface, above the threat-model + AoE-bump bullets that ride
  it); the Determinism focus-fire bullet now speaks of AI options picking.

## Skill: spell Worldfire (Tier A slice 7)

First spell, and the first skill born on the unified ai_options interface
(one self-centered option, aoePriority(count, 3) — trivial on the new
shape). Radius 5, cd 10, `deals_damage`. Damage-source decision: spells
draw on Entity.getEffectiveSpellDamage (amulet base + gloves bonus +
converted momentum + outgoing modifier) — the method already existed,
mirroring getEffectiveOutgoingDamage, and it's the number the curse
designs ("increase damage by spell damage") reference, so the amulet is
the spell-casting stat by construction. Priority base 3 on the AoE bump
encodes "save it for clusters" for free: a single-target cast ties the
basic attack at 3 and loses to slot order (cheaper weapon skill fires);
a cluster rates 4 and the nuke goes off exactly when it should.

Census tests grew with the first utility-eligible spell:
utility_skills 7 → 8 (the test's comment anticipated this), the editor
skill-picker element/button counts 19→21 / 8→9. Tests: useSkill
(Chebyshev-diagonal edge at (3,4) hits, (6,0) doesn't, amulet spell
damage 6 on every hit) + options 3/4 + the cooldown gate.

## Skills: stacked-bump ladder + spell Shockwave (Tier A slice 8)

Second spell. Shockwave: radius 1, distance 2, cd 5 — per hostile in
radius, attack for 1x effective spell damage then knock back with +0.5x
collision (bash's pair, AoE'd; the knockback handler no-ops dead defenders
so a killing attack doesn't push a corpse). Born on ai_options.

The new convention it motivated — the STACKED-BUMP ladder: an AoE skill
with multiple value components adds +1 per component that pays beyond the
base. AoE-knockback skills: base + 1 (two or more targets) + 1 (any
target's push would collide). "Any collides" is honest for an AoE — the
cast has no target choice, so a colliding target genuinely adds value to
that exact cast (contrast old bash's summary seam). Helpers:
collidingTargetCount (allocation-free, reuses knockbackWouldCollide so
prediction can't drift) + aoeKnockbackPriority (the ladder in one place,
next to aoePriority). Slam RETROFITTED onto the ladder — its damage IS the
1x collision, so the old AoE-bump-only rating under-sold clustered+walled
casts (4 → now 5; single-target unchanged at 3). Blitz stays on plain
aoePriority (no knockback; different weapon bar, no competition).

Tests: aoeKnockbackPriority table, collidingTargetCount (caught my own
layout bug — the "out of radius" entity stood on the open target's push
path and was a genuine second collision), shockwave useSkill (attack+
knockback pairs, 7/2=3 collision, LIFO order) + full ladder 3/4/5, slam
retrofit 3/5. Census: second utility-eligible spell → utility_skills 9,
picker counts 23/10.

## Tests: utility-skill census made structural (no per-skill churn)

Every new spell/cantrip landed broke two snapshot counts (utility_skills
census + the editor skill-picker's element/button totals) — pure churn
during the Tier A spree. Fix: derive, don't snapshot. The picker test now
asserts `5 + 2 * utility_skill_ids.len` elements and
`1 + utility_skill_ids.len` buttons — the same list the picker iterates,
so it self-updates per skill while still catching double-emitted or
dropped cells. The utility_skills census test drops its exact count (its
policy assertions — weapon exclusion, eligibility, list consistency — are
the real content) with a comment pointing at the picker test for the
structural coverage. New skills no longer touch either test.

## Skill: spell Piston Bolt (Tier A slice 9)

Third spell. Single-target attack at range 3 for 1x effective spell damage
with the DOUBLED converted momentum bonus — getEffectiveSpellDamage folds
the conversion in once, the skill adds getConvertedMomentum a second time
(the impale/skewer precedent, on the spell pipeline). cd 3, targeted,
weakestTarget pick, flat 3 (impale's rating — conditional-bonus attack
above the basic 2). Census tests untouched (the structural-count fix from
the previous entry paying off immediately). Tests: the doubled-bonus
arithmetic on an awkward value (amulet 6 + momentum 4 → log2 2 → 6+2+2 =
10) + the option pick/rating.

## Skills: AI rating scale re-anchored to value units (+ stale-doc cleanup

The tuning interjection, settled before chain lightning lands on it. The
scale now has a semantic: priority ≈ the cast's value in units of a plain
1x hit — 0 = don't cast, 1 = a plain attack, +1 per significant bonus (a
conditional damage multiplier, a stun landing on a non-stunned target,
collision damage, a control effect worth ~a hit; lifesteal only when the
caster is below half health — sustainability is not tempo; minor riders
like ±1 momentum and non-colliding displacement count 0).

Motivating case: a 1-target spinblade tied piston bolt at 3 and slot order
(weapon left of spell) picked the strictly worse cast. Under value units
1 < 2 and the single-target skill wins; ties now mean equal value, so the
slot-order bias reads "at equal value prefer the cheaper slot".

- aoePriority(count, base) = base + count − 1 (base 1 = plain per-target
  hit; 2 = a global rider worth a hit, flash strike's teleport).
  aoeKnockbackPriority = base + count − 1 + colliding_count (+1 PER
  colliding target, not +1 for any — an AoE has no target choice, each
  collision genuinely adds a hit's worth).
- Full retune: plain attacks (shoot/toss/spark/unwounded slice/low chop/
  open-field bash+powerful shot) 2→1; one-bonus casts (wounded slice,
  healthy stab/chop, impale, cleave+head_shot unstunned, colliding bash/
  powerful shot, throw, retreating swipe, piston bolt, heal-below-half)
  3→2; skewer 4→3 (two bonuses); plain AoE base 3→1 (rating = count);
  blitz base 4→ inline count + unstunned count; flash strike base 3→2;
  howl base 1 (rating = inactive count); slam/shockwave base 3→1.
- vampiric_strike: the full-health gate REMOVED — offered always, rated
  1 / 2 (below half). The handler_tests_ai on-cooldown test relied on the
  old gate (stab on cd + full-health player = no skills); now sets
  vampiric on cd too.
- daze: re-rated as pure control (no base hit): unstunned pick = 1 + its
  momentum, stunned-momentful = 1, else no option — strictly more precise
  than the old flat 3/2.
- STALE-DOC cleanup discovered en route: the ai_options migration had left
  every file's OLD `/// AI priority` doc (and the orphaned
  `/// AI target selection` docs, sometimes fused with kept docs) stacked
  above the new `/// AI options` docs — the migration's doc-walk stopped at
  a blank line between doc and fn. Harmless to compilation, hence invisible
  until now; swept by marker (leading stale run up to a kept-doc marker).
- Tests: both helper tables rewritten for the linear formulas; every
  rating assertion moved down a rung (two cascade bugs in my scoped-swap
  script caught by the suite — cleave's two sub-blocks swapped, worldfire's
  "cluster of two" block actually contains three targets and now correctly
  rates 3); new blitz formula coverage (2/3/4) + drain's lifesteal bonus
  (2 targets + wounded caster → 3).

## Skill: spell Chain Lightning (Tier A slice 10)

Fourth spell, landing on the freshly re-anchored value-unit scale.
Attacks the target and every hostile in its CONNECTED COMPONENT: flood
fill over hostiles where two hostiles within the skill's EFFECTIVE radius
(Chebyshev) of each other are connected, transitively. Connection rule
settled in discussion: allies are not chain nodes — they cannot conduct,
so a hostile line broken by an ally does not arc (two hostiles only bridge
if within radius of each other; the ally occupying the middle tile makes
that impossible in a line). Damage 1x effective spell damage per member,
cd 5, range 1 for the initial target.

The option is the first genuinely multi-candidate targeted rating: argmax
over valid targets by (component size, then the focus-fire tail), rated
aoePriority(size, 1) — under value units a 1-link chain rates like a plain
attack (1) and a 3-web rates 3, so the AI saves it for webs exactly like
the AoE skills. chainComponentIndices is file-local (one consumer family;
BFS with an append-only marching queue — no alloc/free churn beyond the
visited set).

Tests: the 3-hostile line arcs fully (ally + far hostile excluded); the
ally-between-hostiles line breaks at 1; the options test picks the larger
component — my first layout was wrong (the "lone" target sat diagonally
adjacent to the pair head, silently merging the components into one
size-3 tie) and the failure output caught it.

## Skill: spell Adrenaline Surge (Tier A slice 11) — spells complete

All five spells done. Adrenaline Surge: enemy-targeted finisher — reset
the target's ON-BAR cooldowns (all skills of both equipped weapons, the
swap-available thirds included, plus equipped utility skills) and attack
it once per cooldown reset this way. Range 1, cd 5, 1x effective spell
damage per hit. The re-arm-if-it-survives cost is deliberate (balance
tunable later, per the author).

Engine shape (the reset_weapon_cooldowns precedent, one step broader):
- `Entity.onBarSkillIds(defs)` — the full equippable set (6 weapon slots
  deduped + 5 utility), fixed-size, distinct from collectSkillSlots (the
  8 EXPOSED slots). Shared by the handler and the skill's aiOptions so
  enumeration cannot drift. Off-bar preserved cooldowns (the
  swap-inheritance ticking ones) deliberately excluded — "on the bar"
  only.
- New SubLevelEvent `adrenaline_surge{attacker, defender}` — machinery:
  the enumeration needs weapon_type_definitions, unreachable from
  useSkill. aiOptions (which receives the defs) computes the same count
  for its rating: option = the target with the most ticking on-bar
  cooldowns (focus-fire tail ties), rated = the count in value units —
  literally one hit per reset; no option when nothing ticks.
- The handler's push order matters and the tests caught me implementing
  it BACKWARDS: resets must go on the LIFO stack LAST (drain first) so
  they land even when the attacks kill — change_cooldown no-ops on a dead
  entity, so attacks-first loses the resets on a killing cast.

Tests: handler (3 resets incl. the swap-available third + utility,
skewer's off-bar cd untouched, 3×4 damage; the kill case zeroes cooldowns
despite death; nothing-ticking no-op), options (count outranks
focus-fire; the off-bar cd not counted — also caught my test forgetting
to EQUIP blink, which the count rightly ignored), useSkill delegation.

## Skills: cantrips Burst, Meditate, Accelerate (Tier A slice 12)

Cantrips done. Design note settled on the way: the non-ending pool's
ratings only ORDER the cantrips/enchantments/curses — enemy_turn_attack
re-pushes itself after each non-ending cast, so every worthwhile one fires
before the turn-ender. Ratings there don't gate "whether", just "which
first".

- Burst: spinblade's shape with spell damage, cantrip (non-ending) — a
  mini-Worldfire at a tenth of the cooldown. aoePriority(count, 1).
- Meditate: resets each OTHER equipped utility skill (itself excluded).
  Simpler than Focus — utility slots live on the entity, so useSkill
  composes change_cooldown directly (no defs, no machinery event). Rating
  = the reset count.
- Accelerate: +1 momentum per enemy within radius 3, one change_momentum
  of the counted amount (the use_skill handler's universal +1 lands on
  top, the toss precedent). Rating = direct enemy count (the author's
  call over my log2-sublinear discounting — pool ordering only).

Tests: burst (radius filter + spell damage + rating 2), meditate (blink +
  howl reset, itself and an off-bar preserved cooldown excluded, rating =
  reset count), accelerate (two-of-three enemies counted, ally excluded,
  delta +2, rating 2).

## Skills: enchantments That Which Reaches, Bull Form, That Which Rushes (Tier A slice 13)

The pure-modifier trio, on the That Which Lingers template (self-cast
create_effect, options flat 1 — the enchantment pool's ratings only order
the non-ending skills). Reaches: range/radius +1; Bull Form: distance +10
(knockback + retreat); Rushes: cooldown -1 (applied where cooldowns are
set, in use_skill) + speed +1. effect_sprite null on all three until art
ships. Tests: create_effect payloads + the modifier fields on each effect
definition via generated_lookups + the flat-1 option.

## Skills: enchantments Explodes, Promise of Death, Diamond Form (Tier A slice 14) — TIER A COMPLETE

Tier A finished: 20 skills, zero engine changes beyond what the
convention interjections themselves added. Three reactive enchantments,
with two author rulings recorded in DESIGN → Architecture:

- **Utility-spell-damage rule**: any damage a utility skill deals —
  directly or via reactive effect attacks — is getEffectiveSpellDamage.
  That Which Explodes' retaliation attacks use it.
- **Cooldown-reset scopes differ by direction**: Adrenaline (enemy-
  targeted) = on-bar only (the swap-inheritance count exploit: rotate
  many skills, each inherited cd adds a reflectable attack — hidden and
  broken); Promise of Death (self-buff) = FULL sweep incl. off-bar
  preserved cooldowns (nothing to inflate).

The skills:
- That Which Explodes (duration 2, cd 10): on_incoming_damage → attacks
  every hostile within radius 1 of the holder. Options on the threat
  model (2 threatened, nothing unthreatened). Note: reactor callbacks
  get (entity, state, allocator) — no attacker/damage context (the known
  Tier C gap); explode doesn't need it.
- Promise of Death (duration 1, cd 10): on_opponent_death → change_
  cooldown per ticking SkillId (runtime loop over the hole-free generated
  enum) + heal to full. Flat 1 when an active hostile exists.
- Diamond Form (duration/stun 5, cd 10): useSkill = self-stun then
  create_effect; the effect is a zero-everything interceptor (attack-only
  — collision still lands, the interceptor rule) + on_end_turn heal of
  max/10 (fires while stunned: a stunned turn still cycles start/end).
  Options under the desperation gate — threatened AND below half → 2
  (casting it otherwise trades five turns of actions for nothing).

Tests: explodes' reactor (radius/team/spell-damage) + threat gate;
promise's full sweep (on-bar + swap-available + utility + OFF-BAR skewer
all reset, heal-to-full) ; diamond's self-stun+effect ordering, the
  999-damage interception, the 23/10→2 heal truncation, and the
  three-branch desperation gate.

End-of-session review with the author. The architecture held (20 skills,
zero engine changes beyond convention work); the test suite caught four of
my own bugs (adrenaline's backwards push order, the cleave cascade swap,
worldfire's three-target "cluster of two", the ally on my collision test's
push path). Follow-ups recorded where they belong:
- TODO → Skill Logic: non-ending pool rating audit (ported cantrips/
  enchantments kept pre-value-unit numbers unexamined).

  compositions (adrenaline's tests are the template); aiOptions allocation
  churn as a watch item.
- AGENTS → Testing discipline: the three process lessons — dry-run sweep

## Enemy teams: level-format `team` key + official-content animal teams (slice 1)

Multi-team levels: a `team` integer on every entity — 0 = the player's
team (helpers the player doesn't control), 1+ = mutually hostile enemy
teams (AI battles). Hostility was ALREADY team-generic across the combat/
AI layer (`team != other.team` in skills/helpers/threat, aggro, turn
flow, win condition, on_opponent_death), so this slice is pure authoring
surface — no engine change.

- `parseEntityDefinition` (loaders.zig): optional `team` key in the pairs
  overrides the caller's default (enemies 1, player 0). u32, no artificial
  cap. Player save/loadout paths never carried/will carry the key (the
  player is always team 0).
- Parser whitelist: `team` added to `level_enemies_keys`. (The
  content-validation tests would have flagged shipped files with an
  unwhitelisted key — the whitelist edit and the content sweep landed
  together on purpose.)
- `writeEntityDefinition` (writers.zig): emits `team {d}` only when ≠ 1 —
  absent-on-reload equals absent-on-write, 1 is the load default.
- Official content: all ANIMAL enemies (wolf, bear, crab, giant_crab) are
  now explicit `team 2`; skeletons stay implicit team 1. Gameplay
  consequence (deliberate): forest/seatown/wetlands levels now feature
  animals-vs-skeleton AI battles when placed in each other's aggro range —
  animals no longer side with the skeletons against the player.
- Tests: loadLevel with a team-2 second enemy (key overrides default,
  tiles/entities unchanged in shape); writeEditorMission fixture's Brute
  is team 2 — asserts the team-1 file omits the key, the team-2 file
  carries `team 2`, and the reload round-trips the value.

Tooling note: the edit-tool call reported success for a two-edit batch
where only the first edit applied (the team override silently missing —
surfaced by the failing loader test, then re-applied). Lesson: verify
multi-edit batches actually landed, not just the success message.

## Enemy teams: editor event + handler (slice 2)

`editor_set_entity_team` / `player_set_editor_entity_team` — the scalar-
field shape (target EntityEditTarget + value u32), one field = one undo
step. Wiring: the EditorEvent + player wrapper (events.zig), the handler
arm (editor/handlers.zig — `template.team = value` behind the shared
`editorEntityTemplate` null-guard), the thin forward
(handlers/player_input.zig), and the `validatePlayerAction` arm
(state.zig). Session-log serialization + deep-copy came free via the
comptime machinery.

- Team is ENEMY-authorable only: the validation arm rejects the
  `player_def` target (the layer-event precedent) — the player's team is
  definitionally 0, and a crafted log setting it would corrupt the win
  condition's team comparison. Values are otherwise unrestricted u32
  (same posture as the unbounded base stats).
- Tests: team 2 + team 0 commits ride the timeline and undo; crafted
  out-of-range type id records nothing. The panic-path validation
  (player_def reject) is not unit-tested per the no-expectPanics
  convention (AGENTS → Testing discipline).

## Enemy teams: inspector Team field + text-input commit (slice 3)

The Team row in the enemy inspector's Identity section, wired through the
existing scalar-field machinery end to end:

- `EntityStatField` += `team` (types.zig) — the one lever. The enum drives
  the digits-only buffer filter (`textFieldIsNumeric` keys on the union
  tag), the value source (`Entity.textFieldValue` += team arm), and the
  commit switch (input_handlers' `commitFocusedTextEdit` += team →
  `player_set_editor_entity_team`). Team is identity-not-stat, noted on
  the enum.
- Content plan (editor_inspector.zig): "Team" row in Identity, after
  Name — enemy content only (the player inspector stays read-only; the
  commit's player_def target is rejected at the replay seam, slice 2).
- Tests: the Team field's formatted value + label emission in the
  scroll-0 window; end-to-end commit test (1→2, 2→0 helper, empty-buffer
  no-op, same-value no-op, two undos revert both commits). The existing
  windowed-emission tests re-anchored: the 2-unit field shifts every
  downstream scroll offset by +2 (identity 9→11 units, 45→47 total,
  clamp 35→37).

### Test-harness side fix: duplicate idle points in runToIdle

The new commit test exposed a latent harness footgun: `runToIdle`'s
UNCONDITIONAL `recordIdlePoint` double-records when called after a
commit path that drains + records internally
(`resolveTextEditOutcome` → `pushPlayerActionAndDrain` →
`maybeRecordIdlePoint`). Duplicate idle points at the same event index
make `undo` restore to the CURRENT state — a no-op undo step: idle
points {0,2,2,4,4}, undo → points[3] = 4 → same state. The max_health
commit test had dodged it accidentally (no runToIdle after its second
commit). Fix: `runToIdle` now calls `maybeRecordIdlePoint(true)` — the
same dedupe the live gameLoop uses. No existing test relied on the
duplicates (full suite green).

Also noted: the edit tool again reported success for a batch where one
edit silently didn't apply (the state.zig validate arm — caught by rg
verification, not by the tool). Second occurrence this session; verify
multi-edit batches explicitly.

## Enemy teams: helper coloring (slice 4)

Team-0 entities render with the PLAYER gradient — the "helper" reading of
team 0 (DESIGN → Entity & UI Coloring updated with the settled rule):
the gradient resolves by TEAM (0 → player, else enemy), the INDEX by
player-ness — the player entity keeps the settings-driven
`player_color_index`; every other entity (helpers included) uses its own
authored `color_index`, so a helper sides with the player visually while
staying distinguishable from the player's settings color.

- `entityDrawable` (view.zig): `is_player: bool` param; body color =
  team gradient + (settings index for the player, own index otherwise).
  Layer colors already keyed per-layer own index; weapons/health bars
  already gradient-by-team — both correct for helpers unchanged.
  `collectEntityEntries` passes `index == 0` — the player is the FIRST
  pointer in every caller's slice (level entities[0], hub player, editor
  player template; the entity-index-0 invariant), noted at the site.
- Editor inspector (editor_inspector.zig): `InspectorEntityContext`'s
  gradient for an entity_type target resolves by the template's team — a
  team-0 type's whole content tints player-gradient (the author sees
  helper coloring live in the viewport too, via buildEditorScene's
  entityDrawable path).
- In-game entity inspect panel (panels.zig): already keyed its gradient
  on `entity.team == 0` with fixed indices — correct for helpers with no
  change.
- Tests: entityDrawable color resolution (player settings-index vs
  helper own-index vs team-2 enemy gradient, distinct theme gradients);
  inspector strip tint for team-0 vs team-2 types.

## Enemy teams: "enemy tools" → "entity tools" rename (slice 5)

The editor's entity tooling is no longer enemy-only (team 0 = helpers,
1+ = enemy teams), so the "enemy" naming lied. Renamed across the board:

- **File format:** the level-file/editor-defaults section header
  `Enemies` → `Entities` — parser section whitelists (level_sections,

## Camera clamping (levels/hubs)

The polishing pass on camera framing: small levels sat off-center (the
camera is player-centered, so a level fitting on screen showed it pushed
toward whichever edge the player stood on), and big levels showed void
past their edges when the player stood near one. Spec + design in
DESIGN → Platform Seam → Camera clamping. Two slices:

1. **Region builder + panel-width extraction** (`view.zig`):
   `middlePanelWidth`/`middlePanelsOccupiedWidth` extracted out of
   `buildMiddlePanels` (the inspect panel's dead-target/dead-index/
   hub-screen no-render conditions moved into the width helper; the
   builder now force-unwraps what the helper guaranteed non-null — the
   level-handler fail-fast precedent). `cameraViewRegion` derives the
   clamp region per frame: y bounded by the top/bottom bars, x bounded
   from the left by the panels' occupied width, null outside
   levels/hubs. `cameraViewRegionFor` (pure) drops the panel bound when
   the remaining width can't fit the margin band (4 tiles at the zoom)
   — the "panels fully cover the screen → act as if none open" rule
   falls out of feasibility, no threshold constant.
2. **Clamp math + wiring**: `computeCamera` gained a `?Rectangle`
   view_region param and applies `clampCameraAxis` per axis —
   level-flush bounds ALWAYS (pan included: panning stops at the level
   edge, never into void; a level narrower than the region is centered
   as a whole and pan is a no-op on that axis), and the
   `camera_edge_margin_tiles` (2) player-margin band ONLY for the
   automatic camera (`pan == null`) — sequential clamping (flush then
   margin) gives "shed the void as far as possible without pushing the
   player past 2 tiles of clearance". A pan suspends the margin on both
   axes until the next recenter (player move / screen transition).
   `frame()` computes the region at both camera sites (pre-drain input,
   post-drain render — panels can open mid-drain); the pan solve in
   `handleCameraPan` passes `null` region for its reference so the
   grabbed point tracks exactly in the level interior, with resistance
   only at the edges. Levels clamp on `level_tiles`, hubs on
   `hub_tiles` (bbox — levels are non-rectangular).

Level bounds are the tile-grid bounding box, not authored dims — the
only "level rectangle" that exists for non-rectangular layouts.

Tests: the width helper's no-render conditions; occupied width (gaps
only between rendered panels); the region's vertical/horizontal bounds,
feasibility boundary (exactly-enough honored, one-pixel-short fallback,
zoom-scaled band), null outside levels/hubs, hub band; clamp semantics —
near-edge corners keep exactly 512 px (2 tiles) clearance from the
region edge, mid-level player stays exactly player-centered, a fitting
level centers as a whole (player position and pan both irrelevant), one
axis fits/other clamps, pan roams within the level but stops flush at
the edges (and suspends the y margin while panned), panels shift the
margin band to the viewable region, hub bounds, null region = unclamped
(the pan-solve contract). All hand-computed from the spec, not from the
implementation.

Deferred remainder: the EDITOR viewport's framing (sidebars + no player
following) is a different problem, untouched — the editor camera still
centers on the active level's player_start, unclamped.

## Camera clamping — follow-up: pan wiggle room

Author request: the pan stopping dead at the level edge felt like a hard
wall. `camera_pan_void_tiles` (tunable, 4): when a pan offset is active,
`clampCameraAxis` widens the flush bounds by that many tiles of world
pixels — the window may show up to 4 tiles of void past an edge before
stopping. On a fitting axis, a pan wiggles ±4 tiles around the centered
position instead of being a no-op. The automatic camera stays strictly
void-free (slack 0); `pan_slack == 0` replaced the `pan_active` bool as
the axis clamp's "automatic camera" signal. The margin band keys on the
same zero test. Tests updated: far pans stop exactly 1024 px past each
edge, an interior pan near the edge now passes through (its void is
inside the budget), the suspended y margin lets the plain player-centered
y pass while panned, and the small-level pan wiggles around the center.

## Camera clamping — editor viewport

The deferred remainder of the clamping pass (author request): the editor
camera now clamps on the active level's layout, with completely free pan.

- `screenWorldBounds` gained the editor arm (active level's `level_tiles`
  bbox via `selectEditorLevel`; live level/hub take precedence — during
  playtest/validate the editor state persists on a `.level` screen and the
  instantiated level bounds apply). An empty editor level has no bounds →
  unclamped player_start-centering (previous behavior).
- `cameraViewRegion` on `.editor`: the same band as the game (top row +
  tool palette bound it vertically) at FULL width — sidebars and pickers
  deliberately ignored (they never reframe the camera), no panel logic.
- `computeCamera`: in the editor viewport (`editor != null and level ==
  null`) a pan skips the clamp ENTIRELY — no flush bounds, no wiggle.
  Unpanned = clamped framing (same rules as gameplay: margin band around
  the player_start marker, flush bounds, small levels centered as a
  whole); panned = roam anywhere; the clamp resumes when the pan clears.
- Tab-switch recentering: the pan-clear check in `update()` compared
  `playerPosition` before/after — in the editor that's the active level's
  player_start, so a tab switch already recenters, EXCEPT that fresh
  levels all come from `data/default_level.txt` and share a player_start
  (tabbing between them changed nothing). Replaced with
  `view.cameraRecenterKey` (player position + editor active level index),
  so every tab switch recenters and re-clamps on the new layout.

Testing side note: the clamp-test helper `levelStateWithPlayer` returned a
GameState whose `.entities` pointed into the helper's dead frame — a
dangling pointer that survived on stack-layout luck until the new editor
tests shifted the frames and turned it into a player-tile garbage read
(`@intFromFloat` panic). The player entity now lives in file-scope test
storage. The same arena-blind-spot class as the use-after-free note in
AGENTS → Testing discipline, but in a test helper.

Tests: editor clamps around player_start with the level-test numbers,
bounds follow the active tab (two levels sharing a player_start, big →
small layout), pan completely free (±100k world px passes through), empty

## AI movement modes (point-blank cluster-seek + kiting)

Modal movement selection for AI entities: `enemy_turn_move` picks ONE
movement mode per entity per turn instead of always approaching.

- `Skill.point_blank_area_of_effect` (defaults false): marks skills whose
  AoE is centered on the caster — spinblade, slam, blitz, howl, worldfire,
  burst, drain, shockwave (that_which_explodes is reactive, not a cast —
  false; flash strike targets landing tiles — false). Deliberately NOT
  required like deals_damage: a forgotten flag only makes the AI dumber
  (walks instead of cluster-seeks), it corrupts no mechanic.
- `src/skills/movement.zig` (excluded from the build.zig SkillId scan
  alongside skill.zig/helpers.zig/threat.zig): `MovementMode`
  (approach / point_blank_cluster / keep_range) + `selectMovementMode` +
  the two destination fns — pure, in-file tested. Cooldown-dependent by
  author decision: an off-cooldown offensive point-blank skill on the
  EXPOSED bar (collectSkillSlots — the pool enemy_turn_attack casts from;
  a main-hand weapon's third skill is NOT exposed) → cluster-seek; else
  off-cooldown computeMinRange > 1 → kite at that range; else approach.
  The user's "keeping min-range distance" reading: computeMinRange is THE
  standoff — approach converges on it from outside, kiting opens to it
  from inside; both modes meet at the same distance.
- Handler wiring (level.zig): the approach logic extracted into
  `enemyApproachTurn` (unchanged behavior — the existing handler tests
  pass untouched) + `pushEnemyAttack`/`pushEnemyMoveThenAttack` (the
  wait→move→attack LIFO shape, previously inlined twice). The arm selects
  the mode, gets a destination (null → approach fallback — no cluster to
  seek / nobody in reach), and pushes move-then-attack or attack-only
  (destination == own tile → stand and cast).

A test-authoring note worth keeping: the first movement tests gave the
entity a MAIN-HAND staff and expected blitz — but a weapon's third skill
is only exposed in the off hand, and movement (like the attack phase)
reads collectSkillSlots, so the tests needed dual-wield staff (blitz via
the off hand's slot 3). The exposed-slot shape is now pinned in test
comments. Handler-drain tests: cluster-seek through processEvent
(position lands on the max-hit tile), blitz-on-cooldown → kite retreat to
the standoff, already-at-standoff → stands.

Design: DESIGN → Architecture (AI movement modes). Known limitation
recorded there: keep_range maximizes distance to the nearest SINGLE
hostile — retreating toward a second enemy is possible; multi-hostile
avoidance is a future mode.

## AI movement modes — follow-up: stay-put tie rule

Author report: enemies shuffled up-left even when their current tile was
already as good as any option. Root cause: the destination fns'
"current tile wins ties" intent was half-implemented — the (x, y)
tileBefore tiebreak could displace the CURRENT tile on equal scores, so
any equal-valued up-left neighbor lured the enemy into a pointless move.
The original fixtures never exercised the tie (no equal-valued
alternative existed — the "nice values" trap), so the bug shipped green.

Fix: an equal-value candidate never displaces the current tile; stay put
unless a STRICTLY better tile exists (more targets / more standoff).
tileBefore only orders reachable-vs-reachable ties (when the current tile
is out of the running entirely). No minimum-improvement threshold —
anything strictly better moves (author decision; integer scores make
"strictly better" already the coarsest sensible step).

New tie tests were verified load-bearing by reverting each guard
individually: cluster (caster at a 2-target tile, an equal-2 up-left
neighbor), keep-range (at the standoff, an equal-distance left neighbor)
— both fail without their guard, pass with it. Each test also pins the
strictly-better-moves half (a 3-target tile / a farther standoff tile is
taken). The keep-range "moves" fixture's expectation is (2,6), not the
naive (4,6): on an open grid five reachable tiles sit at distance 3 and
the reachable-vs-reachable tiebreak picks the leftmost — hand-compute
fixtures against the convention, not the first tile you eyeball.

## Daze AI rating crash (u1 arithmetic overflow)

Live-play crash report (Seatown staff skeleton's turn, crash log
crash_20260903_161841): `daze.aiOptions` panicked with integer overflow
on `const rating: u32 = 1 + @intFromBool(defender.momentum > 0)`.
@intFromBool yields u1; the peer type of `1 + u1` is u1, so the true case
computes 1+1 = 2 — which overflows u1 and traps. The cast to u32 must be
explicit: `1 + @as(u32, @intFromBool(...))`.

Pre-existing (the line shipped with the daze port), not caused by the
movement work — but data-dependent: it only fires when an UNSTUNNED
defender within daze's range carries momentum, and every real player
does (use_skill grants +1 momentum, persisting). The daze tier test
covered unstunned-no-momentum (1), stunned-momentful (1), the mixed
class pick, and the stunned-momentumless no-op — every tier EXCEPT the
unstable one. Added the missing tier (unstunned + momentum → rating 2),
verified it crashes on the unfixed line. Swept for the sibling shape:
only input_gestures.zig adds @intFromBools, and it already casts each to
u8 explicitly.

The third nice-values escape this session (movement tie fixtures, the
dangling test helper, now this) — each shipped green on fixtures that
never touched the degenerate case.

## Meteor replaces Daze (staff skill 2 rework)

Daze (stun + full momentum drain, no damage) was underpowered and boring
in playtesting — a pure-control single-target with no board impact. It is
replaced by Meteor: attack each target within radius of the target tile —
range 3, radius 1, cooldown 3, main-hand damage (the Spark damage model),
the Worldfire per-target attack loop centered on a clicked tile.

Design decisions (author-confirmed): the caster's own tile is a legal
target (a point-blank cast — range-0 is not skipped, unlike Flash Strike
which only skips (0,0) because it teleports); the AI scans ALL tiles in
range including occupied ones, counting hostiles ON the candidate tile
(distance 0 — hostileCountWithinRadius already counts them, so the
"direct hit" requirement needed no helper change; the real Flash Strike
difference was its empty-tile constraint, which Meteor doesn't share);
rating is plain per-target value units (aoePriority(count, 1) — a
1-target cast ties the basic attack and loses to slot order, so the staff
saves it for clusters, the Worldfire posture at a third of the cooldown).

Mechanically pure composition: no engine changes. The SkillId enum and
the skill-icon table (`skillIconSpriteId` = `skills/<tag>`) are generated
from filenames, so deleting `src/skills/daze.zig` + adding
`src/skills/meteor.zig` + `data/weapon_types/staff.txt` `skill_2 meteor`
was the whole wiring. assets/skills/daze.png renamed to meteor.png as
placeholder art (TODO notes the artist owes a real meteor icon).

Tests (skill_tests.zig): the max-cluster option pick (occupied-tile
center beats off-tile centers), the point-blank own-tile cast, the
unreachable → no-option case, single-target rating 1 + cooldown gate,
and the useSkill multi-attack. One fixture lesson worth repeating: the
first cluster fixture placed the pair at (3,0)/(3,1) expecting (3,0) to
win outright — but Chebyshev makes (2,0)→(3,1) distance 1, so (2,0) ALSO
counted 2 and won the scan-order tiebreak; the fixture now uses a
diagonal neighbor so the on-tile center strictly wins. Same lesson as the
movement-tie fixtures: hand-compute against the convention, not the first
tile you eyeball.

Stale-reference sweep: threat.zig + helpers.zig doc comments cited Daze
as their example (the control-only min-range case; the one
multi-cast-options skill — with it gone, every ai_options goes through
singleOption); comments reworded generically. movement.zig +
handler_tests_ai.zig test comments updated (spark + meteor, both range 3
— min/max-range behavior unchanged: daze dealt no damage, meteor does at
the same range 3, so computeMinRange/computeMaxDamageRange results are
identical).

## Editor camera clamp snapshot (level-switch-only reframing)

The editor's unpanned camera clamp was recomputed from the ACTIVE
level's LIVE tile bbox every frame (`screenWorldBounds` scanned
`level_tiles`), so any edit that moved the bbox reframed the camera
mid-edit — painting a tile past the edge (or erasing an extreme tile)
made the viewport jump. Author request: clamp only when switching the
current level.

- `types.TileBounds` (inclusive tile coords, zoom-independent) +
  `Editor.clamp_bounds: ?TileBounds` — a SNAPSHOT of the active level's
  tile bbox. Null = the level was empty at snapshot time (the unclamped
  editor camera).
- `refreshEditorClampBounds` (editor/handlers.zig) is the single refresh
  site, called ONLY where the active level switches: `openFreshEditorMission`,
  the open_editor mission branch (player_input.zig), the inline
  `editor_set_active_level` handler, `addEditorLevel`, and the
  `editor_delete_level` arm that clamps the active index onto new content
  (a delete BELOW the active tab shifts the tab with its level — same
  content, no refresh). Mid-edit tile events (`editor_set_tile`, the
  placement verbs) deliberately never refresh it.
- Because the refresh rides the same recorded events, undo/redo + replay
  reproduce the snapshot by construction: undoing an edit keeps the
  framing, undoing a tab switch restores the previous snapshot verbatim
  (it does NOT re-derive one — a crafted/undone state simply carries the
  snapshot its timeline says it should).
- `screenWorldBounds` (view.zig): the editor arm now converts the
  snapshot to world pixels instead of scanning live tiles; the live
  level/hub arms are unchanged (during playtest/validate the editor state
  persists on a `.level` screen, and the instantiated level's live bounds
  still take precedence). The editor arm no longer uses
  `selectEditorLevel` (rendering still does).
- The camera CENTER still tracks the live player_start — only the CLAMP
  bounds are snapshotted (recentering on a moved '!' is the center's job,
  not a reframe).

Tests: view (clamp follows the per-level snapshot with the old big/small
numbers; a mid-edit-shrunk live grid keeps the snapshot framing), handler
(snapshot refreshed on switch, held across `editor_set_tile`, reverted
verbatim by undo-of-switch; crafted states without open_editor carry no
snapshot). DESIGN → Platform Seam → Camera clamping updated.

## Editor tile-tool drag-painting (handleEditorTileDrag)

The last remaining editor viewport input: left press + drag with the tile
tool paints floor tiles continuously.

- **Gesture** (`handleEditorTileDrag`, input_gestures.zig — the
  marquee/move-drag pattern): a plain left press over the viewport (tile
  tool active, not over blocking UI) claims the drag and paints the tile
  directly under the cursor immediately — a clean click is
  indistinguishable from the old click path (same
  `planEditorTilePaintActions` planner, same empty-plan no-op gate; the
  press paints on the press tick because the input state marks the button
  held at the press edge). While held, each tile the pointer ENTERS that
  the drag hasn't visited paints the same way; the visited set
  (`SessionState.editor_tile_drag_visited`, reset at press,
  `active_anims`-shape backing-allocator list — Session-owned, not
  UiState, so the wholesale UiState reset on screen transitions can't
  orphan the buffer) stops re-fires when the pointer wiggles back over
  painted ground.
- **Empty-stack firing rule**: paints push only when the event stack is
  empty. A plan computed while earlier events sit unprocessed could
  reference placement indices those events are about to shift — two
  paints at tiles covered by the same multi-tile decoration would
  double-delete the placement and panic (the reason the selection move
  chains `editor_commit_selection_move` against live post-delete state).
  In practice a paint drains within a frame, so the gate is invisible.
- **Pause over blocking UI** (the marquee's last-valid-corner rule): while
  the pointer is over a panel, no paint and no visited marks; painting
  resumes at whatever tile is under the pointer on re-entry. A press over
  blocking UI never claims — dragging out of a panel onto the world paints
  nothing.
- **Ownership split**: the gesture owns the pointer press — the idle-input
  tile arm (`handleIdleInput`) defers while `UiState.editor_tile_drag` is
  set, so a claimed press can't double-fire; the keyboard confirm-at-
  cursor path still lands in the arm when no drag is in progress. Tool
  switch away from tile / tab / screen change ends the drag on the
  gesture's next call (context clear, the marquee pattern). Undo
  granularity is PER TILE by design (events.zig `editor_set_tile`).

Also in this commit: DESIGN's "Remaining: default level template
(data/default_level.txt)" line was stale (the template landed with
editor_add_level) — removed alongside the drag-painting remainder.

Tests: press paints immediately / held paints entered tiles / visited
wiggle never re-fires / release re-arms; press over blocking UI never
claims + mid-drag pause + resume; mid-drain deferral (held crossing a new
tile while the previous paint is still on the stack fires nothing, then
fires once drained); tool-switch context clear; the idle-arm defer (+
positive control). DESIGN → Level Editor → Active-tool model updated.

## Editor ctrl+A select-all: tool-agnostic (switches to the select tool)

ctrl+A previously fired only with the select tool active. Author request:
fire from any tool — decided (after weighing "stay on current tool") that
the action also SWITCHES to select, because the "selection nonempty ⇔
select tool" invariant makes a selection on another tool incoherent (paint
clicks would have to wonder what a selection means), and every reason to
select all — move, delete, marquee-refine — is a select-tool verb anyway
(the user would press 1 next regardless). Precedent: the palette add-type
handler already bundles the tool switch that makes the result coherent
("the author lands on the thing they just created").

- Input gate (`handleIdleInput`): the select-tool condition dropped; the
  nonempty-plan gate stays (an all-selected level never fires — note the
  plan is never empty off the select tool, since the '!' is always
  selectable and an off-tool selection can't exist).
- Handler (`player_select_editor_all`): when another tool is active, an
  `editor_set_tool{.select}` is appended AFTER the planner's editor_select
  events — the stack drains back-to-front, so the switch processes FIRST
  and the selects run with the select tool active (keeping
  editor_select's defensive tool guard honest rather than relying on its
  leniency). The switch rides the action's idle point: one undo restores
  the previous tool + the empty selection.
- `validatePlayerAction`: the "without the select tool active" panic arm
  removed (the action is legal from any tool now).
- ctrl+D and Delete needed NO change: they depend on a selection, which
  can only exist on the select tool — ctrl+A is the only action that
  CREATES a selection from nothing, so it's the only one needing the
  switch.

Test lesson (recurring): a crafted state mutation must land BEFORE
runToIdle — the idle-point snapshot is what undo replays to, so a
tool/selection seeded after it reverts to the pre-seed value on undo (the
seeded-selection pattern the older tests already follow).

Tests: ctrl+A from the tile tool fires + switches + selects everything;
one undo restores the tile tool + empty selection; the all-selected
no-op gate unchanged. DESIGN → Level Editor → Selection model updated.

The fresh-mission open — the main-menu Editor button's action — is now

(`new_editor_mission`, editor context).

  — DESIGN's "no unsaved-changes confirm / generation bump / undo across

- Consumption sits in the anytime block next to
  `toggle_editor_mission_browser`, behind the editor-screen gate (every

- The five-site keybind checklist (AGENTS → New-keybind pipeline
