  (context editor), raylib_backend KeyN table entry, Action enum +

  consumption. The ctrl+S lesson test (a dispatch pin, not just
  checkAction) is mirrored for ctrl+N.

Test note: `pushPlayerActionAndDrain` drains inline and records NO idle
point — the LIVE loop's post-update `maybeRecordIdlePoint(events_processed)`
is what makes such actions undo steps, so a handler test must call
runToIdle after the consumption call to mirror it (the first version
asserted undo without it and undid past the swap).

Tests: the ctrl+N translateInput dispatch pin (editor set fires; game +
menu sets dormant — a playtest/validation run deactivates the binding),
the consumption swap (fresh "New Mission" state, one template level,

## Unified drag threshold (2px) + threshold-gated camera pan

One movement threshold for every drag gesture, and the camera pan now
respects it.

- **The split before:** TWO constants with different values —
  `ui.drag_threshold_pixels = 8` (inventory/skill slot drags, handleDrag)
  and `input.drag_threshold_pixels = 0` (right-click inspect/delete
  cancel, editor marquee, editor selection-move). Unrelated history: the
  0 constant predated the UI drag lifecycle and was never retuned.
- **Unified:** `ui/element.zig`'s `drag_threshold_pixels = 2` is the single
  constant (re-exported `ui.drag_threshold_pixels`); `input.zig`'s copy is
  DELETED (input.zig already imports ui.zig, so the layering holds —
  no cycle: nothing in ui/ imports input.zig). All four input_gestures
  sites + the three input_handlers test sites now reference the ui
  constant. Strict `>` promotion everywhere (a zero value would still
  tolerate a no-movement press — the rationale kept in the doc comments).
- **Camera pan threshold:** `handleCameraPan` previously engaged the pan
  on the very first held tick — a 1px wiggle panned. Now a right-press
  records `camera_pan_press` (screen position) + the anchor (the world
  point under the PRESS — press-anchored grab, so what you pressed on
  sticks to the cursor), and the pan only ENGAGES once the pointer moves
  beyond the threshold; crossing drops the press record (latch — moving
  back near the press point keeps panning). A sub-threshold release is a
  clean right-click, consistent with the pending-right-click gestures
  that cancel at the same threshold. New `SessionState.camera_pan_press`
  field, cleared alongside the anchor at main.zig's three pan-clear sites
  (screen transition ×2, cameraRecenterKey). The pan offset still
  persists after release (sticky pan — unchanged).
- **Tile painting deliberately NOT changed:** the editor tile drag has no
  threshold by design — click and drag paint the same thing (the tile
  under the cursor), so there is no click-vs-drag distinction to make and
  the press tile paints immediately (a clean click behaves identically to
  the click path).
- DESIGN updates: the camera-pan paragraph (press-record + threshold
  engage + press-anchored solve) and the right-click-inspect coexistence
  wording (both record at press; engage/cancel at the same threshold).

Tests: new `handleCameraPan: pan engages only past the drag threshold`
input_handlers test (the first camera-pan test at all — press records but
doesn't pan, at-threshold stays unpromoted, past-threshold engages +
latches, release clears anchor/press while the offset persists). The
existing symbolic threshold tests (marquee, move-drag, right-click
cancel) pass unchanged — they were written against the constant, not the
value.

## Hostile-effect aggro (no more free sniping of inactive enemies)

Before: an inactive enemy hit by a skill reaching beyond its aggro_range
(worldfire radius 5, chain lightning, crossbow at range vs. aggro 3) stayed
inactive — it never woke, never acted, a free kill.

Rule: **being the DEFENDER of a hostile effect activates an inactive entity**,
regardless of range. "Targeted" and "dealt damage" collapse into one rule
because targeting IS event emission — the sub_level_events that name a
defender are the record of it being targeted.

- One-line `activateEntity` call at the top of five `handleSubLevelEvent`
  arms: `attack` (covers plain weapon attacks + every damaging skill +
  adrenaline_surge's emitted strikes transitively), `stun`, `knockback`,
  `collision` (a shove into an uninvolved third entity aggros it), and
  `swap_positions` (entity_b, the target).
- No new event type, no log/replay schema change: the `is_active` flip is a
  pure deterministic state transform inside the handler; the indicator anim
  is already replay-gated inside the shared `activateEntity` helper (now
  used by aggro_check + aggro_in_radius + the five hostile-effect sites).
- Targeted-with-zero-effective-damage aggros (Reflect zeroing, future
  invulnerability) — the entity was targeted, that's the semantic.
- NOT covered (deliberate): same-team/self buffs (heal, change_momentum,
  change_cooldown). Hostile momentum transforms are Tier B; the rule extends
  when those land. Player "activation" by enemy attacks is harmless by the
  entity-0 convention. No attacker-side activation — the only constructed
  case (that_which_explodes interceptor) takes damage first, so the defender
  rule covers it.
- Side effect of the rule: aggroing an enemy via damage now also blocks the
  level exit until it's killed (check_level_end counts active enemies) —
  correct, that's what aggro means.
- Cosmetic edge accepted: a killing hit flips is_active on the corpse +
  queues the indicator anim over the dying enemy (500ms, harmless) — kept
  the arm-top placement for the cleaner "targeted aggros" semantic.

Tests (handler_tests_ai.zig, new section): attack / stun / knockback /
collision / swap each activate an inactive defender placed beyond every
aggro_range (proximity can't fire — only the new rule can). Smoke-tested
that they run by flipping one assertion (expected failure observed, then
reverted). DESIGN → Architecture (the aggro paragraph) documents the rule.

## Turn counters increment at turn START (the final exit turn counts)

Before, `mission.turns_spent` + `player_data.turns` incremented in the
player's `turn_end` handler — so the final turn (walking onto the level
exit) never counted: check_level_end → end_level's screen transition
clears the stack mid-turn, and turn_end never runs. A two-turn-per-level
playthrough recorded one turn per level; the mission-complete stats and
the validation author medal undercounted.

- The counter block moved from the `turn_end` player arm to the
  `turn_start` player arm (handlers/level.zig) — after the dead-guard, so
  a dead player never counts a turn, and before the stun branch, so a
  stunned turn still counts (it did before, via turn_end).
- Semantics: turns_spent counts turns BEGUN. At any idle moment it
  includes the in-progress turn; the final exit turn is included.
- `deriveValidationTurns` (validation_replay.zig) switched from counting
  player `turn_end`s to counting player `turn_start`s — it is
  test-asserted equal to the live counter, so it had to follow. Existing
  stored validation replays derive slightly higher under the new rule
  (pre-release; no shipped files to migrate).
- DESIGN → Custom Missions & Online Services → Turn counters + author
  medals updated (increment site, begin-not-end rationale, derived-count
  source).

Test ripple (all mechanical, values re-derived from the new semantics —
not patched one-by-one: each playthrough was re-traced): a "skip turn +
exit turn" per level = 2 begun turns/level (was 1 completed), a beeline
= 1/level (was 0). handler_tests_editor: chaining/restart/crown/
validate-button/personal-best/stats-screen tests; main.zig editor
playtest counter test (level entry already counts turn 1, the skip
round begins turn 2); handler_tests_turnflow counter test moved to
turn_start; validation_replay fixtures switched to turn_start events.

## Spawn-relative coordinates (levels + hubs normalize to the '!' origin)

Parse-time displacement: `loadLevel` + `loadHub` displace everything in a
loaded layout by `-player_start` after the layout walk — the player spawn
(`!`) is always world (0,0), coordinates can go negative.

- The problem: the raw grid assigns world = grid index, so a layout-bbox
  growth to the left/up (e.g. a decoration placed off the playable area —
  decoration anchors carry no tile and expand the grid) shifted EVERY
  existing thing at load. Absolute positions in recorded logs (validation
  replays, session logs, crash dumps) silently broke even for edits that
  didn't touch the run.
- Spawn-relative positions are invariant under bbox growth in ANY
  direction. The editor load path (`buildEditorMission` → `loadLevel`)
  shares the normalization; the editor's writer already offsets by bbox
  origin, so load→save round trips are idempotent. File bytes are
  untouched → existing missions' content hashes unchanged.
- Levels/hubs without a `!` are left as-is (nothing to anchor on).
- Runtime coordinates of all shipped content changed (spawn-relative now);
  tests pinning raw file positions updated to the displaced values
  (loadLevel/loadHub parser tests, the beginnings editor round-trip test,
  the validation-fixture level-2 expectations).

Design: DESIGN → Logging & Replay → Spawn-relative coordinates. This is
the first half of the revalidate plan (the second: a revalidate button
that re-certifies a stored replay against new content) — normalization
makes benign bbox edits replay-compatible so revalidation can pass.

## Replay checking mode (rejectReplay + reconstructFromEventLogChecking)

The replay-verification layers (verifyReplayMatch, validatePlayerAction's
whole validate* family, the non-player-seed check) all fail fast via
@panic — a diverging replay is an integrity violation. The revalidate
feature needs the SAME check as a benign report ("does this stored run
still match the current content?"), so panicking had to become catchable.

- Every `@panic` site in the replay-validation region (117 of them) became
  `self.rejectReplay(msg); return;` — a scripted conversion with the
  invariant `rg '@panic\("replay validation|@panic\(msg\)' src/state.zig`
  returns zero (verified; the compile catches anything the sweep missed —
  all sites are in void fns, so the `return` unwinds cleanly, including
  `orelse` blocks where it diverges).
- `rejectReplay`: normal mode panics with the identical message (behavior
  unchanged — every existing replay test passes untouched); checking mode
  records the FIRST failure on `history.replay_rejection` (event index +
  backing-owned message) and returns, and the replay loops abort on the
  next `replay_rejection != null` check.
- New public `reconstructFromEventLogChecking` = reconstructFromEventLog
  with checking mode on; returns `?ReplayRejection` (null = clean). On a
  rejection the scratch history is left mid-replay — callers discard it.
- This is deliberately the shape the future server-side upload validation
  wants: the same error-returning path, no fail-fast wrapper. Design:
  DESIGN → Determinism & Tiebreaking → Replay CHECKING mode.

Tests (handler_tests_editor, the validation-fixture home): a clean log
replays with NO rejection + lands on the main menu like the normal
reconstruction; a content edit that moves the level end out from under
the run's recorded exit step rejects at the machinery-divergence layer;
an edit that deletes the exit tile makes the recorded move illegal and
rejects at the seed-legality layer.

## Revalidate Mission (the re-certify button)

Closes the scenario: an author validates a mission, places decorations
off the playable area (or makes any edit the run doesn't touch), and the
stored replay goes "unvalidated" on the content-hash mismatch — with no
way to re-certify except replaying the whole mission by hand.

Three slices:

1. **Spawn-relative coordinates** (the earlier DONE entry) — makes
   benign bbox-growing edits replay-COMPATIBLE (positions no longer
   shift). Without it, revalidation would spuriously fail on exactly
   the motivating edit.
2. **Replay checking mode** (the earlier DONE entry) — the same
   verification, catchable.
3. **The feature** (this entry):
   - `validation_replay.revalidateMission` — PURE (file reads only;
     the caller owns the rewrite): load the stored replay, gate on the
     mission.txt uuid identity, compute the current content hash, and
     reconstruct the recorded run in a SCRATCH history via
     reconstructFromEventLogChecking against the files as they are now.
     Returns valid{hash_hex, turns} | invalid{reason}. Deliberately the
     shape the future server-side upload validation wants (the
     error-returning path, no fail-fast wrapper).
   - The `player_revalidate_mission` orchestrator (handlers/
     player_input.zig): entirely live-only (`!replaying` — the check
     reads CURRENT files, not recorded state; a replayed session
     re-records the click but re-runs nothing). On success rewrites
     validation_replay.txt with the same events + the NEW content hash,
     KEEPING the original created stamp + derived turns (same run,
     re-certified). Every failure (no replay file, malformed, uuid
     mismatch, divergence) surfaces via the error popup with the reason;
     the old file is kept on failure.
   - UI: the editor's options menu, "Revalidate Mission" under New
     Mission (Action + applyAction + the options_action consumption —
     save-first then push, the Validate contract). Button-only (no
     keybind).
   - validatePlayerAction arm: editor screen + editor present (the
     structural bar; the handler owns the rest).

Tests: benign edit (rename) re-binds the hash (turns/created/uuid kept,
hash == the recomputed current hash and it CHANGED); divergent edit
(moved level end) rejects + keeps the file; no-replay-file and
uuid-mismatch reasons; the options-menu wiring end-to-end (save-first +
orchestrator recorded + the popup); the button is editor-only in the
options menu. Smoke-verified by flipping one assertion (observed FAIL,
reverted). DESIGN → Custom Missions & Online Services → Validation
replay → Revalidate; the deferred top-bar-promotion decision lives in
TODO → Level Editor.

## src/skills/ + src/effects/ purity (interface/support files to src/ root)

Author request: every file in src/skills/ should be a skill, and every
file in src/effects/ an effect. Four non-skill files had accumulated in
src/skills/ (excluded from the build.zig SkillId scan by name) and one
in src/effects/; the directories now contain ONLY definitions.

Moves (all to src/ root, names describing the job rather than the
directory they happened to live in):

- `skills/skill.zig` → `skill.zig` (the Skill interface)
- `skills/helpers.zig` → `skill_helpers.zig` (targeting/lookup helpers)
- `skills/threat.zig` → `ai_threat.zig` (AI range/threat math)
- `skills/movement.zig` → `ai_movement.zig` (AI movement-mode selection)
- `effects/effect.zig` → `effect.zig` (the Effect interface)

build.zig: the `scanDir` exclusion-list parameter is GONE — both scans
now assume directory purity (a non-definition file in src/skills/ would
silently become a SkillId, which is exactly the enforcement we want).
The generated-lookups template imports the root-level `skill.zig`/
`effect.zig`. The ~60 definition files' imports re-pointed via a
sed sweep dry-run on one file first (per the sweep-script rule);
generated_lookups.zig + generated_test_root.zig regenerate per build.

DESIGN/AGENTS pointers updated (AI threat model, AI movement modes,
tiebreaking helpers); DONE archive entries left as-is per policy.

## Diamond Form removed (design rejected)

`src/skills/diamond_form.zig` + `src/effects/diamond_form.zig` deleted
(skill + effect), the three skill_tests blocks and their imports removed.
Everything else was automatic: SkillId/EffectId are generated by the
build.zig directory scans (deleting the files removes the variants),
`utility_skill_ids` is comptime-derived from the enum, and no data file,
loadout, or asset referenced it.

Rationale (settled as DESIGN → Architecture → Skill design principles):
the game's goal is speedrunning encounters, and Diamond Form is the
antithesis — a self-stun of 5 turns with invulnerability forces any
encounter in which it's used to run at least 5 turns longer with zero
player decisions (taking control feels bad), and it's a built-in-downside
skill (self-stun as a cost), a design type rejected at all costs. It came
from the original Unity design doc; the TODO Tier A entry now records the
removal so a future skills pass doesn't re-port it as "missing". Tier A
count: 19 skills.

## Damage multiplier ordering (multipliers apply last)

Skill damage multipliers now apply to the FULLY-MODIFIED total, never the
raw weapon/spell number: aggregate every additive modifier first (the
getEffective* pipeline: gear, effects, converted momentum — plus
skill-specific additive riders), then multiply. Convention: DESIGN →
Architecture → Damage multiplier ordering; the shared 1.5x helper is
`skill_helpers.damageTimesOneAndAHalf`.

- Reordered (were multiply-raw-then-modify): Throw, Retreating Swipe
  (1.5x of the effective off-hand damage), Impale, Skewer. For
  Impale/Skewer the doubled-momentum rider rides INSIDE the multiplier
  (author decision: "all modifiers first" is literal — no exceptions;
  Impale's momentum now effectively counts 3x: 2 × 1.5, a buff).
- Already compliant, refactored onto the helper for structural
  consistency: Chop, Stab, Slice (conditional 1.5x after the pipeline —
  they always did it this way).
- Unaffected: Bash/Powerful Shot/Shockwave (collision payload = half the
  already-effective total), Charged Bolt (momentum ×3 multiplies a single
  modifier — order-invariant).
- Tests: three ordering regression guards in skill_tests.zig (Throw with
  a gloves bonus proving the multiplier hits the modified total;
  Impale/Skewer with momentum proving the rider rides inside).

## Effective-value audit of all skill logic

Author-requested verification that skill logic never uses base values
where modifiers should apply. Audited: all 43 skills (damage bases,
range/radius/distance reads, stun + skill durations, heal amounts,
half-health conditions), the 9 effects, skill_helpers, ai_threat,
ai_movement, and the cooldown system.

Result: clean everywhere EXCEPT one catch —
`effects/that_which_explodes.zig` hardcoded the explosion radius
(`const radius: i32 = 1`), so radius modifiers (That Which Reaches +1)
did nothing for the explosion. Fixed to
`holder.getEffectiveRadius(1)`; TWR + TWE on the same holder now
explode at radius 2. Regression test added (holder with a +1 radius
modifier hits an enemy at Chebyshev 2, not one at 3).

Convention recorded: DESIGN → Architecture → "Skill logic always reads
EFFECTIVE values" (raw reads are legal only as base inputs to a
getEffective* call; runtime counters are read raw directly).

## Clone auto-save decision: turns-only personal best

The clone auto-save decision at mission completion no longer compares
per-material harvest rates. It now matches the validation replay's
personal-best rule (validation_replay.replayOverwriteDecision):
strictly FEWER turns than the existing clone → auto-overwrite; tied or
slower → keep the old clone and set overwrite_offered (the existing
manual "Overwrite Clone" button on the mission-complete overlay).

The harvest model is unchanged (a clone still stores
materials_collected + turns_to_complete and pays out rate * turns on
future completions) — only the overwrite DECISION is turns-only.
Materials no longer influence whether a run replaces the clone; a
material-rich slow run keeps the faster clone by default and can be
stashed manually via the button.

Removed: `cloneIsStrictlyBetter` (the Pareto per-material-rate helper)
+ its 4 turnflow tests; the decision is a single turns comparison
inline in end_level. Comment/doc sites updated (types.zig overwrite_
offered, events.zig + player_input.zig routing comments, DESIGN →
Clones step 2/5).

## macOS native port (cross-build + persistent dir + .app bundle)

Three slices, one session. Working rules in AGENTS → Build & Test; settled
persistent-dir design in DESIGN → File System & IO → Persistent path.

- **Cross-compile (aarch64-macos from the Linux box).** `zig build
  -Dtarget=aarch64-macos` compiles raylib (ObjC/Cocoa sources) + the whole
  game and links a Mach-O arm64 exe with no Apple SDK. The blocker: raylib's
  `linkMacOS` adds the framework SEARCH paths (the `xcode_frameworks` .tbd
  stubs) to the raylib library's module only — the `-framework X` link flags
  propagate to a consumer exe but the `-F` paths do NOT, so our exe's link
  failed with `unable to find framework 'Foundation'. searched paths: none`.
  Fix: our build.zig.zon declares the SAME xcode_frameworks package (same
  url+hash, deduped to one zig-pkg entry; `.lazy = true` so Linux builds
  never fetch the 16 MB package) and build.zig adds
  `addSystemFrameworkPath`/`addLibraryPath` to the exe's root module, gated
  on a macos target. The lazy-dep protocol on a fresh machine: first build
  configure returns early (zig fetches the package, re-runs the script);
  second build links. Also gated the Linux-only `.so`-strip archive step on
  `.linux` targets.
- **Persistent dir.** `resolvePersistentPath` in native.zig gained a
  `builtin.os.tag` switch: Linux keeps `$HOME/.ziglop`, mac defaults to
  `$HOME/Library/Application Support/ziglop` (Finder-visible convention —
  same discoverability-over-convention reasoning as the Linux dotfile, see
  DESIGN). Flag/env overrides unchanged; web IDBFS unchanged. The name rides
  the ziglop→taplop rename sweep. The path contains a space — all uses go
  through `std.Io.Dir` handles + argv elements, nothing shells out to a
  path string; runtime round-trip still on the hardware checklist.
- **.app bundle.** For macos targets the install step also assembles
  `zig-out/ziglop.app/` (Contents/MacOS/ziglop via `addInstallFileWithDir`
  with a custom dest dir + Contents/Info.plist via WriteFiles +
  `addInstallDirectory`). Minimal plist: identity
  (com.linusweggehjalsted.ziglop), LSMinimumSystemVersion 11.0,
  NSHighResolutionCapable. NO icon (no suitable art; generic icon until an
  .icns is generated — TODO) and NO codesigning (needs a mac host; a
  browser-downloaded bundle needs `xattr -cr ziglop.app` once — notarization
  is a demo-milestone decision).
- Runtime validation on real hardware is STILL PENDING (compile ≠ run — the
  web-build lesson): checklist in TODO → Platform Layer → macOS native port.

## macOS: Command as Control (backend key table)

First mac hardware test surfaced the ctrl-vs-Command issue: the shipped
binding set (`data/default_settings.txt`) names `ControlLeft` etc. (W3C
KeyboardEvent.code ids — the cross-platform convention), but mac convention
is Command for shortcuts, and nothing bound the super keys. Fix at the
backend key table, the site that owns physical-key → id mapping:
`mac_key_mappings` (comptime-gated on `builtin.os.tag == .macos`) maps
`left_super`/`right_super` to `ControlLeft`/`ControlRight`, appended to
`shared_key_mappings` (the old `key_mappings` const renamed). Every
ControlLeft binding + the `getModifiers` chord machinery then work on Cmd
unchanged; physical ctrl keys keep working (both map to the same ids).
Held-key tracking is per-id, so a user holding Cmd + left-ctrl and releasing
one drops the modifier early — accepted corner. One binding set still ships
for all platforms; translateInput stays platform-agnostic. Design: DESIGN →
Input (macOS: Command reports as the Control ids). The same hardware test
reported 9-slice panels not rendering on mac (fine on Linux/web) — open,
see TODO → macOS native port.

## Dev diag log (dev-mode, persistent-dir troubleshooting)

The mac bring-up needs data from a machine whose user shouldn't have to
live in Terminal. Added a best-effort diagnostic log to raylib_backend.zig,
gated `build_info.dev_mode and !emscripten`, flushed (whole-file rewrite)
to `logs/diag.txt` in the persistent dir after every section:

- **Boot section** (first render, once GL is live): game_version, target,
  window points vs framebuffer pixels (the retina check), render-target
  dims, and GL vendor/renderer/version/GLSL via a direct `extern glGetString`
  call. raylib itself goes through its internal glad loader, so nothing
  links raw gl* symbols — the macos build gained an explicit
  `linkFramework("OpenGL")` on the exe for it (the xcode_frameworks
  package ships the .tbd stubs; a Linux build already had libGL via
  raylib's linkLinux).
- **One-shot probes**: the first plain `drawSprite` (the known-working
  control — fires on slots/health bars in-game; main-menu buttons are
  spriteless so the control does NOT fire on the menu alone) and the first
  `drawNineSlice` (full draw state: sprite id, texture id/dims, panel
  color + theme_darkest + resolved tint, destination, all nine
  source/destination piece rects — computed once via the pure
  `ui.nineSlicePieces` and shared with the draw loop).

Every write is `catch return` — diagnostics never crash the game. Verified
locally end-to-end (Linux, `--data-dir` scratch): boot section + panel
probe captured, including the zero-height center pieces of a 2-corner-tall
bar. Comptime-gated: non-dev builds analyze none of it. The friend's next
build carries this; the mac 9-slice investigation (panels render nothing on
mac, everything else renders — draw path audited and identical to working
sprites) proceeds from his `logs/diag.txt`.

## mac 9-slice panels: "fixed by the OpenGL framework link" — FALSIFIED

> This entry's conclusion is WRONG — the release-build bisection
> falsified it (see the CORRECTION entry below). The framework link is
> NOT the fix; it stays only because glGetString/glFinish need it.
> Kept for the trail.

Mystery bug, empirically resolved. Two consecutive mac builds rendered
EVERYTHING except 9-slice panels (all panels invisible; sprites, text,
everything else fine). The next build — zero game-code changes to the draw
path — renders panels correctly, deterministically per binary (the friend
verified: old build still broken, new build works).

The only rendering-relevant delta between the broken and working builds:
the dev-diag work added `exe.root_module.linkFramework("OpenGL")` to
build.zig (needed for the diag's direct `glGetString` extern — raylib
resolves all GL through its internal glad loader, so nothing else links
OpenGL; the broken builds linked no OpenGL framework at all).

What the friend's diag.txt ruled out: the draw state on mac is byte-identical
to Linux (same texture 384x384, same tint, same nine source/destination
rects, same zero-height-piece skips), on Apple's GL-on-Metal shim (M1, GL
4.1 / GLSL 4.10). So the game-side path is provably identical — the
difference is purely link/dyld config: with the framework linked, dyld loads
OpenGL eagerly at launch; without it, GL exists only via glad's lazy dlopen
at raylib init. Loader/timing difference on Apple's shim is the plausible
lever, but "sprites worked while panels didn't" fits no clean theory, and
"eager vs lazy framework load changes 9-slice visibility" is the honest
extent of our knowledge. The mechanism stays unexplained — the LINK is the
fix. It is NOT dev-gated (release builds carry it); the build.zig comment +
AGENTS note say so explicitly so it's never stripped as diag-only cruft.

Open resolution: which precise element fixed it (framework link vs a
dev-only diag behavior — the boot glGetString calls or the mid-frame probe
file write). The decisive experiment is the release build (dev_mode=false
→ all diag code comptime-dead, framework link present): if panels render
there, the link alone suffices and release builds are safe; if they break
again, a dev-only element is load-bearing and needs an always-on minimal
variant (a boot-time glGetString touch, unconditional on mac). In flight —
the friend has the release build.

Diag bonus findings (mac, M1): window 1920x1080 points with framebuffer
1920x1080 pixels — 1:1, i.e. NO retina/high-DPI scaling (raylib runs
without FLAG_WINDOW_HIGHDPI; content upscaled by the compositor on retina
screens), and 1920x1080 points likely exceeds the laptop screen at default
scaling — window sizing follow-up in TODO → macOS native port.

## mac 9-slice panels — CORRECTION + the real fix candidate (upload stall)

The previous entry's conclusion (the OpenGL framework link was the fix) is
FALSIFIED. Full bisection across friend-tested mac binaries + local tests:

- mac ReleaseFast, no dev code, no framework link: panels INVISIBLE
- mac ReleaseFast, no dev code, WITH framework link: panels INVISIBLE
- mac Debug (dev diag present): panels render
- mac ReleaseFast + `-Ddev-mode=true` (dev diag present): panels render
- linux ReleaseFast (no dev code): panels render

So neither the framework link nor the optimize level is the variable — the
DEV DIAG CODE is load-bearing on mac. The one rendering-relevant thing the
diag does that nothing else does: the panel probe's mid-frame file write
between the panel texture's lazy upload (getTexture → ensureSpriteLoaded)
and its first draw.

Working theory (fits every data point): on Apple's GL-on-Metal shim, the
FIRST lazily-uploaded texture uploaded and drawn within the same frame
samples as fully transparent without a stall between upload and draw —
ui/panel is the first such texture of the main menu, so all panels vanish
while later-uploaded textures (entities, icons — warmed-up frames) survive;
a zero texel under the premultiplied blend is src.rgb=0/src.a=0 = INVISIBLE,
matching "don't render at all" (not black). The probe's syscalls are the
stall that made the working builds work.

Fix candidate: `completeTextureUploadMac` (raylib_backend.zig) — glFinish +
2ms sleep after each sprite/outline texture upload, comptime mac-only, NOT
dev-gated (release builds need it; ~30 textures × one-time cost = invisible
at startup). Called from ensureSpriteLoaded + rgbaBufToTexture (the mid-frame
upload sites). If glFinish alone doesn't cover shim staging, the sleep does;
if the friend's next plain-release test still breaks, lengthen the stall.

The OpenGL framework link STAYS regardless: glGetString (dev diag) and
glFinish (the fix) need it. The diag harness also gained a render-target
PIXEL READBACK probe (diagLogTargetReadback — samples the offscreen target
at the probed destinations at end of frame; "pixels present" = blit/present
failure, "pixels absent" = draw failure) — verified locally on Linux, unused
so far on mac because the bisection resolved first; it's there for the next
mac mystery.

## mac 9-slice panels — upload-stall theory FALSIFIED, fix reverted

The completeTextureUploadMac fix candidate (glFinish + 2ms usleep after
every texture upload, mac-only, not dev-gated) did NOT fix the friend's
build — panels still fully transparent. This falsifies the upload→draw
stall theory (the stall sat exactly where the dev probe's file write sits)
and the fix was REVERTED (falsified fixes don't linger as dead code).

Current state of the mystery — six friend-tested/local binaries:
release-no-dev broken (with and without the OpenGL framework link),
Debug-dev and release+dev-mode render, release-no-dev+upload-stall broken,
linux release renders. Ruled out: framework link, optimize level,
upload-stall timing, game-side draw state (byte-identical on a working mac
build), Linux repro. The surviving variable: dev-mode-conditional code
presence — prime suspects now the diag boot glGetString calls (before the
first beginTextureMode), the diag file writes, mid-frame allocations,
binary-layout noise masking latent UB, or an unidentified dev_mode consumer.
Full matrix + hypothesis list + the next-session experiment ladder (incl.
the ReleaseSafe first build and the never-yet-exercised-on-mac render-target
readback probe) live in TODO → macOS native port → mac 9-slice panel bug.

## Native allocator: c_allocator in release builds (DebugAllocator was boilerplate)

The native entry had used `std.heap.DebugAllocator(.{})` unconditionally
since the first functional commit ("rendering!") — standard Zig template
boilerplate, never a decision (the old DONE line "DebugAllocator in debug,
page_allocator in release" described a config switch that never existed in
the code). Web got a deliberate exception early (c_allocator —
DebugAllocator's mmap backing breaks emscripten's JS heap views); native
never got the same review.

What the audit found (Zig 0.16 std source): DebugAllocator's stack traces
default to Debug-only (0 frames elsewhere), its safety checks (double-free
detection, canaries) follow `std.debug.runtime_safety` — on in Debug +
ReleaseSafe, OFF in ReleaseFast/Small — and its leak report only fires on
`.deinit()`, which the entry point never calls (and shouldn't:
process-lifetime allocations — settings, the persistent-dir path — are
intentional, so a deinit would only report false positives). Net: in
ReleaseFast the DebugAllocator bought NOTHING — just "quite slow and
wasteful" (std's own words, >100 bytes overhead per small allocation) with
an mmap/page-fault-prone backing, sitting next to libc malloc that's
already linked via raylib.

Fix: `native.zig` main() now picks the allocator by optimize mode —
DebugAllocator in Debug + ReleaseSafe (double-free detection stays
available in dev playtesting AND in the safety-net/troubleshooting
config), `c_allocator` in other release configs (matches the web build's
allocator exactly). Compiled + verified both branches (Debug and
ReleaseFast link clean). Design: DESIGN → Memory & Budget → Session
allocator.

Mac-bug relevance: this lands MID-INVESTIGATION and is a legitimate
named-mechanism experiment — allocation timing through mmap/page faults
is exactly the class of thing that differs on Apple's GL-on-Metal shim.
The in-flight first-state 2×2 binaries (a472891) predate the switch and
are unaffected (all four cells DebugAllocator-backed). From this commit
on, any HEAD `--release=fast` mac cell doubles as the allocator
experiment: if panels render with c_allocator, the DebugAllocator's
mmap timing on the shim was load-bearing — see TODO → macOS native port
→ mac 9-slice panel bug (the NOTE in the experiment ladder).

## mac 9-slice panels — first-state 2×2 results: optimize level is the base variable

The first-state experiment (a472891 — the first mac build + Command-key
fix, BEFORE any diag code existed; dev-mode code there was only the
skip-level binding) closed the missing cells. Friend-tested, all four:

| build (a472891) | panels |
|---|---|
| `--release=fast` + dev-mode | BROKEN |
| `--release=fast` no dev | BROKEN |
| Debug + dev-mode | renders |
| Debug no dev | renders |

KEY REFRAME: the dev/non-dev axis was an artifact of which HEAD cells
happened to be tested. At first state, release is broken REGARDLESS of
dev code and Debug renders regardless — the base variable is OPTIMIZE
LEVEL. Cross-referenced with HEAD (release+dev RENDERS there, with the
diag code), the only thing that has EVER rescued a release build is the
diag code specifically; generic dev code (skip-level) is demonstrably
insufficient. The old "optimize level ruled out (row 4 vs 1)" inference
is corrected — it attributed the release delta to dev code, which the
first-state cells disprove.

Consequences: (A) "a specific diag element masks the bug" is the working
theory, with sharpened candidates (boot glGetString calls, file writes,
mid-frame formatting ALLOCATIONS — the falsified glFinish+sleep test had
none — and the end-of-frame readback sync); (B) layout-noise/UB is
weakened but not dead (a layout mask would have to come specifically
from the diag code). Next round designed in TODO → mac 9-slice panel bug
→ ladder step 0a: four HEAD cells — allocator probe (c_allocator
release), dev regression check, diag-killed loop-closer, and the
ReleaseSafe UB probe.

## mac 9-slice panels — round 2 results: the diag code is THE rescuer; the fault is below Zig safety

Four HEAD cells (all carrying the c_allocator release switch), friend-
tested: release-no-dev BROKEN (allocator ruled out as the sole rescuer —
the switch stays on its own merits); release+dev+diag RENDERS (the switch
didn't break the known-working dev cell); release+dev with the diag
KILLED via a temp comptime toggle BROKEN — with allocator, dev code, and
everything else held constant, flipping only `diag_enabled` re-breaks
it, so the diag code specifically rescues (hypothesis A confirmed at the
block level); ReleaseSafe-no-dev BROKEN SILENTLY — no panic, no trace,
and every Zig-checkable UB class would panic with a trace in ReleaseSafe,
so the fault is below Zig safety: raylib C under optimization, the
GL-on-Metal shim, or unchecked Zig↔C interop. The remaining question is
WHICH diag element is load-bearing; the piece bisection (leave-one-out +
all-on control, five cells) is designed in TODO → mac 9-slice panel bug
→ ladder step 0b.

## mac 9-slice panels — round 3 results: the panel probe is THE necessary piece

Piece bisection (leave-one-out + all-on control; five HEAD release+dev
cells, c_allocator, each diag piece gated by a temp uncommitted comptime
toggle): no-boot renders, no-sprite-probe renders, no-readback renders,
the all-on control renders, and NO-PANEL-PROBE is the ONLY broken cell.
The panel probe — the mid-frame log that sits between the panel
texture's lazy upload and its first drawNineSlice — is the necessary
piece; every other diag piece is individually dispensable.

This pins the mechanism class tightly: the probe makes NO GL calls at
that position. Its effects there are formatting allocations into the
diag buffer through the session allocator (it rescues under both
DebugAllocator and c_allocator), the diagFlush file write, and trivial
state writes. The previously-falsified glFinish+2ms stall sat at the
same position and did NOT rescue — so pure GPU sync / time delay is
out, and the discriminator is CPU-side: allocations vs file-write
syscalls vs mere presence at the position. Layout-noise (B) is nearly
dead: the control rendered and three other piece-removals rendered —
each removal shifts layout too, so "exactly the panel-probe removal is
layout-unlucky" is implausible. Next round (within-probe split:
format-only / flush-only / moved-after-draw) is designed in TODO → mac
9-slice panel bug → ladder step 0c.

## mac 9-slice panels — round 4 results: formatting work is the rescuer; ui/panel is the session's first upload

Within-probe split (three HEAD release+dev cells, c_allocator, temp
uncommitted toggles inside the panel probe): FORMAT-ONLY renders,
FLUSH-ONLY (the file write at the probe position) BROKEN, FULL-PROBE-
AFTER-THE-DRAW renders. So the rescuer is the probe's FORMATTING work,
and it is position-flexible — same frame after the upload, before or
after the first draw. The boot section's appends (same frame, BEFORE the
upload) don't rescue (r3 app-3), and the flush-only cell's end-of-frame
readback appends didn't either — with no probe appends the diag buffer
had spare capacity so they allocated NOTHING, while the format cells'
~750 bytes of appends GREW the buffer. Working hypothesis: a
session-allocator ALLOCATION after ui/panel's upload, within that first
frame, is the rescuer.

Two deductions from the r4 diag files: (1) the [control] sprite-probe
section is absent from all three → no drawSprite ever ran → the friend
judged on the spriteless main menu → the probed first panel
(1408,824 1024×160) is a MAIN-MENU panel and ui/panel is the session's
FIRST texture upload (all other textures upload later, in-game, and
work); (2) the broken cell's readback shows the panel ABSENT from the
offscreen target (75% sample (190,199,97) vs the working builds'
(132,93,76) — the panel's own tint) → the failure is INSIDE the target,
not the blit/present path. Central open question: does the texture
UPLOAD transparent, or does its draw fail? Round 5 (minimal-rescuer
split + raw texel dump) is designed in TODO → ladder step 0d.

## mac 9-slice panels — round 5 results: the unified rescue condition (pure field reads)

Minimal-rescuer split (four HEAD release+dev cells, c_allocator, temp
uncommitted toggles): ALLOC-ONLY (bare 4096-byte session-allocator alloc
at the probe site) BROKEN — the allocation theory is falsified;
STACK-FORMAT-ONLY (the same formatting into a stack buffer, NO heap
allocation, DCE-guarded) RENDERS; READS-ONLY (nothing but field reads of
texture/pieces/tint/destination, sunk via doNotOptimizeAway) RENDERS;
TEXEL-DUMP (file write + GL texture read — which also reads `texture`)
RENDERS.

Unified rescue condition, consistent with EVERY cell ever tested: read
the draw's input values inside drawNineSlice between computation and
draw. Every rendering build does that; every broken build doesn't
(alloc-only, flush-only, glFinish+sleep, boot, no-probe). Allocations,
file writes, syscalls, GPU sync, timing — all irrelevant. The mechanism
is pure CODEGEN PERTURBATION: the optimized codegen of drawNineSlice on
aarch64-macos (ReleaseFast AND ReleaseSafe both break — optimization
level, not Zig safety; Debug -O0 is fine; Linux x86_64 release is fine)
is miscompiled or exploits unchecked UB, and any read of the draw's
inputs masks it by re-materializing the values. Prime suspect: the
by-value rl.drawTexturePro extern-C call chain (Texture2D + rectangles +
Color) or the loop building them from `pieces`. Next: read-set bisection
(which single read is the bullseye — TODO ladder 0e) and, for the first
time in this hunt, a LOCAL investigation: emit aarch64-macos LLVM IR/asm
with vs without the reads and diff the generated code on the Linux box
(ladder 0f).

## mac 9-slice panels — ROOT CAUSE FOUND: uninitialized tint (aarch64-macos miscompile)

The IR codegen diff (ladder 0f — done locally, no friend needed): built the
friend-tested round-5 pair (alloc-only = BROKEN, reads-only = RENDERS) for
aarch64-macos ReleaseFast with LLVM-IR emission (temp uncommitted
`getEmittedLlvmIr` in the bisect worktree's build.zig), extracted
drawNineSlice from both, and diffed.

THE MISCOMPILE: in the broken build, the `tint` of drawNineSlice —

    const tint = if (std.meta.eql(panel.color, ui.default_tint))
        toRaylibColor(theme_darkest, 255)
    else
        toRaylibColor(panel.color, 255);

— compiles to TWO NEVER-INITIALIZED STACK SLOTS (`%4`/`%5` = `alloca
%raylib.Color`), a pointer-`select` between them, and an i64 load from the
selected slot passed as `DrawTexturePro`'s tint argument. **There is not a
single store to either slot in the whole function.** The two inlined
`toRaylibColor` results' stores are absent — the draw tints with
uninitialized stack memory. On the friend's machine the garbage byte in
the alpha position reads 0, and under premultiplied BLEND_ALPHA that is a
fully transparent draw — invisible panels, everything else fine.

Evidence chain: (1) broken aarch64-macos IR — two Color allocas, pointer
select, ZERO stores, i64 tint load; (2) reads-only (renders) aarch64-macos
IR — the same two slots EXIST and ARE stored (i8 stores of r/g/b/a); (3)
identical source on Linux x86_64 ReleaseFast — stores present (Linux
renders). Debug builds (-O0) don't run the offending optimization;
ReleaseSafe does (same LLVM opt level, silent — matches the round-2
ReleaseSafe-broken cell).

This explains the ENTIRE data matrix including the unified rescue
condition: any read of `resolved_tint` (probe format, stack-format,
reads-only, texel dump — all read the tint) forces the color to
materialize correctly → renders; any cell that doesn't read it (alloc-
only, flush-only, glFinish+sleep, boot, no-probe) draws the garbage tint
→ invisible. PREDICTION for the in-flight round 6: the tint-read cell
renders; texture/pieces/destination reads stay broken.

Attribution (Zig frontend emission vs an LLVM pass eliminating the
stores) is open — matters only for the upstream report. Our fix is a
source restructure that avoids the two-branch if/else-expression
returning an extern struct by value (single `toRaylibColor` call on a
pre-selected `types.Color`), verified in IR + a friend cell.

## mac 9-slice panels — round 6 confirms the root cause; fix landed + IR-verified; audit clean

Round 6 (read-set bisection, four cells): texture-read BROKEN, pieces-read
BROKEN, TINT-READ RENDERS, destination-read BROKEN — the pre-registered
prediction held exactly, independently confirming that the miscompiled
value is the tint.

THE FIX (drawNineSlice, raylib_backend.zig): select the source
types.Color first (`source_color = if eql(panel.color, default_tint)
theme_darkest else panel.color`), then ONE toRaylibColor call — no
if/else expression returning the extern rl.Color by value. IR-verified
on the historically-broken config (aarch64-macos ReleaseFast, dev off):
the two never-stored `alloca %raylib.Color` slots are GONE; the tint is
scalarized into registers (zext i8→i64 + shifts) assembled from the
actually-loaded source-color bytes — no allocas, no pointer select,
every byte traceable to real data. Semantically identical to the
original code (same sentinel check, same two possible colors).

AUDIT (clean): the dangerous pattern — an if/else EXPRESSION whose
branches are function calls returning an extern struct BY VALUE, the
result feeding an extern call — existed only at the tint site. The
nearby candidates are safe by shape and by evidence: drawSprite's
source rect is struct literals in both branches (plus a post-mutation
`var`, forcing materialization) and rendered fine in-game on broken
builds; the ?rl.Rectangle optional site is a payload-slot shape,
exercised by in-game slots on broken builds, rendered fine;
drawTextLabel already pre-selects its source color before converting —
the same shape as the fix.

Remaining: the final friend cell (the fixed plain release build, in the
bisect handoff) and the upstream zig issue with a minimized repro (see
TODO → mac 9-slice panel bug → remaining items).

## Render resolution setting (runtime live-apply)

The offscreen render target resolution moved from a compile-time build
option (`-Drender-width`/`-Drender-height`, default 1920×1080) to a runtime
user setting: `render_resolution`, a 720p/1080p/1440p/2160p preset enum
(`types.RenderResolution`, default 1080p everywhere), live-applied so the
fill-rate benefit of a smaller target is immediate. Design: DESIGN →
Platform Seam → Render target resolution (+ Settings screen → Live-apply).

What landed, per layer:

- **types.zig**: `RenderResolution` enum (p720/p1080/p1440/p2160) with
  `label()` — the single "720p"…"2160p" spelling shared by parse (loader),
  write (writer), and the settings-screen row, so the file value matches
  the UI — and `pixelDimensions()`. The comptime 16:9 aspect guard now
  checks every preset (it used to check the build-option pair).
  `Settings.render_resolution` + `SettingId.render_resolution` +
  `default_render_resolution`.
- **build.zig**: the two build options REMOVED — the setting is the sole
  source (two sources invite "which wins?" drift; the build option's use
  case, perf tuning, is exactly what the setting now serves).
- **raylib_backend.zig**: render target dims + scale became struct fields
  (`render_width`/`render_height`, initialized to the default before
  settings load — the backend is built before `createSessionSetup`).
  `applyRenderResolution(resolution) bool` creates the NEW
  `RenderTexture` first and unloads the old one only on success, so a
  failed apply leaves the session rendering unchanged. `blitTransform`
  takes dims as parameters (it was a zero-arg fn over comptime consts).
  All camera-zoom/blit/diag-readback sites read the fields.
- **state.zig**: `SessionState.last_applied_render_resolution` snapshot,
  initialized to the default (in sync with the backend's init-time target,
  so a default setting costs no first-frame swap; a non-default setting
  swaps on frame one).
- **main.zig**: `applyRenderResolutionSetting(backend, history)` called from
  `frame()` next to the audio-volume diff-and-apply — same pattern, keeps
  input handlers free of a backend pointer. On apply failure (raylib's
  `loadRenderTexture` returns a clean error on GPU texture-size limits /
  incomplete FBOs): the setting REVERTS to the currently-running preset
  (the snapshot names it), `markSettingsDirty` so the revert persists, and
  the pending-error popup names both presets ("2160p rendering is not
  supported on this system — kept 1080p."). Recoverable-class handling —
  the failure is detected cleanly at apply time and rendering state is
  untouched. The revert also stops a retry loop: setting == snapshot, so
  the user's next click on the failed preset is the only re-attempt.
  (Boot-time target creation still panics — no prior target to keep.)
- **Loader/writer/parser**: `render_resolution` parsed by label
  (unrecognized values keep the default — preferences, not gameplay),
  written by label, whitelisted in `settings_display_keys`, added to
  `data/default_settings.txt`. No settings-format version bump — a missing
  key falls back to the default.
- **Settings screen**: a "Render Resolution" 4-button choice row after
  Camera Zoom (the camera_zoom pattern); a failed apply snaps the
  highlighted button back to what actually runs.
- **Tests**: label round-trip through writeSettings → loadSettings,
  unknown-value-keeps-default, loader Display-section parse, and the
  diff-and-apply helper against a fake backend (applies on diff, no-op
  without one; failed apply reverts + popup + no retry loop).

Higher presets sharpen SDF text for free (glyphs rasterize into the
target at target resolution through the camera zoom) — no asset changes.
The window size is NOT affected (letterboxed independently; the mac
high-DPI/window-sizing TODO is separate).

Web compiles (WEB OK); browser + native runtime confirmation pending
(the platform-seam "compiles ≠ runs" rule).

## Camera zoom gated to camera-bearing screens

The scroll wheel and the zoom keyboard shortcuts (PgUp/PgDn/ctrl+0) used
to zoom the camera even on screens with no camera — the wheel fell
through the anytime-input wheel-routing chain to its zoom fallback on the
main menu (and the replay viewer), silently mutating the `camera_zoom`
setting while nothing on screen responded. Both paths are now gated by
`cameraZoomAllowed(screen)` at the consumption site in
`handleAnytimeInput` (input_handlers.zig): zoom fires only on hub, level,
and editor. The gate lives at the handler (not in the binding contexts)
because the wheel isn't a binding, and the zoom keys must gate uniformly
across existing installs whose user settings still carry the old
`anytime`-context zoom bindings. Test: the new handler test pins
wheel+keys no-op on main_menu + replay_viewer, zoom on hub.

## editor_move_*_placement removal (cleanup session)

The `editor_move_entity/decoration/item_placement` events — original
scaffolding from the editor event-family design, never wired to a
handler — were REMOVED (cleanup session, keep-or-remove question
resolved). Evidence: zero producers (no planner, input path, or test
ever pushed them; the selection move's chained `editor_commit_selection_move`
delete + re-place covers the use case), and since they were never pushed no
session log in existence can contain them — removal is free of
format-compatibility cost. The comptime serializer, deep-copy, and the
exhaustive-switch catch-all (`else => @panic("editor event handler not
implemented")` — the fail-fast net for future unhooked verbs) all
auto-tracked the removal.

The settled reasoning (why delete + re-place won over stable-index moves):
a stable-index single-placement move verb would preserve placement identity
(same reasoning as the retype verbs' "identity stays stable" comment — it's
why `reconcileSelectionAfterPlacementDelete` exists at all), but the
index-shift repair cost is already sunk and solved, order churn in saved
mission files is cosmetic, and the future gestures that might want
identity-preserving moves (arrow-key nudge, drag-one-thing) are speculative.
If one lands, the verb is ~5 lines to re-add WITH its handler + planner in
the same slice — the discipline the original scaffolding skipped.

## Custom decoration stems: load-side dims resolution (cleanup session)

The reload panic is fixed: a saved mission with a `custom/<mission-dir>/<stem>`
decoration sprite used to PANIC on reload — `resolveDecorationSpriteDimensions`
prefixed `decorations/` and fell through a generic `assets/{id}.png` file-source
read, a path nothing ever wrote. Design clarification settled first (owner
decision): custom assets are ALWAYS mission-bundled — the mission directory is
their only home; `assets/` (incl. any `assets/decorations/custom/` path) is
never a read or write location for them.

- `resolveDecorationSpriteDimensions` is now a two-channel switch, no third
  channel: a `custom/`-prefixed stem reads `{mission_path}/{file-stem}.png`
  via the file source (the mission being loaded — current-truth, so dir
  renames and export→import re-uuids stay correct; the dir name EMBEDDED in
  the stem is namespace-only, never a read path); anything else must hit the
  shipped comptime table. Unknown stems fail fast. The generic
  `resolveSpriteDimensions` fallback (read any `assets/{id}.png` through the
  file source) was dead legacy — deleted; nothing could author a non-shipped
  bare stem (the picker offers only registry/shipped or mission-local picks).
- Plumbing: `loadLevel` gained an explicit `mission_path` param →
  `parseDecorationDefinitions` → `parseDecorationEntry`/`finishLayer` → the
  resolver (base + layer picks share it). Callers: start_level passes
  `start.mission_path`; `buildEditorMission` passes its mission path (param
  renamed `file_path` → `mission_path` — it always held the dir); loadHub,
  the default-level template, the decoration REGISTRY + editor-defaults
  readers, and all tests pass `""` (shipped/mission-agnostic content — a
  custom stem there fails fast, which is the point).
- A vanished/corrupt mission PNG at load time still fails fast (panic →
  crash dump) rather than the recoverable popup — same posture as today's
  missing-sprite panics; not expanded into error-plumbing here.
- Test: "loadLevel resolves mission-bundled custom decoration stems" —
  scratch-dir FileSource + minimal-PNG-header fixtures (parsePngDimensions
  reads only signature + IHDR), base + layer dims asserted through the real
  loadLevel path.
- Also fixed: a copy-paste duplicate "Remaining layer-adjacent opens:"
  heading in TODO.md (the drag-painting prose under it was never a bullet
  list).

## PointerInput.position precision — floatWorldPoint fix (cleanup session)

`PointerInput.position` was `types.ScreenPosition` (i32), truncating the
pointer's sub-pixel precision at the `pointerFacts` seam — so the camera-pan
anchor (`floatWorldPoint`) grabbed the world at integer-pixel precision,
which could jitter at low zoom even though `floatWorldPoint`'s float inverse
was built for exactly that precision. Fix: `PointerInput.position` is now
`input.PointerPosition` (f32) end-to-end:

- `pointerFacts` passes `mouse_screen_position` through untruncated;
  `floatWorldPoint` takes `PointerPosition` (the stale "NOTE: truncated" doc
  gone).
- The UI-grid seam: every hit-testing/threshold site truncates via
  `.toScreenPosition()` at the use site (`handleDrag`, `handleSliderDrag`,
  `handleCameraPan`/`handleRightClick*`/editor gestures' `blockingElementAt`
  + `refAt`/`sliderAt` calls, the gesture structs' `press_position` fields
  which stay i32 — the layout grid is their semantic home).
- World/tile resolution uses the float directly: the pan anchor + press
  record (`SessionState.camera_pan_press` → `?input.PointerPosition`), and
  every gesture's `screenToTile` call (the seven `@floatFromInt` reconstruct
  literals collapsed to plain `pointer.position`).
- The camera-pan threshold compare runs in f32 against the i32
  `drag_threshold_pixels` (hoisted `@floatFromInt`); the other gestures keep
  i32 threshold math (press records are i32).
- Tests: helper/local position fixtures (`tileCenter`, the
  `tilePosition`/`at` closures, `center`/`name_click`/`sprite_click`) build
  `PointerPosition` now; the two UI-grid `screen_position` uses convert via
  `.toScreenPosition()`. Comptime int literals coerce unchanged.

## Rating audit: heal/replenish/focus + the enhancement-enchantment rule (cleanup session)

The non-ending pool rating audit (TODO) opened into a design session. Settled
design in DESIGN → Architecture (AI rating scale — two new bullets); the
short version:

- **Value-unit anchors (owner decisions):** a 20% heal = 1 (idol heal
  2 → 1 — it now TIES a plain attack in the ending pool; slot order makes a
  below-half enemy heal once then attack), a full heal = 2 (replenish
  3 → 2, below-half gate unchanged).
- **Focus gate bug fixed:** its gate fired on ANY ticking cooldown
  (including cantrips) while the reset handler resolves slots 1-3 only — an
  enemy with just a ticking cantrip would burn focus's 10-turn cooldown
  resetting nothing. Now rated by the WEAPON-skill reset count
  (`skillInSlot` slots 1-3, the handler's own resolution — the
  meditate/adrenaline convention). New test pins cantrip-exclusion.
- **Enhancement enchantments rate against their LIVE beneficiaries (+1
  ordering rule, owner design):** rate = best live-beneficiary + 1, where
  live = the PLANNED turn-ending cast if it matches the enhanced Skill
  field, plus positive-rated cantrip beneficiaries (a future stun cantrip
  slots into stone form's scan automatically — the future-proofing the
  owner wanted). No live beneficiary → the enchantment's fallback (stone
  form: the end-of-turn heal at 1, below full health). Ratings skip
  0-rated beneficiaries so enchantments never fire "early" on a cast that
  won't happen.
- **`src/ai_select.zig` (new):** the ONE cast-selection algorithm, extracted
  from `enemy_turn_attack` so enhancer predictions can't drift from the
  real selection. `bestCasts` (both pools, the handler's exact partition +
  strict-> + slot-order tiebreak) for the handler;
  `plannedEndingCast` (weapon/spell slots only) for the enhancers. The
  recursion analysis that shaped the split: an enhancer calling full
  `bestCasts` re-enters its own aiOptions (infinite), and two equipped
  enhancers recurse through each other — so the plan-facing API evaluates
  only non-enhancer slots, and beneficiary scans filter to `.cantrip` types
  (never another `.enchantment`). One-way edge rule documented in the file
  header + DESIGN.
- **Stone form (first consumer):** planned ending cast with
  `stun_duration != null` → rate = plan + 1; stun cantrip scan
  (future-proof, no stun cantrip ships yet — untestable until one exists);
  fallback = the 20%-HoT unit at 1 below full health. Tests pin the plan
  itself (cleave at 2), the +1, the fallback, and the no-beneficiary
  no-cast. Notable faithful behavior: a full-health axe-carrier plans
  CHOP (chop's above-half 2 ties cleave's 2, slot order wins) → no stun
  planned → stone form waits — the plan-dependence is the point.
- Cleanup in passing: two stale test names fixed ("idol heal: priority is
  3" asserted 2; "cleave: priority is 3" asserted 2/1).

## The pass-scoped EvalFrame — memoized + cycle-safe AI option evaluation (cleanup session)

The structural recursion guard from the previous slice (ending-pool split +
cantrip-only beneficiary filters + one-way-edge convention) was REPLACED by
one mechanism, per design discussion: the pass-scoped evaluation frame
(`skill_mod.EvalFrame`, skill.zig; `ai_select.optionsFor`).

- **Why:** the structural rules excluded lingers' entire beneficiary set
  (all enchantments — the duration meta-enhancer scans
  `skill_duration != null` skills, which are all `.enchantment`), forcing a
  "only lingers may scan enchantments" special case. Each new skill shape
  would have needed new case analysis. The owner asked for the clean
  general answer.
- **The mechanism:** `EvalFrame` is a comptime-sized table (in-progress bitset
  + results array, stack-allocated ~a few hundred bytes) opened fresh per
  enemy_turn_attack re-evaluation pass. Every option evaluation goes through
  `optionsFor(frame, skill_id, ...)`: memoized once per pass (the game state
  is frozen within a pass — casts happen between passes), cycle-cut by the
  in-progress guard (a skill whose aiOptions is transitively being computed
  returns empty options — which is also the CORRECT consultation semantics:
  an enhancer scanning beneficiaries must not count itself). Any skill may
  consult any set of skills through the frame; no structural restrictions
  remain. `plannedEndingCast` was REMOVED (one `bestCasts(frame)` again —
  consulting the full plan is safe through the guard); stone form's
  beneficiary scan widened from `.cantrip`-only to all non-ending types.
- **Perf:** evaluation is bounded at once per skill per pass regardless of
  consultation density — retires the "aiOptions allocation churn" watch
  item's concern structurally.
- **Churn:** `ai_options_fn` gained a `frame: *EvalFrame` param (44 skill
  files, one line each — non-consulters take it as `_`; Zig 0.16 errors on
  unused params), the handler opens the frame, and skill tests call through
  a `freshOptions` helper (a FRESH frame per call — a shared frame would
  serve stale memoized options across the state mutations test blocks make
  between calls; a real pass never mutates mid-evaluation).
- Replay-safety: the frame is pass-scoped scratch, never on GameState, never
  serialized; the cut pattern is a pure function of the fixed slot-scan
  order — live and replay compute identical ratings.

## That Which Lingers on the beneficiary rule (rating audit, continued)

Lingers is the duration meta-enhancer — the skill whose beneficiaries are
all ENCHANTMENTS (`skill_duration != null` = the effect-creating skills; a
fact-correction from the audit discussion: the outgoing-duration modifier
feeds `create_effect` durations only, NOT stuns — those flow through stone
form's separate `outgoing_stun_duration` pipeline).

- The old rating was UNCONDITIONAL 1 — it fired on every cd-5 cycle even
  when nothing duration-bearing would cast in its 2-turn window (the same
  waste-bug class as focus). Under the rule: rate = best live beneficiary
  + 1 (planned ending cast if it carries `skill_duration`; plus every
  positive-rated off-cd non-ending skill with the field), NO fallback —
  extends nothing → no cast (its own recast is outside its window,
  cd 5 > duration 2).
- Its self-exclusion needed zero code: the frame's in-progress guard cuts
  lingers from its own beneficiary scan mechanically (it would otherwise
  count its own `skill_duration`).
- The lingers test caught a subtle invariant violation: `freshOptions` had
  called `aiOptions` directly (bypassing `optionsFor`), so lingers' outer
  evaluation ran UNMARKED and its scan then read lingers' own memoized
  result as a beneficiary rating (2 → offered 3 instead of 2). A direct
  call doesn't crash — it silently mis-rates, which is exactly why the
  "every evaluation enters through optionsFor" rule exists in the docs.
  The helper now takes a SkillId and routes through `optionsFor` like
  everything else; the handler path was already correct (it enters via
  bestCasts → optionsFor, where the guard + memo hold).
- Test: lingers+reaches equipped → lingers offers reaches' rating + 1
  (fires first, so reaches' cast gains the +1 duration); alone → nothing.

## That Which Reaches: the virtual-effect sim differential (rating audit, continued)

The owner's extension of the beneficiary rule for GATING modifiers: when
+1 range would flip an impossible cast into a possible one (the enemy just
out of range of every attack), the smart play is the enchantment. Settled
per discussion (DESIGN → Architecture, AI rating scale — the virtual-effect
sim bullet):

- **Mechanism** (`helpers.bestCastsWithVirtualEffect`): shallow-clone the
  entities slice, append the enhancer's own effect to the cloned caster
  (the denormalized `additive_effect_modifiers` copied from the effect
  definition — mirroring create_effect), run `bestCasts` against the
  simulated state. "Evaluate the bar as if I were already active."
- **Comparison** (`ai_select.plansDiffer`): the WHOLE bar, both pools (owner
  decision — an enabled cantrip counts too); any plan difference —
  different skill, different TARGET, different rating, or a plan appearing
  — is the modifier's doing; the sim plan's rating counts as a live
  beneficiary, max'd with the base-value rule, +1 ordering on top.
- **The recursion subtlety found during design:** the sim frame is FRESH
  (the pass frame's memos are for the real state — virtual-modifier results
  must never leak into the real plan) AND INHERITS the caller's in-progress
  set plus the simulated skill. Without the inheritance, two sim-based
  enhancers equipped together (reaches + the future bull-form sim) would
  alternate through each other's fresh sim frames forever — each sim cuts
  only its own skill. The inherited stack excludes everything currently
  being decided from the hypothetical.
- **Reaches' full shape:** base-value rule (planned ending cast if it
  carries range/radius + positive non-ending range/radius beneficiaries)
  max'd with the sim differential; NO fallback — pure modifiers, nothing
  to enhance + no differential → no cast (the old unconditional 1 fired
  into empty turns).
- **Scope note:** duration-type modifiers (lingers) do NOT adopt the sim —
  they modulate magnitude, almost never flipping a rating; the sim would
  burn cost for zero signal. Bull form (+10 distance flips collision
  ratings) is flagged to adopt it when audited.
- Tests: the enabling case (hostile at slice-range+1 → sim flips slice
  from impossible to possible → reaches = would-be rating + 1; one tile
  further → nothing), the enabled-CANTRIP case (burst's radius boundary),
  the in-range base-value case, and reaches-nothing-when-nothing-applies.
  Fixture lesson en route: a main-hand sword puts only skill_1/skill_2 on
  the bar — slot 3 is the OFF-hand's (skillInSlot).

## That Which Rushes on the beneficiary rule (rating audit, continued)

Rushes' cooldown −1 applies where cooldowns are SET (use_skill), so its
beneficiaries are precisely the casts that will fire this turn AND carry a
cooldown > 0 — each such cast's newly-set cooldown comes out one less: the
planned ending cast when it has a cooldown, plus every positive-rated
off-cd non-ending skill with one (all positive cantrips/enchantments fire
this turn). Rating = best + 1, NO fallback — the speed +1 is a future-turn
rider (the movement phase already ran) and per owner decision "the speed
bonus is not worth wasting a full turn's duration on its own": an enemy
whose only plan is a no-cooldown skill (slice) never casts rushes
standalone. No sim (magnitude modifier, no gating). Tests: howl-beneficiary
(cantrip cd 10 → rushes 2), spinblade-planned (two hostiles → spinblade 2,
cd 2 → rushes 3), and the slice-only plan (no cooldown anywhere → nothing).

## Bull Form on the beneficiary rule + sim differential (rating audit, continued)

Bull form (+10 push distance) adopts reaches' exact shape — base-value
beneficiaries (`distance != null`: the planned ending cast with a push, plus
positive non-ending distance skills) max'd with the virtual-effect sim
differential, no fallback. The shared sim+comparison piece was extracted
(`helpers.simDifferentialGain`, taking the caller's real bestCasts to avoid
re-deriving) so reaches and bull form share one implementation.

- **A real bug found while probing** (fixed): `simDifferentialGain`'s first
  version unwrapped `sim.ending.?` / `sim.non_ending.?` after
  `plansDiffer` — but plansDiffer is ALSO true when the real plan exists and
  the sim's doesn't (the modifier removed a cast) → null unwrap panic. The
  sim side is now unwrapped only when it exists; a sim-null difference
  yields no gain (nothing would-be to benefit from).
- **Fixture lesson (the sim was right all along):** the first test fixture
  showed slam's rating NOT flipping under +10 distance — because slam's
  base push (2) already collided with the blocker; the sim correctly left it
  unchanged while flipping BASH's short push (1 → 11). The final fixture
  places the blocker past every base push distance, so the flip is a pure
  rating upgrade (bash 1 → 2 via collision) — bull form rates the would-be
  2 + 1 = 3 over the base-value rule's 1 + 1 = 2.
- Tests: the collision flip (bull form 3) and the no-distance-bar case
  (sword: nothing pushes, no beneficiary, no differential → no cast).

## Non-ending pool rating audit — COMPLETE (rating audit, closing entry)

The audit opened as a "cheap pass" over stale ported numbers and became a
design session that produced four settled mechanisms (all in DESIGN →
Architecture, AI rating scale): the value-unit anchors (20% heal = 1, full
heal = 2 — owner decisions), the enhancement-enchantment LIVE-beneficiary
rule (+1 ordering, only casts that will actually fire this turn count,
fallback gates otherwise), the pass-scoped EvalFrame (memoized once per
pass, mechanical cycle cut — replacing the structural pool-split guards),
and the virtual-effect sim differential (gating modifiers: reaches'
range/radius, bull form's push-collision flips). Every enhancer landed on
the rule (stone form, lingers, reaches, rushes, bull form); three
wasted-cast gate bugs were fixed in passing (focus counting cantrips,
lingers/reaches/rushes/bull_form firing unconditionally into empty turns);
idol heal 1 / replenish 2 / focus-by-reset-count re-anchored the heal
family.

Sanity pass (no changes needed): howl/burst/accelerate/meditate are
already count-based and gated; blink/swap at rating 1 are honest for
repositioning, with the re-evaluation loop providing the follow-through
(blink closes the gap → the newly-possible attack plans next pass).
One playtest-dependent flag stays in TODO: adjacent swaps/blinks can be
pointless shuffles — gate from playtest texture, not blind (adjacent
swaps might be deliberate displacement).

Also retired here: the aiOptions-churn watch item (superseded by the
frame's once-per-pass bound).

## raylib_backend.zig split — src/raylib/ (the platform-seam cleanup session)

The single-file platform backend (2,704 lines: window + render + audio +
input polling + texture caches + SDF text + diagnostics) is now a
`src/raylib/` directory behind a STRONGER version of the same module
boundary: the headless test-root scan (build.zig `collectZigFiles`) skips
the whole directory instead of one filename, and `scripts/test.sh` carries
a boundary assert (`@import("raylib")` may appear only under `src/raylib/`)
so a stray import fails the test run explicitly. The single-seam rationale
from the mac miscompile hunt (one place raylib can be imported; one
exclusion to forget) is preserved — the exclusion is now per-directory,
which is harder to accidentally bypass than a per-file list.

Files, each a commit with `scripts/test.sh` + `zig build` + a boot-to-menu
run + a `scripts/web.sh` compile (the platform-seam compiles-≠-runs rule;
the headless test build never compiles any of this, so those were the real
gates):

- **backend.zig (433 lines, was 2,704)** — the composition root + driver:
  window, render target + `render()` render pass, real clock, letterbox
  transforms, the duck-typed `RaylibBackend` interface main.zig drives
  (`anytype` — unchanged surface), and thin wrappers over the sub-structs
  (`initAudio`/`playSounds`/`updateMusic`/`fontMetrics`/`entitySpriteBounds`).
- **input_poll.zig** — the key/mouse mapping tables (incl. the mac
  Command-as-Control entries) + the read-then-pump poll body as a free fn
  over the backend's scratch buffers; the letterbox transform is passed in
  (window math stays with the window owner).
- **audio.zig** — `Audio` sub-struct: the music intensity stack + the four
  layered-cue caches. Path building moved off the frame_arena onto fixed
  stack buffers; the init-time music phase-lock warning flows through a
  small sink callback (`DiagnosticsSink`) so Audio stays independent of the
  backend type. `deinitAudio` dropped (deinit calls `audio.deinit()`
  directly — it had no external caller).
- **textures.zig** — `TextureStore` sub-struct: the four lazy caches
  (textures / outline masks / composite inset masks / sprite bounds) + all
  mask-generation math (disk-SE dilation, composite blit, opaque-bounds
  scan). `premultiplyAlpha` shared with the font loader. Draw sites go
  through `backend.textures.*`.
- **text.zig** — `TextRenderer` sub-struct: the TTF load (CPU-premultiplied
  atlas) + the SDF text-outline pipeline (build-time blob, shaders,
  comptime constant guard) + `drawOutlinedText`/`drawTextLabel` (frame-arena
  scratch passed in) + `fontMetrics`. Landed with **conversions.zig**
  (toRaylibColor / toPremultipliedColor / referenceRectangle) shared by text
  + draw, aliased in backend.zig.
- **diagnostics.zig** — `Diagnostics` sub-struct (boot GL info, one-shot
  sprite/panel draw probes, render-target pixel readback), moved as-is
  AHEAD of draw so the draw slice landed clean. The `diag_*` identifier +
  `logs/diag.txt` renames the settled diagnostics REDESIGN had planned
  landed here early (author request): everything is `Diagnostics` /
  `diagnostics` / `logs/diagnostics.txt`; the redesign keeps the names and
  moves the type out of the raylib dir + re-gates it behind --diagnostics.
- **draw.zig** — the world passes (tiles, overlays, ground drawables,
  occlusion insets, world overlays) + the flat UI element list as free fns
  over the backend (the handlers/ pattern); the six render-called fns are
  pub, the internal helpers private.

Design constraints kept: DESIGN → Platform Seam (render target resolution,
premultiplied alpha, SDF text outline), DESIGN → Audio (layered cues, miss-
not-cached layers), the aarch64 tint pre-selection shape in drawNineSlice,
the comptime-out diagnostics gating in non-dev builds. The two-runtime
checks each slice: native boot to main menu + the diagnostics file written
with the new name on both the default and $ZIGLOP_DATA paths.

## Editor palette cells render the full scene composition (entity + decoration tools)

The palette's entity + decoration tool cells previously showed the base
sprite only, tinted at the type's color index — a placed, dual-wielding
enemy or a layered decoration looked different in the cell than in the
viewport. The cells now compose exactly what the scene draws:

- **Entity cells** (`emitEditorEntityToolCell`, src/ui/editor_shell.zig):
  base sprite, then overlay layers, then weapons — all at ONE shared
  fitted rect (entity art shares the 512×640 frame + pivot, so a
  per-image fit would be identical anyway, and one fit makes the
  same-rect invariant testable). Tint rules copied from `entityDrawable`
  (view.zig): base + layers at their own color_index into the team
  gradient (player gradient for team 0, enemy gradient otherwise),
  weapons at team gradient index 1; main hand as-authored, off hand
  MIRRORED; weapons suppressed when `displays_weapons` is false.
- **Decoration cells** (`emitEditorDecorationToolCell`): base + layers at
  their own color_index into the world gradient, same shared fitted
  rect (layer dims are validated equal to the base's at load, so one fit

- Tests: a composed-cell test (layered dual-wielding skeleton, a

## Custom-asset rendering (keep_original_colors, slice 1 of 4)

Custom mission-bundled art (`custom/<mission-dir>/<stem>` stems) resolved
its DIMS from the mission dir but never RENDERED — the texture store built
`assets/<kind>/custom/....png` paths that exist nowhere, so custom sprites
drew the magenta fallback in-world, the sprite picker's Mission cells were
text-only, and the footprint editor filled custom grids with dark cells.
This slice wires rendering end to end (prerequisite for the
`keep_original_colors` feature — an "art keeps its own colors" toggle is
invisible without art):

- **`assetPathFor`** (src/raylib/textures.zig): the file-source path for a
  sprite id — shipped ids read `assets/{id}.png`; ids matching
  `<kind>/custom/<mission-dir>/<file-stem>` read
  `missions/<mission-dir>/<file-stem>.png` from the persistent dir (the
  stem embeds the mission dir, so the path derives from the id alone).
  Used by all four decode paths: texture load, outline mask, composite
  inset, sprite-bounds scan — so health bars / occlusion insets / hover
  outlines work on custom art too.
- **The mission scan carries dims**: `SessionState.editor_mission_sprites`
  is `[]MissionSprite` (`{file_name, pixel_dims}` — state.zig); the scan
  (mission_io.rescanEditorMissionSprites) reads each PNG's IHDR at scan
  time (an input-site IO, keeping view() file-free; unreadable files
  degrade to (0,0) = scaleToFit's full-cell fallback).
- **Sprite-picker Mission cells render**: image cells under the kind's
  folder prefix (`entities/custom/...` / `decorations/custom/...` — the
  same ids view() builds), UNTINTED (custom art keeps its own colors —
  the settled `keep_original_colors` pick-side semantics), entity kinds
  at the fixed 512×640 frame, decoration kinds at the scanned dims.
- **Footprint editor**: the custom-stem dark-fill branch removed — custom
  art draws full-size like shipped stems.
- Tests: picker mission blocks (entity + decoration) assert the rendered
  ids + untinted colors; the footprint custom block asserts the image
  branch; handler tests assert the scan's `.file_name`.
