## Double deltaMicroseconds() per frame — all waits/anims slowed ~20-60x (bug fix)

Since the layered-music commit (`9a8ce2d`, "volume lerp"), `frame()`
called the stateful `backend.deltaMicroseconds()` TWICE per frame: once
inline in the `updateMusic(...)` call and once for the gameplay
`delta_microseconds`. Each call returns time since the PREVIOUS call and
resets `last_time_microseconds`, so the music call ate the whole
inter-frame delta (e.g. 16.7ms at 60fps vsync) and handed the gameplay
delta only the microseconds between the two call sites (the
pollInput/computeCamera stretch, well under 1ms). Every clock driven by
`delta_microseconds` — the turn-flow wait timer, `session_clock`,
`animation_clock` (all one-shot + looping anims) — advanced at a small
fraction of real time: every wait stretched enormously, all animations
crawled. `session_clock` was slowed equally (debounced-write deadlines
stretch too, harmlessly).

Fix: read the delta ONCE at the top of `frame()` and pass it into both
`updateMusic` and the wait/session/animation advancement; the hoist also
documents the statefulness trap at the call site. The read moving a few
lines earlier (before `pollInput`) is fine — pure wall-clock
measurement, and slightly more accurate. `updateMusic`'s volume lerp
still receives the same real delta it always consumed.

## Effect pacing 1+2 — the `damage` event + intra-hit waits

Chained effect events fired back-to-back in one drain, stacking their
sound cues (the muddiness) and skipping renders (the mid-drain render
gate means intermediate states never draw). Design decision first: the
options were a presentation-layer sound stagger (like the existing
0.125s damage-number stagger) or waits on the EVENT TIMELINE. Chose the
timeline — sound must stay in sync with the thing creating it, and a
timeline wait also buys visible sequencing. The prerequisite: damage
application was baked into the `attack`/`collision` arms, so there was
no event boundary between a hit's resolution and its damage landing.

**Slice 1 — the `damage` event** (`events.zig` SubLevelEvent +
`handlers/level.zig`): `attack`/`collision` keep their RESOLUTION stages
(aggro activation, their own callbacks, the intercept fold — attack only,
collision deliberately skips it (Reflect counterplay) — + defense) and
push the resolved post-defense amount onto one shared `damage` apply arm
(health, mission stats, hit flash, damage number,
onOutgoing/IncomingDamage gated `triggers_effects`, death push,
lifesteal push). Dedupes the two near-identical apply blocks (the
primitive-composition rule). The `SoundId.damage` impact cue moved into
the apply arm (impact = when damage lands, sound + flash + number
together); behavior change: a hit on an already-dead defender no longer
sounds (was: crunch then early-return), and collision-sourced damage now
also plays the impact cue alongside the wall crunch. Combat-log tier
`.none` (attack/collision entries already represent the hit). LIFO note:
the damage event is pushed last by its resolver arm, so it pops
immediately after the resolver returns — identical timing to the old
inline apply. Cross-version note: session logs / validation replays
recorded before this change fail strict replay verification (handlers
now push extra child events) — pre-release, re-record rather than
migrate.

**Slice 2 — intra-hit waits:** `effect_step_wait_milliseconds` (125) —
distinct from `turn_flow_wait_milliseconds` (500, turn pacing not hit
pacing) — pushed at both resolver arms as `[damage, wait]` (LIFO: the
wait pops first, the damage lands when it elapses). During the wait the
render gate draws, so the resolution state renders before the impact.
Every hit (player + enemy, all skills composing `attack`/`collision`) is
now paced; a 0-damage hit still waits + shows its "0". Full suite passes
(the test harness clears `waiting` per event — waits are no-ops in
tests, same as the turn-flow precedent).

Remaining sweep (per-target AoE gaps, bash's chain, knockback →
collision, attack → lifesteal) tracked in TODO → Effect pacing — note the
knockback arm currently pushes the forced move BEFORE the collision
event, and LIFO means the crunch resolves before the slide lands;
slide-then-crunch presentation needs that push order revisited.

## Effect pacing hotfix — the wait array order + knockback push order

Two ordering bugs from the slice-2 commit, both LIFO mistakes in
opposite directions:

1. **The wait array was inverted at both resolver arms.** pushEvents
   APPENDS in array order and the dispatch pops from the back, so the
   LAST array element pops first. I pushed `[wait, damage]` while the
   comment said "the wait sits last so it pops first" — the damage sat
   on top and landed immediately, and the wait paced the gap before the
   NEXT attack instead (playtest symptom: attack → damage instant,
   multi-attacks staggered). Fix: `[damage, wait]`. The comment was
   right; the array was wrong.

2. **Knockback pushed the forced move before the collision event**, so
   LIFO resolved the crunch (flash + damage number + damage) while the
   defender was still at its origin tile, then the slide landed
   (playtest symptom: impact visuals before the push). Fix: push the
   collision first, the move second — the slide pops first, then the
   crunch, and the collision → damage wait gives the impact visuals a
   beat after the push is visible. Bonus correctness: a
   collision-killed entity now dies at its landing tile instead of
   sliding after death. The damage-number direction is unaffected — the
   destination lies on the push ray, so the axis-normalized
   attacker→defender delta is identical.

## AoE spiral execution order (+ meteor center strike)

All radius AoE skills enumerated targets by walking `level.entities` in
spawn order (reads top-left row-by-row). Replaced with the SPIRAL:
`skill_helpers.spiralTilesInRadius` walks the rings around the center —
innermost first, each ring from its top-left tile CLOCKWISE (top edge
left→right, right edge top→bottom, bottom edge right→left, left edge
bottom→top; ring n has exactly 8n tiles) — and `hostileIndicesInRadius`
(the one enumeration all 9 radius AoE skills use) now maps hostile
entities through that tile walk (`hostileEntityAt` per tile, preserving
the living/hostile/not-caster filter). The center tile is NOT part of
the spiral; meteor — the only AoE that strikes the center — prepends the
center attack so the direct hit lands FIRST, then the splash ripples
outward. (Behavior-preserving note: the old distance filter included
distance-0, so meteor always hit the center; the spiral excludes it and
meteor re-adds it explicitly. Every other AoE is self-centered, where
the center is the caster's own tile — excluded by the same filter both
before and after.) Per-target grouping confirmed already true for every
multi-effect AoE (shockwave attack+knockback, slam knockback+stun, blitz
attack+stun — one target's full effect list before the next), so the
pacing sweep will present one target at a time with no recipe changes.

Tests: the spiral geometry (ring-1 clockwise order, ring-2 continuation,
8n per ring), the filter (dead + same-team skipped, ring order in the
result), and meteor's center-first execution (asserted on the REVERSED
ownedEvents array — last element executes first). Convention: DESIGN →
Determinism & Tiebreaking (AoE execution order).

## Effect pacing 3 — the generic skill rule (ownedEvents interleaves the waits)

Settled as a GENERIC RULE instead of the planned per-skill sweep: every
skill that pushes more than one event gets a 125ms wait between each
consecutive pair, interleaved mechanically in `helpers.ownedEvents` (the
one constructor every recipe's list goes through) in natural execution
order before the LIFO reversal. Skills never insert waits themselves —
pacing derives from the list length, so new multi-event skills are paced
for free and forgetting a wait is structurally impossible (the
machine-walked-truth hygiene rule). Bash's manual wait was removed
(subsumed — it would have doubled the gap); `effectStepWait` became
file-private since only ownedEvents constructs waits now.

Scope decisions (see DESIGN → Architecture → Skill pacing): the rule
covers a skill's OWN authored list only. Effect-triggered lists
(Reflect's counter-hit) and handler-composed follow-ups (death, the
lifesteal heal, knockback's move→collision) resolve immediately — causal
consequences, not an authored sequence. Accepted costs: +1 recorded wait
per gap (session logs/crash dumps/validation replays grow ~2-3x per
multi-event skill use) and linear drain latency on large AoEs (a packed
meteor can run ~4s — deliberate ripple; escape hatches if it drags:
shorten the constant, or a per-skill opt-out field when a real case
appears).

Test fallout was instructive: the membership loops that read
`event.sub_level_event.attack` directly panicked on interleaved wait
events (bad union access) — they now skip by TAG (`event == .meta_event`);
length-pinned sites updated (n events → 2n-1 slots); a new ownedEvents
unit test pins the interleave semantics. The follow-up idea (an
accelerating variant — each skill use resets the gap to 125ms and the
following waits shrink, so long chains wind up) is recorded as deferred
in TODO → Effect pacing.

## Accelerating effect pacing — one decay sequence shared by all the 0.125s waits

The flat rule's linear latency made big AoEs drag; the accelerating rule
makes them wind up. All intra-effect waits now share ONE decay sequence
per skill use, per the agreed example (spinblade ×3: attack → 125 →
damage → 93 → attack → 69 → damage → 51 → attack → 38 → damage):

- `MetaEvent.accelerating_wait` — an EMPTY-payload wait variant. The
  duration is computed at POP time by the wait arm from
  `GameState.wait_acceleration`: 125ms decayed by 3/4 per prior gap in
  the chain (integer math, floored at 1ms — 125, 93, 69, 51, 38, 28, 21,
  15, 11, 8, 6, 4, 3, 2, 1 — long tails converge to near-simultaneous
  without zero-duration no-op events; initially 2/3, retuned to 3/4 the
  same session for a gentler ramp). `acceleratedEffectStepWaitMilliseconds`
  in skill_helpers.zig is the pure decay function.
- Consumers: `ownedEvents`' interleave AND the attack/collision arms'
  hit-resolution → damage-landing gap — the same variant, the same
  counter, so a skill's whole chain accelerates together (the flat-rule
  alternative where only the interleave gaps decay would leave the
  125ms damage beats dominating — the acceleration would barely read).
- Reset: ONE site — the `use_skill` arm. The feared stale-counter
  problem doesn't exist: every attack is skill-mediated (the player's
  attack step IS a weapon-skill use; enemies only cast via bestCasts —
  no bare attack pushes outside skills except adrenaline_surge's
  handler expansion, which rides the use_skill reset upstream).
- Replay-safety (the design crux): the counter is event-driven
  GameState — reset + increments are handler transforms, carried in
  snapshots, recomputed identically on replay/undo. The derived
  durations need nothing in the payload, which is exactly why a
  SessionState counter would have broken (unreplayed state → divergent
  durations on undo). Session-log: the empty payload round-trips (a
  zero-field struct serializes as just the `event` discriminator line —
  pinned in the serializer round-trip test).

Tests: the decay sequence + 1ms floor (skill_helpers), the empty-payload
round-trip (session_log), and an end-to-end harness test (spinblade on
two targets leaves wait_acceleration == 3; a follow-up single-hit skill
resets — exactly 1 wait, proving the per-skill reset). Design: DESIGN →
Architecture → Skill pacing.

## Gear upgrading — design settled (implementation deferred)

Design session settling the upgrade economy + hub vendor panel. The prose
lives in DESIGN → Gear Upgrading, the slices in TODO → Gear Upgrading,
the map line in AGENTS → Subsystem Map. The shape, in brief:

- Income model extracted from the clone design: I(m) = R·m and
  W(m) = R·m(m+1)/2 per wallet, R = N·T = 27 (N = 0.6 materials/turn/
  wallet measured, T = 45 turns; direct pickups and clone harvest merge
  because the clone rate IS the pickup rate). The enemy drop stream
  (gear + inventory + a tome per equipped utility skill on death) is
  inside the measured R, not beside it — sparse enemy gear slots are
  balance + inventory management + R stability.
- Two anchors: 75% tier at m=3 (the b-line boss attempt — 3 completions,
  no central starter mission, wallets drain to zero exactly at the tier
  via the α solve) and 100% at the 66-mission campaign end (on-path
  player ends exactly maxed, wallets empty).
- The starter-anchored cost ladder cost = α·K·R·(1 + (v−s)·d) with
  s derived from new_player.txt and the split mirroring the item kind's
  salvage definition; wallet-binding α solve: armor 0.054 / weapon 0.30 /
  spell 0.60 — the ranking forced by the wallet mix and matching design
  intent (survivability drip, weighty weapons, premium spells). Speed
  0→1 trivial, 1→2 the single biggest purchase, never on dropped boots
  in the official campaign.
- Drops are pre-bought rungs (the model tracks stat points, never
  items): regular drops low-roll variety + materials; boss drops are
  authored high-stat gear riding the uniform death-drop rule (no special
  mechanic), 9-of-10 leaving the final rung purchasable.
- The tail (75→100%) is priced by the tier frontier's wealth gaps
  (≈3.5k / 19.6k / 36.5k parts per wallet) — escalation automatic from
  quadratic income; integer tail prices script-generated once the boss
  drop table exists (the sound_report.sh pattern).
- Post-game: cosmetic base-builder + player customization parked as the
  next design session; composes cleanly (campaign ends wallets-empty).

All numbers are tuning starting points; the anchors + the audit
identities (wallet-binding at m=3, the end-state identity, the
demand-vs-W diff) are the invariants.

## Post-game rewards & cosmetics — design settled (low priority, deferred)

Design session settling the post-completion material sink (builds on the
Gear Upgrading session's parked note). Prose in DESIGN → Post-game
Rewards & Cosmetics, slices in TODO → Post-game Rewards & Cosmetics, map
line in AGENTS → Subsystem Map. The shape, in brief:

- Premise confirmed from existing design, not new work: dreams run the
  official mission lifecycle, so custom missions clone + harvest exactly
  like official ones — every mission ever completed adds ~27/wallet to
  every future mission's paycheck, permanently (the indefinite-scaling
  engine the sink absorbs).
- Overflow guard: u32 wallets + u64 per-clone intermediates put honest
  overflow at ~17,800 distinct missions / ~2.4M replays; a crafted
  "farm" custom mission is the real worst case (~10x). Rule: material
  adds saturate (clamp at u32 max, never wrap). The shop ladder's top
  tier doubles as the drain valve toward that ceiling.
- Hub decoration customization, central hub only: a placement list on
  PlayerData applied as an overlay at hub build (replay-safe, rides
  PlayerData like gear); the editor's decoration planner/rules/registry
  reused for a hub build mode; buy-once-place-freely ownership; the
  dreamguide stays a separate NPC in every hub. Build-mode entry
  UNDECIDED (open in TODO).
- Weapon skins (weapons only, for now): per-type registry + per-type
  selection on PlayerData (`weaponSprite` is the single insertion
  point); ONE unlock mechanism covering both sources — an item skin-id
  flag grants the skin on pickup (unique boss weapons in official
  content, authored drops in custom missions); custom missions ship
  skin art from v1 under the existing `custom/<mission-dir>/<stem>` id
  (resolvable from missions/ anytime; deleted-source fallback renders
  the default sprite + greys the picker entry).
- Pricing: static tier ladder (~x10 tiers, hundreds of parts to a
  near-ceiling flex tier) + evergreen catalog growth + self-gating
  shops (no completion flag); dynamic/wealth-indexed pricing rejected
  again (same reasoning as upgrades).

User note recorded in TODO: cosmetic systems are NOT a priority for a
while — the official campaign comes first.

## WebGL 2 — web build switched from WebGL1 (render smoothing slice 0)

Slice 0 of the render-smoothing work (settled plan: DESIGN → Platform Seam →
WebGL 2 + Sprite-mipmap smoothing; TODO → Platform Layer). The web build now
requests a WebGL2 context:

- `build.zig`: the web raylib dependency sets `opengl_version = .gles_3`
  (raylib-zig's emscripten default is `.gles_2`/WebGL1), and the emcc step
  sets `MIN_WEBGL_VERSION=2` + `MAX_WEBGL_VERSION=2`. The TWO must stay in
  lockstep: raylib compiles for GL ES 3 and submits its built-in shaders as
  `#version 300 es`, while emcc's GL glue defaults to creating a WebGL1
  context — missing the emcc half produced the exact black screen caught by
  the runtime check (every shader failing "unsupported shader version 300").
  Raylib pairs these the same way in its own examples Makefile
  (BUILD_WEB_WEBGL2).
- `src/raylib/text.zig`: the SDF outline shader's GLSL ES 1.00 fallback
  variant is REPLACED by a 300 es variant (same math as desktop, including
  `fwidth`; highp floats — the AA band is a small fwidth delta that mediump
  would band). One shader shape on both platforms now.

Why WebGL2 (settled before the switch): WebGL1 forbids mipmaps on NPOT
textures and most of our art is NPOT (512x640 entities, arbitrary custom
assets) — the sprite-mipmap slice would break most art on web; and ES 3.00
gives `fwidth` for shader AA. Browser floor moves to Safari/iOS 15 (2021) —
accepted, the game's web audience is desktop browsers. Verified in the
browser: page loads, main menu renders, no shader warnings in the console.
WebGL2 also refuses mipmaps on the SDF atlas's unsized LUMINANCE_ALPHA
format — that atlas stays mip-free by design, so the refusal is
self-enforcing. Custom-asset dimension rule (entities 512x640, decoration
art whole 256x256-tile rectangles) recorded in TODO → Content Loading.

## Sprite mipmaps — trilinear sprite filtering (render smoothing slice 1)

Slice 1 of the render-smoothing work (slice 0: WebGL 2, entry above; settled
plan: DESIGN → Platform Seam → Sprite-mipmap smoothing). The harsh world-asset
edges at zooms below 1:1 were undersampled bilinear minification — bilinear
reads only the 2x2 texels nearest each sample point, which is exactly right
at an aligned 2:1 (box filter) and increasingly wrong past it (default camera
zoom 50% x the 0.5 renderScale = 1/4 source scale on a 1080p target; each
destination pixel covers ~4x4 texels but only 4 are read, and which ones
shifts per frame while panning).

`textures.zig` gains `enableTrilinearMipmaps` — `genTextureMipmaps` +
`.trilinear` — applied at the two TextureStore upload sites: the main sprite
load (`ensureSpriteLoaded`) and the generated outline/inset mask upload
(`rgbaBufToTexture`). One choke point, so shipped, persistent-dir shadowed,
and custom-mission art all get the mip chain at load (GPU-side build, +33%
VRAM, no per-frame cost; premultiplied RGBA box-filters correctly, which is
why the existing premultiply prep made this a clean drop-in). Mip-averaging
also turns the binary mask edges into fractional coverage. Magnified and 1:1
draws sample the base level, so nothing sharp got blurred.

Deliberately NOT mipmapped: the SDF font atlas (a distance field box-filtered
between levels would move glyph edges — stays bilinear) and the render-target
blit texture (a <=2:1 box-filtered downscale per frame; per-frame mip
generation would cost for no visible gain). The plain coverage font atlas is
untouched here — it is slice 2's removal target (all text moves to the SDF
pipeline, plain fill at outlineWidth = 0).

Verified: native (zoom 25% — soft stable edges while panning, no new blur at
100%) and the web compile; WebGL2 (slice 0) makes NPOT art (512x640 entities,
arbitrary custom dims) mipmap-legal on web.

## Text unified through the SDF pipeline + outline-width clamp (render smoothing slice 2)

Slice 2 of the render-smoothing work (slice 0 WebGL 2 / slice 1 sprite
mipmaps: entries above; settled plan: DESIGN → Platform Seam → SDF text
outline, TODO → Platform Layer). Two related landings:

**Unification.** ALL text now draws through the SDF pipeline — plain text is
the same shader with a zero outline width, so every string is
resolution-independent (the pre-unification plain path sampled a runtime
128px coverage atlas bilinearly, undersampled 2.5–5:1 at a 1080p target —
the font half of the "native 1080p looks harsh" report). Two subtleties
handled:

- A zero outline width MUST pass a transparent outline color: the collapsed
  band sits exactly on the fill edge, and an opaque one source-over-composites
  black into the antialiased fringe (outA = 2fa − fa² — a dark, over-bright
  edge on every glyph).
- The coverage-atlas font is demoted to a fallback-only load: init tries the
  SDF pipeline first and builds the coverage font only when that fails (below
  that, raylib's default font for a broken TTF, as before). The normal path
  never builds the atlas (drops its startup raster + ~2MB VRAM; the runtime
  "76/95 glyphs" warning disappeared with it). `fontMetrics` reads from the
  ACTIVE font so layout always measures with the advances drawn with.
- Batching note: every label now toggles beginShaderMode (as outlined labels
  already did), so runs of consecutive labels flush the render batch slightly
  more often. Labels already force texture-change flushes when interleaved
  with sprites; hoist to a scoped pass only if it ever shows.

**Outline-width clamp** (a long-standing bug surfaced while verifying):
the 48px material-count labels showed ghost squares at the outline corners.
Root cause: the atlas encodes distance only to −21.33 atlas px (alpha 0 at
scale 6), and the 48px request (8·128/48 ≈ 21.3) lands exactly on the clamp
floor — the shader's fade window straddles it, so every clamped texel
evaluates band ≈ 0.5, and clamped texels are exactly the glyph-rect CORNER
diagonals (true ink distance ~30px where the rect is only 22px padded per
axis) → fixed-size dark squares at each glyph quad's corner. Larger sizes
(56px+ → 18.3 atlas px and below) stay clear of the floor, which is why only
small outlined text squared. Fix: `drawSdfText` clamps the requested
atlas-px width to `sdf_max_outline_atlas_pixels` (floor −2 for the fwidth
window) — an oversized request draws a marginally thinner outline (7.2px
instead of 8 at 48px, imperceptible), never squares. Diagnosed by parsing the
generated blob (glyph rects confirmed to include the 22px padding — not a
quad-clipping issue; a corner-diagonal range issue).

Design: DESIGN → Platform Seam → SDF text outline (unification, clamp, the
transparent-outline-color rule, fallback policy). Verified: native (plain +
outlined text at all sizes, inventory material counts clean), web compile +
browser run.

## Sprite-pass LOD snap — fixing the washed-out 0.75x zoom (follow-up to slice 1)

Follow-up to the sprite-mipmap slice (entries above; design: DESIGN →
Platform Seam → Sprite-pass LOD snap). After trilinear mipmaps landed, zoom
0.75 looked washed out compared to 0.5 and 1.0: trilinear's fractional blend
at a NON-dyadic minification mixes in the heavily-averaged deeper level
(zoom 0.75 on a 1080p target = LOD 1.41 → 41% of the 4x-averaged level 2),
over-blurring versus the ideal 2.67x box. Which zoom washes depends on the
render preset (the camera zoom takes only four values, 0.25/0.5/0.75/1.0,
and zoom × renderScale lands exactly ON a mip level only at powers of two).

Fix — option A of the two considered (the other, exact software-box-filtered
variant textures per zoom level, deferred; see DESIGN): the backend's
sprite-pass shader (`src/raylib/backend.zig`), raylib's default batch
fragment shader (texel × tint, blend-mode-orthogonal, white-texture rects
pass through) plus an `lodBias` uniform, snapped per frame to the SHARPER
adjacent mip level for the current zoom × render-preset combo
(`spriteLodSnapBias` — subtracts the LOD's fractional part; 0 at exact
powers of two, so on-level combos render identically to before). Residual
cost: the sharper level is undersampled by up to 2^frac (≤1.5x across the
16 combos) — mild sparkle on fine detail instead of uniform blur, the
standard sharpness trade.

Two raylib facts shaped the implementation:
- SetShaderValue binds the program itself (rlEnableShader), so the
  set-uniform-then-beginShaderMode pattern (inherited from the SDF path) is
  sound rather than lucky.
- EndShaderMode restores the DEFAULT shader, not the enclosing scope — so
  scopes must not span text draws: one scope for the text-free world layers
  (tiles/overlays/ground/insets — the big batch-friendly runs), per-item
  scopes for world overlays (floating combat numbers) and UI elements
  (SDF labels switch shaders mid-element; every element draws sprites
  before text, so per-element scoping is exact). Per-element scoping adds
  no meaningful flush cost — slice 2's per-label shader toggles already
  flush at that granularity.

Shader compile failure degrades to plain trilinear (no scope; the
washed-out intermediate zooms return rather than anything breaking).
Verified natively at all four zooms (0.75 matches the crispness character
of 0.5/1.0; 0.25/1.0 pixel-identical to before) + web compile.

## Global top bar — always-visible options/undo/redo + redo button

The infinite undo/redo timeline is core to the game, but its only surface
was the undo button in the level/hub/editor top bar — invisible on menus
and under full-screen overlays. Redo had NO button at all (machinery fully
wired since the input-convergence work: binding, anytime flag,
`history.redo`, consumption + sound — only the UI was missing).

Landed (`screens.zig` / `view.zig` / `state.zig`):

- **`buildGlobalTopBar`** (renamed from `buildTopBar`): options, undo, redo
  in the top-left, emitted LAST in view()'s UI assembly — the painter's-order
  list draws it above everything (options menu, mission-complete/fail,
  error popup) and hitTest's topmost-first scan gives it click priority.
  Zero new layering machinery: "always on top" is a property the flat
  element list already had. The editor's level tabs deliberately stay in
  the editor arm (UNDER overlays, per the design call); the tab row starts
  right of the bar's three cells (region_left 2→3 slots in editor_shell).
- **Redo button**: mirrors undo's glyph flipped horizontally
  (Image.flip_horizontal — emitted inline; emitIconButton has no flip
  parameter and this is the only flipped icon button). ui/icon_undo AND the
  flipped redo are magenta placeholders — artist list (icon_redo planned).
- **Dim state**: `GameStateHistory.canUndo`/`canRedo` (new, mirroring
  undo/redo's own branching incl. the mid-drain jump-to-current-idle case;
  unit-tested) thread through `RenderContext` into the bar. An unavailable
  button gets its background re-drawn on top at 50% alpha tinted the
  theme's darkest — the same wash skill cooldowns use. Still clickable
  (no-op, exactly like the keybind).
- **Options button**: hidden on the main menu (that screen's button stack
  is its option surface; the Escape chain the action routes through already
  no-ops there — no remnant cleanup was needed, the main menu never had an
  options entry). Clicking it while the menu is open toggles the menu
  closed (routes through the Escape chain, same as before). Slot stays
  reserved so undo/redo don't shift position between screens.
- **FPS overlay** moved below the bar (it owned the top-left corner before).

Buttons emit the same anytime actions as the keybinds — no handler changes,
replay-safe by construction, undo/redo reachable from any screen including
over the mission-complete overlay (undoing the completing move dismisses
it; it's on the timeline).

## Top bar shrunk to 128px buttons + editor primary actions matched

Follow-up to the global top bar (entry above): the top bar's buttons
(options / undo / redo) went 256x256 → 128x128 (`top_bar_slot_size`,
new; `top_bar_height` 256 → 128). The bottom bar's 256 slots are
deliberately untouched — `slot_size` is the bottom bar's / pickers'
constant, the top bar now has its own. The editor's Test + Validate
buttons match (`editor_primary_actions_width` derives from the new
constant; level-tab clamps follow).

Everything downstream derives, so the cascade was automatic —
`middle_panel_height` went 1648 → 1776 (and is now a DERIVED constant,
reference_height − bars, instead of a hand-maintained literal), the
editor inspector/metadata windows fit one more row, the pickers grew
128 taller, the camera band +128 at the top, the FPS overlay moved
below the bar. The window-census tests pinned to the old geometry were
updated from the builder's (unchanged) semantics; the inspector's
label-census helper now prints the found window on mismatch, which
made the sweep mechanical.

## Middle panels top-anchored + dedicated bottom-bar indicator strip

Follow-up to the 128px top-bar pass (entry above): with the band 128
taller, the middle panels grew to fill it and ran straight into the
bottom bar — hiding the indicator row (momentum above the health globe,
active effects above the skill bars, move/attack steps above skip) behind
open panels. That overlap predates the top-bar change (the old 1648-tall
panels ended at the bar top too); the taller band just made it obvious.

Settled geometry (DESIGN → UI Framework → Entity inspect):
- `middle_panel_height` is now the inventory grid's EXACT-FIT content
  height, DERIVED from the same constants the builder lays out with
  (`middle_panel_header_height + 2*ui_gap + inventory_rows*slot`), not
  the band height — the panel can never outgrow its grid, and the value
  can't go stale (its previous form, a hand-maintained 1648 literal,
  was exactly the drift pattern the derive-don't-curate rule warns
  about; the brief reference_height−bars derivation inherited from the
  128px pass was wrong for the same reason — it coupled the panel to
  the bars instead of to its content).
- Panels are TOP-ANCHORED in the band (the old "vertically centered" was
  a no-op while panel height equaled the band; centering a shorter
  panel would re-cover the strip). The strip between the panel bottoms
  and the bar is the indicator row's dedicated space — indicators moved
  flush against the bar top (the freed strip is exactly one 128 icon
  tall, so the old 16px ui_gap above them had to go; keeping it would
  clip the icon tops under the panels).
- Known edge: effect icons wrap UPWARD when more than one row is active,
  and a second row rises back under the panels (needs ~16+ concurrent
  effects to hit; accepted).

## Testing discipline — design settled (DESIGN → Testing)

The test-design session TODO called for: a coherent pass over the suite's
brittle shape, motivated by the 128px top-bar change breaking ~15
window-census tests whose semantics were unchanged. The DESIGN went in
this session; the file-by-file census sweep is the follow-up task
(TODO → Census-test sweep).

What landed (all in DESIGN → Testing):
- **The four bug classes** the suite exists to catch (determinism/replay,
  gameplay semantics, format round-trips, UI structural emission) with
  the deletion criterion: an assertion serving none of them asserts
  churn-by-design.
- **Tier conventions** — pure-fn tests inline in the owning file; handler
  drain tests in `handler_tests_*.zig` via the harness; skill contracts in
  `skill_tests.zig`; UI structure tests inline in the owning ui file. Per-
  variant convention: every new event variant lands with ≥1 drain test.
- **Assertion patterns** — contract over mechanics; derive expectations
  from the source the code iterates; exhaustiveness properties over
  pinned windows (iterate all scroll offsets, assert reachability/
  clamps — geometry is the input, never the expectation); semantic
  queries over positional ones; one assertion kind per fact; census
  helpers print found-vs-expected (expectInspectorLabels is the pattern);
  awkward values.
- **Deletion policy** — subsumed tests are deleted, not ported; strength
  is the criterion, not count.
- **Coverage matrix REJECTED** with the reasoning recorded (comptime
  impossible; grep report lies via helper-mediated pushes; blanket smoke
  test dies on fail-fast preconditions). If an untested-variant gap bites
  again, the grep report is written then, as an advisory.

Doc moves in the same pass: AGENTS → Testing discipline now holds only
the working mechanics (arena blind spots, no-expectPanics workaround,
sweep-script rules) and points at DESIGN; the Subsystem Map gained a
Testing line; the TODO notes ("Test design session", the coverage-matrix
half of "Handler test coverage", "Test values that miss edge cases")
collapsed into pointers/settled design.

## Census sweep slice 1 — the editor inspector (exhaustiveness shape + the shared census helper)

First file of the census-test sweep (TODO → Census-test sweep; design:
DESIGN → Testing). `ui/editor_inspector.zig`'s window-census tests —
hand-pinned visible-row windows at magic scroll offsets (the shape that
broke ~15 tests on the semantics-neutral 128px top-bar change) — were
converted to the exhaustiveness shape:

- **`src/test_ui_census.zig`** (new, test-build-only): the hoisted
  mismatch-printing census helper. `expectContentReachable` builds a panel
  at EVERY scroll offset 0..clamped max and asserts (1) each window's
  labels are an ordered subset of the expected full content list, (2) the
  union of all windows covers the list — no never-emitted row, no
  unreachable row. Geometry is the input, never the expectation; the
  expected list is the panel's semantic content contract, not a window
  snapshot. Panels duck-type
  `buildAt(self, scroll, *UiElementList) anyerror!i32` returning the
  CLAMPED offset (the builder's own clamp; a maxInt probe yields the max).
- `InspectorPanel` / `MetadataSidebarPanel` — file-local census drivers
  over the two builders (the second file to adopt the helper defines its
  own driver struct; the helper itself is shared).
- 13 tests converted. Pinned windows became per-offset scans (semantic
  facts asserted wherever visible, plus stronger "never at ANY offset"
  checks for hidden controls); the entity-content census pins the full
  semantic label list once; counts derive from source enums

## Custom-asset dimensions — slice 1: load-side warn + degrade (footprint clamps + dims floor)

Custom content is untrusted: every spec violation in the mission/sprite
load path now degrades with a warning instead of crashing or silently
rendering wrong — the balance-bounds posture, extended to geometry. Design:
DESIGN → Custom Missions & Online Services → Custom-asset dimensions.

- **`resolveDecorationSpriteDimensions` → `?Vector2`**: an unknown shipped
  stem or a missing/invalid mission PNG returns null instead of panicking;
  the caller degrades to a 256x256 fallback (renders magenta — the texture
  store can't resolve it either) with a warning naming the stem.
- **Dims floor (`flooredSpriteGridDims`)**: custom decoration dims floor to
  whole 256px tiles, minimum 1x1 per axis (a sub-256 sprite previously
  produced a 0x0 bbox — a footprint-tile panic on hand-authored content;
  a 1000px sprite already rendered with its edge silently cropped). Floor
  warns; >4096px warns (max texture size — no size cap, huge art is legal).
  Entity frame constants moved to `types.entity_sprite_frame_*`
  (editor_shell + view alias them).
- **Footprint clamps (`clampDecorationFootprint`, replacing
  `validateDecorationFootprint`)**: out-of-bbox tiles dropped, world tiles
  overlapping a level/hub tile dropped, malformed `footprint` lines skipped
  (was a panic), an emptied or authored-empty footprint defaults to the
  sprite grid's bottom-left tile (the pick-commit default). All warnings
  name the decoration + file; all clamps are pure functions of the file
  bytes → replay-safe.
- **Decoration layers**: a dims mismatch vs the base warns and the layer is
  kept (renders cropped — the view builds layer pieces from the BASE's
  source rects); an unresolvable layer sprite warns and stays. Was a
  load-time panic.
- **Entity sprites (base + layers)**: warn-only when a custom stem isn't
  512x640 or can't be resolved — the fixed-frame render continues.
- **Surfacing**: the warnings thread through `loadLevel`/`loadHub`/`
  `buildEditorMission` to the same `surfaceWarnings` popup as balance
  bounds; `loadHub` gained `file_path` + `warnings` params (start_hub now
  surfaces them; hubs are official content so the list is empty in
  practice). Registry/defaults paths pass null (shipped content —
  regressions are caught by the content tests, not runtime popups).
- Tests: the four footprint clamp classes (malformed / out-of-bbox /
  overlap / empty — valid art never warns, exact warning count), custom
  decoration dims (floor, >4096, missing fallback, unknown shipped stem),
  layer mismatch kept + warned, custom entity sprite warn-only (three

- Cleanup: a leftover `std.debug.print` in writers.zig's

## Custom-asset dimensions — slice 2: the render-side magenta gate

The "never silently render off-grid art" half: a custom sprite whose pixel
dims fail its kind's spec is treated as MISSING at every render path — the
existing magenta fallback draws, exactly like absent art. Complements the
load-side floor/clamps (slice 1: geometry stays valid; slice 2: the pixels
stay honest).

- **`types.customSpriteDimsPassGate(sprite_id, dims)`** — the predicate
  lives in types.zig (raylib-free, unit-tested): `entities/custom/…` must
  be exactly the fixed 512x640 frame; `decorations/custom/…` whole
  multiples of 256 both axes (zero/negative gated); every other id passes
  untouched — the gate is scoped to custom art only (shipped art is
  certified by the build-time metadata table; ui/ icons are 128x128 and
  world/ sources have their own conventions). No SIZE gate: the >4096
  load warning is advisory, huge art renders where the device allows.
- **Applied at the texture store's three decode sites**
  (src/raylib/textures.zig): the main texture load (ensureSpriteLoaded —
  a gated sprite caches as known-missing, so the magenta path is taken
  with zero re-read cost), the outer outline mask (the highlight falls
  back to a rectangle ring around the magenta box), and the composite
  occlusion-inset blit (blitSpriteAlpha returns its existing
  `error.MissingSprite` — a gated sprite contributes no alpha, so the
  inset trace matches what's actually drawn). `getSpriteBounds` stays
  ungated — it's pure layout math (palette aspect-fit), not visual
  output.
- **Entity wrong-dims art now renders magenta, not stretched** — the
  load-side warning text updated to match ("will render as fallback"),
  and the DESIGN section records the gate semantics.
- Tests: the predicate's three contracts in types.zig (entity exactly
  512x640, decoration multiples of 256 incl. huge/zero/negative
  awkward values, non-custom ids never gated). The store itself is
  raylib-linked (headless-excluded) — the predicate is the testable
  seam, the store wiring is three one-line checks.
- Platform-seam verification per the compiles-≠-runs rule: native +
  web builds compile (`scripts/web.sh`); the gate is on the
  texture-load path (post-GL-init), same code shape as the existing
  missing-asset fallback it extends.

## Custom-asset dimensions — slice 3: the editor picker filter

The mission-local sprite-picker tab offers only spec-conforming art per
kind — the acquisition side of the same gate the render side applies
(slice 2). The scan (`rescanEditorMissionSprites`) already carries each
file's IHDR dims, so the filter is pure — no IO at pick time.

- **Filter rules** (editor_pickers.zig, the mission_local cell build):
  `customSpriteDimsPassGate` on the cell's graphic id (entity picks:
  exactly 512x640; decoration picks: whole multiples of 256 — an
  unreadable (0,0) scan entry fails every spec and hides), PLUS the
  decoration-layer rule: a layer pick must match the edited base's dims
  (the load-time invariant, same rule the Official tab's layer list
  already applied — a grid-conforming 768x768 file still hides against
  a 512x256 base).
- **The hidden note** — never a silent vanish: "N sprites hidden — <the
  kind's spec>" as a centered text label at the bottom of the picker
  panel (mission tab only; the Official tab never hides so it never
  notes). Shows alongside "No sprites" when everything was filtered, so
  an author whose PNG vanished sees WHY, not a broken scan.
- Tests: entity pick (conforming shown, wrong-dims + unreadable hidden,
  exact note text), decoration pick (non-multiple hidden), decoration
  layer add (base-dims mismatch hidden despite conforming grid), and
  the Official tab's no-note guarantee.

## Custom-asset dimensions — slice 4: pick-commit backstops + the Revalidate art report

The last layer — the editor can no longer mint spec-violating types, and
the publish checkpoint reports them. With this, every layer of the
custom-asset spec is enforced (load warn+degrade, render magenta gate,
picker filter, commit backstops, Revalidate report).

- **Pick-commit backstops** (input_handlers.zig, the picker filter's
  defense-in-depth — a stale scan or crafted input):
  - Entity base + layer picks: a custom stem must resolve to exactly the
    fixed 512x640 frame (`loaders.customEntitySpriteConforms`, wrapping
    the IHDR read + the types predicate) — otherwise the pick no-ops,
    nothing recorded (the load + render sides would degrade the same art
    anyway; committing it would only author a guaranteed-magenta type).
  - Decoration base picks (mission-local branch): the resolved dims must
    be whole 256px tiles (`types.decorationSpriteDimsConform` — subsumes
    the old positive-dims check).
  - Decoration layer picks were already fully backstopped (unresolvable +
    base-dims equality); its stale comment citing the removed load-time
    panic fixed.
- **The Revalidate art report** (`customSpriteSpecReport` in
  player_input.zig): at the publish checkpoint, the success message
  carries a violation list — every distinct custom sprite the editor's
  palette references (player def + entity types + decoration types, base +
  layers) that is missing/invalid or wrong-dims per its kind.
  Revalidation still PASSES (violations degrade to magenta at runtime) —
  the author certifies with eyes open, matching warn-not-reject
  everywhere else.
- **types.zig predicate split**: `entitySpriteDimsConform` +
  `decorationSpriteDimsConform` (the specs, callable without an id) with
  `customSpriteDimsPassGate` delegating to them — one fact, one place.
- `loaders.minimalPngHeader` went pub (the cross-file test-fixture
  helper; production never calls it). The footprint-editor open gate
  verified sound (grid derivation + 8x8 capacity check — a deliberate UI
  gate per the design, not a rejection); its stale TODO comment fixed.
- Tests: the wrong-dims entity pick no-ops (sprite unchanged, no undo
  step — the existing conforming pick test's fixture upgraded to a real
  512x640 IHDR PNG); the revalidate success message carries the spec
  report (missing sprite + non-conforming decoration listed) and the
  no-custom-art success carries none. Picker scroll remains a follow-up
  if real content ever overflows the picker's 6 columns.

## The editor browser — front door for all three editor kinds (tabbed window + main-menu entry)

The long-term goal is three editors (missions, hubs, campaigns — only the
mission editor exists). The editor front door is ONE tabbed modal, not a
chooser flow: the former mission browser (`buildEditorMissionBrowser`,
`Action.toggle_editor_mission_browser`, `UiState.editor_mission_browser_open`)
became the **editor browser** (`buildEditorBrowser`, `toggle_editor_browser`,
`editor_browser_open`).

- **Entry points.** The main-menu Editor button now toggles the browser
  (previously it fired `open_editor{null}` directly — a fresh mission; that
  menu_action path is deleted). From inside the editor: the options-menu
  Open Mission button + ctrl+O (unchanged), plus the window's own Back
  button. The toggle + New Mission consumption sites accept the editor +
  main-menu screens via `editorBrowserReachableScreen` (input_handlers.zig);
  every other screen no-ops (the save_editor_mission discipline). The
  keybinds ship editor-context, so on the main menu only the button path
  can fire them.
- **Binding rename self-heal.** Existing installs' settings.txt naming
  `toggle_editor_mission_browser` warn + drop at load (unknown action), and
  the renamed action's default ctrl+O binding applies — the same
  self-healing the deferred `toggle_options_menu` rename relies on.
- **Kind tabs.** New `types.EditorKind` (mission today; hub + campaign
  append when those editors land). The tab row derives from the enum at
  comptime (`editor_browser_kind_specs`); the two label switches
  (`editorBrowserKindLabel` tab label, `editorBrowserNewButtonLabel` New
  button) are exhaustive with no else-arm — a new kind is a compile error
  until named + routed. A kind appears as a tab only when its editor lands
  (no placeholder tabs for unbuilt editors).
- **One New button, derived from the active kind** ("New Mission" fires the
  same recorded `open_editor{null}` as ctrl+N) — chosen over a per-tab
  button set: buttons for content that isn't on screen would be dead
  buttons, and the derive-don't-duplicate discipline applies to UI too.
  From the main menu it opens the editor directly; the options-menu New
  Mission button stays (kept for now, possibly dropped later).
- **Per-kind content.** The mission list (Your Missions / Official tabs +
  rows + scrollbar) moved to `buildMissionBrowserContent` behind an
  exhaustive `switch (kind)` in the parent. Kind switch = direct UiState
  write (`editor_browser_kind`) + scroll reset, off the undo timeline
  (the list-tab convention).
- **Tests** (contract-shaped, derived expectations): the kind-tab test
  walks the same comptime spec list the builder walks (a new kind can't
  appear as a tab without appearing in the test); one-New-button derived
  label; the kind-switch handler case (write + scroll reset + closed-browser
  no-op); the browser toggle's main-menu open + non-reachable-screen no-op
  contract updated (was "editor-only no-op"); the new_editor_mission
  main-menu open added to its gate test.
- **Docs.** DESIGN → Level Editor → The editor browser rewritten for the
  tabbed window (entry points, kind derivation, single New button);
  fresh-mission paragraph re-anchored on the New buttons; the Escape
  overlay chain gained the (pre-existing but undocumented) browser entry;
  TODO → Level Editor gains the hub/campaign editor design-session item.

## Custom art carries on save — stem-namespace normalization + the referenced-art copy (the single-dir rule)

A spurious "custom sprite could not be resolved" warning on opening the
"miku test" mission exposed a model split: the load-side dims check read
`<loading-mission>/<file-stem>.png` (mission-relative), while the render
side read the stem's EMBEDDED namespace (`missions/<dir>/<file-stem>.png`
— assetPathFor, ids are self-describing). A mission renamed after
authoring kept stems naming the old dir — art rendered (old dir existed)
but the dims check warned against the new dir.

**Decision (settled):** custom art lives in the mission's OWN directory
and NOTHING resolves it elsewhere — the stem's dir component is identity
only. The rejected alternative (load-side resolves via the embedded
namespace too, matching the render side) was moot: the texture store has
no mission context, so "only the own dir" can only hold if the embedded
dir IS the own dir — which makes the SAVE the enforcement point:

- **Writer normalization** — `writeEditorMission` (now taking the save
  target's dir name) rewrites every `custom/<anything>/<file-stem>` to
  `custom/<uuid>_<name>/<file-stem>` in the written level files
  (normalizedCustomStem in writers.zig; non-custom + degenerate stems
  pass through). The in-memory Editor is untouched — the side effect
  stays replay-safe.
- **Referenced-art copy** — `copyReferencedCustomSprites` (mission_io.zig,
  step 3b of saveEditorMission) copies each referenced custom PNG (entity
  + decoration palette types, base + layers — referenced only, per
  decision) into the save target. Source: the mission's current dir
  first, then the stem's embedded namespace (the one-time migration
  read for pre-rename content; a missing source is skipped — it already
  warned at load). A copy write failure fails the save (the config-write
  class).
- Consequences: a renamed mission's re-save lands self-contained (old
  dir deletable, exports carry their art); a stem rewrite changes the
  content hash — Revalidate re-binds as usual. The in-session editor
  keeps old-namespace stems until reopen (renders fine; the next save
  normalizes again).
- Tests: the writer normalization contract (all four channels — entity
  base + layer, decoration base + layer — normalized, shipped stems
  untouched, stale namespace absent, unplaced types unwritten); the
  handler save contract (rename: art copied under the file stem into the
  new dir + the written level file carries the healed namespace).
- Docs: DESIGN → the save/export flow carries the rule; the Sprite id
  convention section now states the single-dir model once (both
  consumers + the save-enforced invariant), replacing the drifted
  "resolves from the mission directory being loaded" phrasing.

## Middle-panel reopen order — a reopened panel lands rightmost (bug fix)

`UiState.toggleMiddlePanel`'s open path used "fill the first empty slot",
but panels render left-flush in slot order (`buildMiddlePanels` skips nulls
and keeps relative order). Closing a middle panel leaves a hole at its old
slot, so reopening it while others stay open put it back in that hole —
LEFT of panels opened after it (open inventory → skills → close inventory →
reopen: inventory rendered left of skills). Only closing every panel reset
the slot assignment, which made open order look sticky.

Fix (the field's own doc comment said "ordered by open time" all along —
the implementation just didn't honor it on reopen):
- Open path: append after the last open panel (rightmost in display
  order). No-op when all four slots are open (same as before).
- Close path: compact the remaining panels down, so open slots are
  always a contiguous prefix — a reopened panel cannot recall its
  pre-close slot even indirectly.

Invariant now stated on the field: open panels occupy a contiguous prefix
of the slots, so slot order IS display order.

Tests: inline in `src/ui/state.zig` (the pure-fn tier) — open order =
display order, close compacts, reopen lands rightmost, closing the
rightmost panel leaves the prefix intact, and the full-strip edge cases
(fifth open ignored; a close+reopen at capacity never clobbers a slot).

## Global top bar tooltips — the hover pass ran before the bar existed (bug fix)

The options/undo/redo buttons carried tooltip headers the whole time
(`buildGlobalTopBar`), but no tooltip ever spawned for them. Root cause:
ORDERING in view()'s assembly. The hover-tooltip pass (`tooltipAt` →
`buildTooltip`) ran near the end of the assembly, but the global top bar is
emitted LAST (after it) — for click priority above modals — so the top-bar
buttons were never in the element list when the pass hit-tested the
pointer. Anything the pass couldn't see, it couldn't hover. The buttons'
tooltips have been dead since the global top bar landed (ec8f5dc), not
since the 128×128 shrink (a040c03) — the shrink is just when it was
noticed. (The hover-HIGHLIGHT pass runs after the top bar, which is why
button highlighting kept working and masked the difference.)

Not the icon: `emitIconButton`'s icon image is `blocks_input = false`
(passes hover through to the button beneath) — the layering was fine.

Fix: move the hover-tooltip pass to immediately after `buildGlobalTopBar`.
Consequences:
- Top-bar tooltips spawn (the fix).
- The pass now also sees the settings screen / editor browser / error
  popup (previously emitted after it). None of those carry tooltip-bearing
  elements, so nothing changes for them — and modal shielding is
  unchanged (`hitTest`'s blocks_input short-circuit still prevents a
  tooltip from an element behind a modal). The one tooltip that can draw
  over a modal is one spawned by the top bar itself, which sits above
  modals by design (click priority) — its tooltip belonging to the same
  layer is consistent.
- The old comment's "error popup stays above tooltips" invariant is
  restated precisely: no tooltip can bleed THROUGH a modal from behind;
  top-bar tooltips may sit above it, like their buttons do.

Test: full-`view()` contract test in view.zig — hovering each top-bar
cell center emits that button's tooltip header (Options/Undo/Redo at the
tooltip header font size), and the inter-button gap spawns none. Also
closed a facade gap found on the way: `top_bar_slot_size` was never
re-exported from `src/ui.zig`.

Sweep: the `Action` enum member + its doc comment (the "renaming awaits"

`applyAction`/`translateInput`/`checkAction` sites, the default binding in
