anytime-first comment, and the escape/editor test fixtures. The button-layer
sound path derives from `@tagName(action)` (audio.zig + sound_report.zig),
so the report follows automatically — no shipped asset is affected (no
button layers exist yet).

Docs: DESIGN → Escape overlay chain + the main-menu gating note renamed in
place; TODO item checked off. DONE.md's older entries keep the old name —
they are the archive of sessions where it was current.

## Diagnostics redesign — raylib-free type + the --diagnostics runtime flag (any build)

The settled redesign landed (DESIGN → Platform Seam → Diagnostics; the
original dev-gated shape's rationale is preserved in that section). Motivation
(why now): the rendering session landed four platform-seam changes with zero
automated coverage — src/raylib is headless-excluded by necessity — and the
structural answer to "verify the seam without being at the machine" is a flag
that works in the very binary that misbehaves.

The seam, as designed:
- `src/diagnostics.zig` (NEW, raylib-free — compiled + tested in the headless
  test build): the `Diagnostics` type = append buffer + section one-shot
  policy + flush scheduling. Plain-value structs (`BootValues`,
  `SpriteDrawValues`, `PanelDrawValues`, `PixelSample`) are the wire format
  across the seam; the type formats them and owns the file policy
  (whole-file rewrite of `logs/diagnostics.txt`).
- `src/raylib/diagnostics.zig` (hollowed out): the GL-gathering probe sites
  — `glGetString` identity reads, draw-state conversion, the render-target
  pixel sampling. All `rl.*` stays in the raylib dir; only values cross.
- Runtime activation replaces the comptime gate: `enabled` on the type,
  defaulted to dev-mode-native at backend init, OR-ed on by the
  `--diagnostics` CLI flag in native.zig (a new `parseBoolFlag`, the
  `--replay`/`--data-dir` pattern). The code ships in EVERY native build —
  verified: a ReleaseFast build with `--diagnostics` writes the log
  (boot + panel probe seen live), without the flag writes NOTHING (no
  logs dir at all). The dev build behaves as before (default active).
- Flush scheduling: sections only mark pending; `flushIfPending` runs at the
  END-OF-FRAME safe point — the last statement of `RaylibBackend.render`,
  after `endDrawing`/`swapScreenBuffer` (which came out of a `defer` so the
  flush can follow them) — plus at clean shutdown via `deinit`. The old
  system flushed immediately after each section, MID-DRAW on the probe
  path — exactly the observation-perturbs-the-observed-system failure the
  design calls out.
- Leak fix along the way: the audio subsystem's diagnostics sink used to
  append unconditionally into a never-flushed buffer in non-dev builds (a
  slow process-lifetime leak); `append` now self-gates on `enabled`, so an
  inactive instance accumulates nothing.

Tests (inline in src/diagnostics.zig, the file_source.zig scratch-dir
pattern): section one-shot policy (second boot with different values is a
no-op; probes stay one-shot after the readback), probe destination capture +
readback arming/consuming, whole-file-rewrite + pending-flag lifecycle
(stale file until the next flush — never mid-draw), and disabled = no buffer
growth + no file. The backend half stays headless-excluded (compile ≠ run:
the release/dev runtime checks above were manual, per the platform-seam
rule).

Docs: DESIGN → Platform Seam → Diagnostics flipped to the implemented shape;
AGENTS's two overlapping diagnostics entries consolidated into one (the old
"Dev diagnostics log" + "Diagnostics log" pair) + `src/diagnostics.zig` added
to Key Files; TODO item checked off.

## Options menu on the main menu — per-screen content + Exit Game (design reversal)

Reversal of a recorded decision (DESIGN previously held "options menu is
NOT reachable from the main menu"). The original exclusion existed because
the menu's content was session-only (Restart/Exit-Mission/Exit-to-Menu are
meaningless without a game in progress); the per-screen button lists
dissolved that reason, so the decision rule became: session-flow verbs +
mode entries stay on the main-menu stack, preferences and one-time views go
under Options.

Landed shape:
- **Main-menu stack:** Continue* / New Game / Load Save / Editor —
  Settings + Credits moved INTO the options menu. One convention from
  every screen: settings is always one step inside the menu.
- **Options menu, main-menu variant:** Settings / Credits / Exit Game. No
  session verbs, no Exit to Main Menu. Export Save
  is also hidden there (no game in progress; Load Save is that screen's
  workflow) — that gate previously excluded only the editor, and the new
  builder test caught the leak before runtime.
- **Exit Game:** native only (a browser tab is the user's to close, not
  ours — the web build omits the button and the handler's comptime os gate
  is the defensive half for a future keybind). New button-only
  `Action.exit_game`; the dispatch sets `SessionState.quit_requested` — a
  request, not a state transform (never recorded, off the undo timeline);
  the game loop's exit condition consumes it and the shutdown defers flush
  pending writes + diagnostics.
- **Entry point:** the top-bar options button, now emitted on EVERY screen
  (the unused `current_screen` parameter dropped). Escape opens the menu
  anywhere — the chain's final-branch main-menu no-op gate removed.
- **No Continue button in ANY options-menu variant** (a follow-up call the
  same session): the `.escape` action — Escape keybind + the top-bar
  options button toggle — is the close path everywhere; a Continue button
  would collide with resume-game meanings (the mission-complete overlay's
  Continue, the main-menu stack's Continue).
- **Routing consequence:** `.open_credits` moved from the idle
  `menu_action` path to the anytime `options_action` dispatch (idle input
  is gated while the options menu is open, so a Credits button inside it
  could never dispatch the old way — same reason Settings routes there).
  The credits Back button reuses the toggle.

Painter-order fix (caught in play, the session after landing): the
credits panel emitted inside the main-menu view branch — BEFORE the
screen-independent options-menu block — so with both up (credits opened
from the menu's Credits button), the full-screen options panel covered
the equally full-screen credits panel entirely: the flag was logically
open (Escape correctly closed credits first, per the chain), but nothing
rendered. The load-save browser had the same latent emission spot. Both
moved to AFTER the options-menu emission (still main-menu-gated); a
view-level regression test pins the order (options panel < Exit Game
button < credits panel).

Tests: escape opens + closes the options menu on the main menu (the old
no-op test reworked); the options_action dispatch drives the credits
toggle both ways and the Exit Game quit request; builder tests pin the
main-menu options-menu variant (meta entries present, session verbs +
editor block + Exit to Main Menu absent) and the slimmed main-menu stack
(Continue gated on continue_available; New Game/Load Save/Editor present;
Settings/Credits absent).

Docs: DESIGN → Escape overlay chain (arm 8 + the reachability section
rewritten as the reversal with its history note); AGENTS had no stale
references.

## Z-order census — the overlay ladder pinned; escape chain aligned to it

Session-end reflection flagged the recurring bug class: both user-caught
bugs this session (dead top-bar tooltips, credits covered by the options
menu) were overlay-emission ORDER bugs in view() — z-order knowledge lived
implicitly in one 4,300-line assembly function, and the escape chain's
"ordered to mirror the view's z-order" promise had drifted out of sync.

**Design first (settled, DESIGN → Modal overlays → the z-order ladder):**
the canonical emission order is now written down — base UI → drag ghost →
options menu → main-menu overlays (load-save browser, credits) →
mission-complete → mission-fail → settings screen → editor browser →
error popup → global top bar → hover tooltip → FPS label. The full-screen
overlays' RESERVED slot (below the options menu — nothing renders them
yet) is stated so buildWorldMap/buildFullCombatLog land in the right place.

**Two chain/emission mismatches found** (both between never-co-rendered
surfaces, so behavior-neutral): the chain claimed settings above browser
and fail above complete; emission says browser above settings and complete
above fail. Resolution principle: the chain's own doc comment promises it
mirrors the view — so the VIEW's emission is the spec, and the chain arms
were reordered (browser arm first, complete arm before fail). Zero
view() changes.

**The census test** (view.zig): two forced frames — every reachable
overlay flag set at once — asserting marker elements emit in ladder order
(marker = a distinctive button action per surface; LAST occurrence for
surfaces whose action also appears in a lower surface, e.g. the credits
panel's Back vs the options menu's Credits button). Frame 1 is the main
menu (options menu, load-save browser, credits, settings, editor browser,
error popup, top bar, tooltip, FPS); frame 2 is a dead-player level
(bottom bar, options menu, mission-fail, mission-complete, settings,
browser, error, top bar, FPS). A silent view() reorder OR a chain reorder
without the emission following now fails the suite. The two regression
tests from this session's bugs are subsumed as the census's pairwise
cousins (kept — they document their specific incidents).

Docs: DESIGN → Modal overlays gains the ladder section (with the
never-co-rendered ordering note + the reserved full-screen slot); DESIGN →
Escape overlay chain's arm list reordered to match; the chain code + its
arm comments now point at the census as the pinner.

## Startup settings repair write — stale settings.txt self-heals on launch

The popup-repeat bug: an install whose user settings.txt carries stale
entries (a renamed action's old name, an unknown key) saw the startup
warning popup EVERY launch, because the on-disk heal only happened via the
next debounced settings write — which only fires when the player changes a
tunable. In-memory the overlay already self-healed (warn + drop + inject
the default); the disk never learned.

Fix: when `overlayUserSettings` SUCCEEDS (the user file parsed + loaded)
but produces warnings, it sets a `repair_write_needed` out-param, appends a
reassurance line to the popup ("settings.txt was out of date; a repaired
copy is saved automatically (these settings warnings won't repeat)"), and
`createSessionSetup` marks settings dirty — the SAME debounced path as
preference changes, so the full-format write fires ~1s after boot (the
native defer + web beforeunload flushes cover a quick quit). Next launch:
no warnings.

Scoping (the deliberate non-writes):
- A user file that FAILED to parse or load sets NO repair flag — the overlay
  fell back to defaults, and rewriting would overwrite possibly
  hand-recoverable content. That warning deliberately repeats until the
  player fixes or deletes the file (data-loss guard, tested).
- Warnings from the other startup config files (themes, weapon types,
  salvage, shadow fallbacks) are unaffected — rewriting settings heals
  nothing there.

Structural note: `writeSettingsToFile` + `markSettingsDirty` moved from
`input_handlers.zig` to `state.zig` (next to the `PendingWrite` machinery
they serve) — `session_setup` is a leaf module and can't import
`input_handlers`; all callers already import state.

Drive-by fix (exposed by the new tests running the garbage-file path under
`testing.allocator` for the first time): `parseConfigFile` leaked the
working-list backing memory for content that never made it into a section
(pairs/groups before any header, or pending at EOF with no header open) —
invisible in the arena-wrapped parses. Now deinit'd before return.

Tests (session_setup.zig): stale-entries overlay sets the flag + injects
the renamed action's default + the heal write is idempotent (write →
re-overlay → zero warnings); invalid-user-file guard (no flag, broken file
left untouched on disk); the `createSessionSetup` wiring contract (fake
backend: the write is scheduled on `pending_writes`, fires past the 1s
debounce, and the rewritten file overlays warning-free). DESIGN → Input →
Binding overlay semantics + Error Handling → three contexts updated (the
old "no write-on-load" prose replaced by the repair-write rule).

## Keybind editor slice 1 — full W3C key table in input_poll

`shared_key_mappings` grew from the ~40 keys bound in
`data/default_settings.txt` to the FULL key set raylib can report (every
`KeyboardKey` member except the super keys, which stay mac-only and map to
the Control ids — the existing convention). Ids follow the W3C
KeyboardEvent.code names (KeyA–KeyZ, Digit0–9, BracketLeft, NumpadEnter,
BrowserBack, ...), matching the existing entries' convention. A binding —
authored in defaults or captured by the future rebind UI — can now name any
physical key with no backend edit; the backend key table is retired from
the new-keybind wiring sites (five → four, updated in DESIGN → Input).

Unbound-but-mapped keys reach `translateInput` and match nothing
(`checkAction` only matches bound inputs) — inert. Poll cost: one
`isKeyPressed` per table entry per frame (~110). `max_events_per_frame`
derives from the table length (formula, unchanged). A comptime uniqueness
guard (compile error on a duplicated key or id; the mac overlay excluded —
it intentionally reuses Control ids) catches copy-paste dupes at compile
time; the file is raylib-linked so it rides the native build, not the test
build.

TODO: keybind editor slice list added (4 slices; settled design recorded
there). Runtime verified on native + web (main menu loads).

## Keybind editor slice 2 — derived binding contexts + the one-combo-one-action rule

The settled design (agreed in session): a binding's active contexts are
DERIVED from `actionBindingContexts(action)` — the single, compiler-enforced
declaration — instead of authored per binding. `InputBinding.context` (the
field) is gone; the settings file KEEPS its `context` line as INFORMATIONAL
(writer emits `primaryBindingContext(action)` — first declared member of the
set; loader ignores the line; context-less entries parse fine). No
`file_format_version` bump: old files parse (lines ignored), new files keep
the line so an older binary still validates it.

Why derived: every one of the 44 shipped bindings already used a context
equal to its action's full valid set except one deliberate narrowing
(`toggle_editor_browser` — valid {editor, menu}, shipped editor-only). The
widening is the one behavior change: the editor-browser-family keys
(ctrl+O, ctrl+N, …) now fire on the MAIN MENU too — verified safe (both
consumption sites gate on `editorBrowserReachableScreen`, editor + main
menu). The old ctrl+N test asserted the narrowed behavior and was updated
to the derived behavior.

The conflict rule (agreed): one combo (same input + same required
modifiers) fires ONE action per context. Three layers:
1. **Engine**: `isSuppressed` gained the equal-specificity tiebreak — a
   same-combo equal-specificity DIFFERENT-action competitor appearing
   EARLIER in the binding list wins (first-match-wins, deterministic, keeps
   replay safe). Same-action earlier entries never suppress. Replaces the
   old "equal-specificity ties co-fire" rule (nothing shipped relied on
   co-fire — every same-combo pair in the defaults is cross-context).
2. **Load** (`loadSettings` conflict scan): same combo + different actions
   whose derived contexts INTERSECT (they would co-fire) → warn + drop the
   later entry (first listed wins). Same combo + same action → duplicate,
   warned + dropped. Cross-context same-combo pairs legal (kept silently).
   Warned files ride the startup repair write — the popup explains once,
   the file self-heals.
3. **UI** (slice 4, TODO): prevented at assignment (steal with warning).

Two bugs caught by tests during the slice:
- The competitor gate in `isSuppressed` was first written as
  `my_contexts.intersects(other_contexts)` — WRONG (two sets can share a
  context while one is inactive: {menu, game} vs {editor, menu} in-game).
  The correct gate is the old semantics restated: the competitor's derived
  contexts intersect the FRAME's active set. Compile error (unused param)
  flagged it before a silent behavior bug shipped.
- The conflict scan's injected-default case: a user rebinding that
  collides with an INJECTED default (user Enter→skip; confirm unmentioned
  → its default Enter injected) must drop the injected default SILENTLY —
  a warning would pop the same message EVERY launch (the injection
  re-runs every launch; the repair write can't remove it). Regression
  test pins the silence.

New helpers in types.zig: `BindingContextSet.intersects` (the derived gate
+ conflict predicate), `primaryBindingContext` (writer's informational
line), `rawInputsEqual` + `sameCombo` (combo identity, shared by the
loader scan and the future keybind UI). The load-time action↔context
validity layer was DELETED (nothing to validate — no binding can name a
context its action doesn't fire in); what remains per entry: unknown action
warn + drop. The 24 input.zig + 7 loaders.zig test fixtures lost their
`.context` fields (a sed sweep dry-run against ONE file, full diff
inspected, then the second — the AGENTS sweep discipline).

Tests: context-less/context-line entries load (rewritten from the dropped
validity tests); conflict warn+drop (first wins); duplicate warn+drop;
cross-context + modifier-distinguished combos kept silently;
injected-default collision silent; engine equal-specificity conflict
first-match-wins; same-action duplicates both fire. Docs: DESIGN → Input —
Binding contexts (derived), Action↔context classification, Hybrid
precedence (+ the new binding-conflicts bullet), Binding overlay semantics;
TODO friction item updated (backend key table + context line no longer
wiring sites). Runtime verified native + web (main menu loads).

## Keybind editor slice 3 — the Keybinds tab (read-only) + two-column Settings

The settings screen gained content tabs (Settings / Keybinds —
`UiState.settings_tab`, tab buttons under the header,
`.select_settings_tab` + `clicked_settings_tab` payload through the
options_action dispatch; a switch resets the keybind scroll, the
browser-tab convention). Escape still closes the overlay from either tab.

**The Keybinds tab** (read-only — editing is slice 4): bindings sorted by
action (declaration order, stable so an action's combos keep file order),
one group header per action + one row per binding — modifier/key 9-slice
panels ("+" between; `keyIdDisplayLabel` prettifies ids: Ctrl/Shift/Alt,
KeyZ→Z, Digit1→1, left→LMB) and the action panel at a fixed column,
labeled "Action — Contexts" with the DERIVED context set. Scroll is the
game-wide row-scroll convention (`keybind_scroll_offset` = first visible
row, one notch = one row, lower clamp at the input site, upper clamp
authoritative in the builder).

Display labels are comptime-generated (`actionDisplayLabel` /
`contextSetDisplayLabel`) so new Action members + context-set shapes label
themselves. Lesson worth keeping: comptime labels must be built by STRING
CONCATENATION (each `++` produces a compiler constant) — comptime-var
buffers copied into a table do NOT materialize into the binary and arrive
as scratch garbage at runtime (caught by a label-dump probe; the
concatenation form is the StaticStringMap mechanism).

**The Settings tab went two-column** (6 rows per column,
`settingsControlRowRect`): a new layout-fit test exposed that a single
12-row column needs 1792px where the region between the tab row and the
Back button has ~1610 — the last row would overlap the Back button, and
would have even BEFORE the tab row (the shipped screen's Show FPS row was
already kissing the Back button). Two columns fit with margin and use the
3840-wide reference screen properly. The fit is pinned by a test (lowest
control bottom clears the Back button top).

Tests: tab row + active highlight on both tabs; the settings tab keeps
its controls + fits; the keybinds tab groups (one header per action, both
combos), emits key panels + "+" + prettified labels + "Action — Contexts"
labels; scroll window + clamp (short list resets to 0, overflow clamps to
the last full window, same window size at every offset, negative clamps
to 0). Docs: DESIGN → UI Framework → Settings screen rewritten for the
tabs + both layouts. Runtime verified native + web.

## Dead-binding advisory — the missing-Escape class pinned shut

The missing-Escape regression (the full-table rewrite dropped the escape
row; Escape silently did nothing everywhere — see the fix commit) exposed
the open TODO item's failure mode concretely: a binding naming an input id
no platform table can produce is silently dead, and NOTHING could catch
it — the poll is raylib-linked (invisible to the headless test build) and
the uniqueness guard checks duplicates only, not missing rows.

The fix, both directions:
- **`types.producible_key_ids` / `producible_mouse_ids`** — the ids the
  backend tables can produce, declared in raylib-free code (types.zig —
  loaders can't import input.zig: input imports ui, ui imports loaders;
  types is imported by all three sites). The initial lists were GENERATED
  from the tables (machine-walked, not hand-copied).
- **A comptime lockstep guard in input_poll** — the key + mouse tables and
  the lists must name exactly the same ids, both directions (a table id
  missing from the list = the loader would warn a real binding as dead; a
  list entry with no table row = the loader accepts a binding nothing can
  produce). Verified by pulling Escape from the list: the native build
  fails with "key table id missing from types.producible_key_ids: Escape"
  — the exact regression, now a compile error.
- **A load-time advisory warn** (`loadSettings`, user-file warnings path):
  a binding naming an unproducible id warns ("...names input id 'Escapee'
  no platform mapping can produce; the binding can never fire") and is
  KEPT — the id may be valid on another platform or a future table, and
  dropping would lose the entry. The startup popup deliberately repeats
  until the file names a producible id. Gamepad ids warn until a gamepad
  table lands (per-variant check: a KEY binding naming "left" is dead
  even though the mouse table produces "left").

Tests: `inputIdProducible` per-variant contract (W3C ids producible, typo
not, mouse ids as mouse only, no gamepad yet); the loader warn keeps the
entry + names the id + the failure mode. TODO: friction item checked off
(both halves done).

## Keybinds tab follow-ups — no group headers + the wheel-before-gate fix

Two changes from playtesting the read-only keybinds tab:

**No group headers.** The action name rides in every row's action panel
("Undo — Anytime"), so the per-action header rows were pure duplication —
removed. The list is one row per binding, still sorted by action
(declaration order, stable) so an action's multiple combos sit adjacent.
The `KeybindRow` union (header/binding rows) went with them — the builder
iterates the sorted bindings directly.

**The wheel-before-the-gate fix.** Slice 3's wheel routing lived in the
scroll chain AFTER the options-menu gate — but the settings screen opens
ON TOP of the options menu in-game (the menu stays open underneath), so
the gate's `return` ate the wheel before it ever reached the keybinds
branch: scrolling worked over the main menu and was dead in-game. The
routing moved BEFORE the gate (the slider-drag-before-the-gate pattern in
main's frame); DESIGN → UI Framework → Settings screen notes the placement
rule.

Tests: the headerless shape is pinned (no exact-action-name label exists
— the spelling only appears inside "Action — Contexts" labels); the
existing scroll window/clamp tests carry over unchanged (rows are now
just bindings).

## Editor actions are editor-only — the actionBindingContexts fallthrough fix

Playtesting the keybinds tab surfaced it: EVERY editor action displayed
"Editor + Menu". Root cause: a pre-existing fallthrough bug in
`actionBindingContexts` — the ~54 editor-screen actions (save_editor_mission
through select_editor_all) never got their own arm and fell through into the
editor-browser family's `=> .{ .editor = true, .menu = true }`, with the
browser comment sitting INSIDE the prong list making it look like two
groups. Latent while contexts were authored (the set was only the
load-time validity set; the bindings' own "context editor" lines gated) —
slice 2's derived contexts made the set the real gate, slice 3's tab
displayed it.

The fix (agreed): EVERY editor action is EDITOR-ONLY for keys — the big
group, the browser family (ctrl+O/ctrl+N — narrowed from the slice-2
widening), and the tool-shortcut group now share one
`=> .{ .editor = true }` arm. The browser still OPENS from the main menu via
its BUTTONS (clicks bypass the context gate; the
`editorBrowserReachableScreen` handler gates stay for those) — a main-menu
surface has no editor semantics for the shortcuts.

Behavior on the main menu was already nil for the big group (consumption
sites gate on editor presence / screen == .editor — verified), and the
browser family's menu fires are gone with the classification. The conflict
rule gets correctly more permissive: editor-screen actions + menu actions
sharing a combo are legal cross-context pairs now, not phantom conflicts via
the menu member.

Tests: the ctrl+N dispatch pin reverted to editor-only (editor fires, menu
+ level/hub don't); the keybinds tab label test expects "Select editor
tool — Editor". The `{editor, menu}` set is now unused (no action carries
it) — `contextSetDisplayLabel` handles any subset generically for when a
future action genuinely needs it.

## Keybind editor slice 4 — the editing flows (listening → pending, picker, add/remove/reset)

The Keybinds tab became the full rebinding UI (the settled design from the
TODO → Keybind editor item):

- **Listening**: a row's combo area starts a rekey — the row swaps to a
  highlighted "Press a key… (Esc to cancel)" panel. The capture seam is the
  text-input model: while ANY edit is active (`UiState.keybind_edit` — the
  new `ui/keybind_edit.zig` state machine), `translateInput` suppresses ALL
  binding translation and routes raw presses into the edit. The first
  non-modifier key or mouse press captures (a click anywhere binds the
  clicked mouse button); the held modifiers become the combo's requirements;
  Escape cancels at every phase. Resolved once per frame in `main.frame`.
- **Pending**: the proposal row shows the captured combo + Confirm/Cancel
  buttons + the steal warning (warn color): "This combo currently fires
  Undo (game) — confirming will remove it" / "...is already bound to Undo —
  confirming removes the duplicate". Confirm applies: rebuild
  `settings.input_bindings` (replace/append + REMOVE the stolen entry —
  first-listed-wins, the edited row wins) + `markSettingsDirty`.
- **Picker**: a row's action panel (or the standalone Add button) opens the
  right-column action picker — the full scrollable action list on the tab's
  right half; picking moves the row's combo to it (reassign → pending) or
  starts the standalone add's listening. The wheel scrolls the picker while
  open. X removes directly (no confirm); Reset re-loads the embedded
  defaults' bindings (the safety net).
- The whole UI rides ONE action (`.edit_keybind`) + the `KeybindCommand`
  payload union — one Action enum member + one button/anytime payload field
  covers all nine commands, instead of nine actions.

**A real slice-2 bug caught by the slice-4 steal test**: the conflict
predicate used plain set intersection — but {anytime} ∩ {game} is empty
while both are simultaneously active in-game (anytime rides along), so an
anytime+game same-combo pair slipped through BOTH the loader's conflict
scan and the UI's steal scan. Fixed with `types.bindingContextsCoFire`
(the activation model: one of game/editor/menu + anytime riding; the modal
error_popup alone) used at both predicate sites. The engine's runtime gate
was always correct (it tests the frame's actual active set).

Tests: the capture seam (captures + held modifiers, modifier-only never
captures, Escape at every phase, mouse capture, translation suppressed —
via translateInput); the steal scan (co-firing steal, excluded row, same-
action duplicate, cross-context legal); the interactive chrome (per-row
rekey/reassign/X/+ buttons + the standalone Add + the min-width contract).
FOLLOW-UP (TODO): an end-to-end harness test for the apply/remove rebuild
ownership path.

## Keybind pending: Enter confirms (the modal-capture-state convention)

Agreed convention (the Enter-as-confirm discussion): **while a modal state
owns the keyboard, Escape cancels, Enter triggers the primary action** —
and the rule lives in each state's input seam, not a global mechanism (one
consumer today; the shared flag gets extracted when a second seam-driven
confirmable surface appears — the same call as B-simple).

Implementation: `routeKeybindCapture` returns `.confirmed` for an Enter
press during the PENDING phase → `resolveKeybindCaptureOutcome` applies.
The obvious worry — Enter often being the key being rebound TO — is not
ambiguous by phase separation: capture happens during LISTENING, so by
PENDING an Enter press can only mean confirm (and during LISTENING Enter
is an ordinary capturable key). Tests pin both directions.

Docs: the convention bullet lives in DESIGN → Input (where a new modal
state's builder will find it); the Settings screen's pending paragraph
points at it.

## Console input slice 1 — src/console.zig (parser, SPSC queue, merge, action fold, dumps)

The scripted/TAS stdin channel's raylib-free core (settled design:
DESIGN → Input → Console input; slice 2 — the native reader thread + stdout
writer wiring — is next).

- `ConsoleCommand` union over the full vocabulary
  (press/release/move/scroll/type/action/wait/dump/quit); payloads are
  fixed-buffer bounded strings (`BoundedText`), so parse→queue→merge
  allocates nothing — the only allocations are the drain-time frame-arena
  dupes on the game thread.
- Parser: exact-match verbs/ids/actions/dump kinds; unknown input ids error
  with the dead-binding advisory's message shape; blank lines + `#` comments
  skip (scripts are annotatable); `type`'s payload is the rest of the line
  verbatim (the verb split consumed exactly one separator, so a doubled
  space types a leading space).
- The queue is a single-producer single-consumer ring with atomic
  monotonic counters — NOT a mutex. Zig 0.16 removed the self-contained
  `std.Thread.Mutex`: std locks (`std.Io.Mutex`/`Condition`) need an `Io`
  handle on BOTH threads, and the game thread has none inside `frame()`.
  An SPSC ring needs none. Full-queue backpressure is a yield-spin in the
  reader (a piped script faster than the drain can never drop or reorder
  commands; the reader paces the game).
- `applyFrameCommand` (frame()'s drain, called right after the backend
  poll): input commands merge into the frame's `PlatformInput` (string
  payloads duped into the frame arena — queue slots are reusable
  reader-thread memory, so merged events must not alias them); `quit` sets
  `session.quit_requested`; `dump` writes via `writeDumpText`. The action
  fold (`foldInjectedActions`, called right after `translateInput`) runs
  `applyAction` — the same call the button path uses, with KEYBIND firing
  cadence (see DESIGN for the pressed_button-guard difference).
- `PlatformInput` gained `actions: []const types.Action = &.{}` — the
  semantic-action seam the console merge fills; empty for every hardware
  frame. `FrameState` gained the `console_queue` (empty/no-op without a
  reader — web).
- Dump output is stored as the concrete `std.Io.File.Writer` PARENT, not
  the interface: the vtable resolves the parent via `fieldParentPtr`, so an
  interface copy would dangle (a segfault the first test iteration caught).
- Dumps: state (screen/world/stack/history/waiting/entities), ui (overlay
  flags, scroll offsets, tile cursor, camera pan), settings (the writer's
  own full-file text), bindings (one line per binding, count derived from
  the same list), history (the session-log body via `writeEventLog`).
- Tests: console.zig inline tests (parser table incl. every error message,
  queue roundtrip + wait pacing, merge correctness + the arena-ownership
  pin, action fold, dumps, `writeDumpText` through an Allocating writer
  passed by real parent pointer) + `src/input_tests_console.zig`
  (handler-level pins: `press Escape` closes the options menu end-to-end
  through merge → translateInput → handleAnytimeInput; `scroll 1` with the
  options menu + keybinds tab open moves `keybind_scroll_offset`;
  `action escape` via the fold; chords across frames via held-state
  persistence; release completes the held model; quit).

Two design wrinkles settled before code (recorded in DESIGN): the per-frame
drain lives in the shared `frame()` (the poll happens inside it, and the
action fold needs the frame's PlayerInput there) — native-only in effect
because only native spawns a reader; and the action cadence is keybind
semantics (per-update-call through the drain), not the button path's
once-per-frame guard — identical to a real key edge, deterministic either
way.

## Console input slice 2 — native wiring (reader thread + stdout dumps)

The console channel's native side (settled design: DESIGN → Input → Console
input; slice 1 — the raylib-free core — is the previous entry).

- `native.main` wires the queue's dump output FIRST (the main thread's Io —
  dumps are written from `frame()`, so the writer belongs to the main
  thread's Io + the queue's own 4096-byte buffer), then spawns the reader
  thread. Always on, no flag. Spawn failure warns on stderr and the game
  runs without the console.
- `consoleReaderThread`: its OWN `std.Io.Threaded` (an Io handle is not
  shared across threads; libc malloc backs it), a 4096-byte read buffer,
  `File.stdin().reader(...).interface.takeDelimiter('\n')` for lines (null
  on EOF), `parseCommandLine` per line — skip skips, command pushes, err
  reports on stderr. EOF / read error / oversized line exits the thread
  (an stdin-less launch — double-click, the mac app bundle — is immediate
  EOF, zero cost). Detached, never joined: a quit while blocked on stdin
  leaves the thread to die with the process — joining would hang the exit
  waiting for input that never comes.
- **The wasm32 counter fix**: wasm32 rejects 64-bit atomics
  (`std/atomic.zig: expected 32-bit integer type or smaller`), so the SPSC
  ring's counters are u32 with wrapping arithmetic (`-%` / `+%`). Wrap-safe:
  the ring's invariant is the occupied count (`write_counter -%
  read_counter`), which stays correct across counter wraparound because the
  capacity (64) is far below 2^32 — the classic ring-counter trick.
- **The by-value-self dangling-slice bug (caught by the runtime smoke, not
  the suite)**: `ParseOutcome.errorMessage` originally took `self` by
  value, so the returned `.err.view()` pointed into errorMessage's own
  dead stack frame — the subsequent `std.debug.print` read a frame that
  print's own call machinery was concurrently reusing, producing
  DETERMINISTIC mangled stderr (message fragments interleaved with print's
  stack pointers). The headless suite passed the same path (the outcome
  lived in a live caller frame there) — same bug class as the
  `inputEventFor` by-value id fixed in slice 1: any function returning a
  `.view()` slice must take the owner by POINTER. Rule of thumb for
  `BoundedText`: views are only as alive as the caller's copy.
- **Script edge discipline (verified live)**: a second `press` of a key
  that was never `release`d produces NO edge — held-state persistence means
  the key is (synthetically) held, exactly like a physical key held down.
  Scripts that need repeated presses must press/release per press. This is
  by design (chords across frames depend on it), not a bug.
- Runtime checks (native, piped): `dump state/ui/bindings/history` to
  stdout (bindings listing derived from the same list the picker iterates;
  history = the session-log body); parse errors on stderr clean;
  `press Escape`/`release Escape` open then close the options menu (dump
  ui before/after); `quit` exits 0; `< /dev/null` runs until killed (EOF
  path); web build compiles (WEB OK).

Follow-up candidate: a real TAS fixture script (menu click-through via
`move` + `press left`, a level start, `dump history` → a `--replay`
fixture) once there's a need for one — the machinery is in place.

## Console input — pointer-position persistence (the `move` overwrite bug)

Found by live smoke minutes after slice 2 landed: a scripted `move` + 
`press left` clicked NOTHING — the press frame hit-tested the HARDWARE
mouse position (reference-mapped), not the scripted one. Root cause: the
native backend emits a `mouse_move` event EVERY frame unconditionally
(it always pushes the current position — the behavior translateInput's
own `mouse_moved_this_tick` change-detection already works around), so a
console `move` position set on its own frame was overwritten by the next
frame's hardware report before any subsequent command landed. Held keys
persist across frames; the pointer position did not.

Fix (the held-key model applied to the pointer): the queue remembers
`pointer_position` (set by `move`, persists until the next `move` — the
console's pointer is where the console left it), and every INPUT-command
frame re-applies it as a `mouse_move` event appended AFTER the backend's
events (last writer wins within the frame), ahead of the command's own
events. Deliberately NOT a sticky override that hardware must fight: only
command frames re-apply, so frames between commands — and everything
after script EOF — stay on the hardware position; a human at the window
never loses the pointer. `dump`/`quit` frames do not re-apply (dumps stay
pure projections — no pointer perturbation).

Also the answer to "which space does `move` use": reference space,
end to end — the backend maps the hardware pointer through the letterbox
inverse into reference space at the poll and reports the viewport as the
reference dims, so a script computes coordinates once against the
reference layout (3840×2160) and they click the same buttons at any
window size / render resolution. DESIGN → Input → Console input now
carries both facts.

The handler-level pin (`input_tests_console.zig`): runConsoleScript
simulates the backend's unconditional per-frame hardware `mouse_move`
(the behavior that causes the overwrite) and asserts the press frame
acts at the scripted position while a no-command frame stays on the
hardware one. The harness needed ONE queue across the whole script (the
live queue lives on FrameState; a fresh queue per line would drop the
remembered position). Live-verified: `move 1920 1256` + `press left`/
`release left` clicks the main menu's Load Save button (fresh data dir,
3-button layout, button center at reference (1920, 1256)) with the
hardware mouse resting elsewhere.

## Console input — the ui dump's interactive-surface listing

The `dump ui` extension that makes scripts self-documenting: alongside the
overlay flags, the dump lists the LAST-RENDERED interactive surfaces
(`previous_view_state.ui_elements` — the exact list the press/release
dispatch hit-tests against), each with its rect and its CENTER — a valid
click point, reference space, so a coordinate from the dump clicks the
same surface at any window size / render resolution. Button lines carry
the action name (the same enum `action <name>` accepts), sliders their
setting + value + range, text fields their current text, ref-bearing slots
their drag identity.

Seam: `applyFrameCommand` (and the writeDump → dumpText → dumpUiText
chain) gained the `ui_elements` param — frame() passes
`previous_view_state.ui_elements` (empty before the first render). The
interactive listing lives in the projection (pure over the element
list), unit-tested with hand-built elements; live-verified with the
self-documenting loop: `dump ui` → read `button ... center 1920 1256
action toggle_load_save_menu` → `move 1920 1256` + press/release → the
browser opens, and a follow-up `dump ui` lists the newly opened
browser's own Back button.

## Console input — the level dump (the active world, gameplay-decidable)

The dump that makes the console a full gameplay channel (agreed follow-up to
the ui dump): `dump level` lists the ACTIVE WORLD — level or hub.

- Level: name, turn_phase, tile count, the level-end flag, prepared skill,
  the phase's `highlighted_tiles` (the game's own computed legal targets —
  a script never reasons about legality, it clicks a highlight), entities
  (name / team / tile / health / aggro), and the player's utility skill
  slots + cooldowns (ready / cooldown N / none).
- Hub: name, player + NPCs, and the mission exits (mission id + tile) —
  the click targets that start missions.
- Every tile line carries its CENTER — a click point projected through
  the frame's LIVE camera via the new `view.tileClickCenter` (tile center
  through `tileToScreen`; the inverse of `screenToTile`, so a coordinate
  straight off a dump line resolves back to its tile — pinned as a
  round-trip in the projection test).
- Seam decision (agreed option a): the console drain in frame() moved to
  AFTER the camera computation (the camera depends only on state + zoom +
  pan, not on input), and `applyFrameCommand` (+ the writeDump → dumpText
  → dumpLevelText chain) takes the camera + zoom. Alternative rejected:
  scripts replicating computeCamera/tileToScreen themselves — duplicates
  the math, rots on camera changes.
- Projection test: a harness level with entities/skills/highlights/flag
  asserts the exact lines (centers derived via the same helper), the
  click-center round-trip through `screenToTile`, and the no-world case.
- Live-verified as a MINI RUN: `dump ui` → click New Game (center off the
  dump) → hub dump (mission exits with centers) → click the "beginnings"
  exit → level dump ("Beginnings 0": 4 move highlights, 4 entities, skill
  bar) → click a highlight center → the player moved (0,0)→(1,0), the
  turn cycled (no aggro'd enemies → straight turn_end → fresh
  player_move highlights). The full loop — dump, decide, click, verify —
  works end to end with zero knowledge beyond the dumps.

## Console input — wait idle (turn-flow pacing)

`wait idle`: hold commands until the game is idle — stack empty, no wait,
no modal error, the SAME condition under which the game accepts player
input (the frame's own idle gate, computed in applyFrameCommand) — then
release the next command on that first idle frame. The pacing primitive
for scripted turn flow: enemy turns drain over real-clock wait timers, and
a `wait <n>` frame count is a guess that either wastes time or races the
drain; `wait idle` is exact by construction. A new `.wait_idle` command
kind (parser: `wait idle`); popped like `wait n` (consumed inside
takeFrameCommand, arms a `wait_until_idle` hold). Note: a stall means the
game never idled — itself a bug worth noticing; the human at the window
still controls everything.

Tests: parser case, queue hold/release (held on busy frames, released on
the first idle frame, hold cleared after), and an applyFrameCommand pin
against a real harness history (quit behind the hold never fires while
the startup batch is pending; runToIdle → the next frame releases it).

## Console input — the agent live run (slice 3: an AI plays the game)

The agreed curiosity run: the agent (glm) drove a full gameplay session
entirely through the console channel — every decision made from dump
output alone (no screenshots; this model cannot read images).

Method: a fifo keeps the game's stdin open across the agent's tool calls
(a `sleep` holder prevents EOF between command writes); commands written
as observed, output file read per step — a genuinely interactive session,
not a pre-scripted blind run.

The session: boot → `dump ui` (New Game center) → click → hub → `dump
level` (mission exits with centers) → click "beginnings" → level "Beginnings
0" (4 skeletons... 3 skeletons, skill bar, flag) → walked toward the
nearest skeleton (aggro at chebyshev 3) → slice prepared via `press
Digit1` (no target at range 2 — sword needs adjacency) → skip attack →
enemy turn drained under `wait idle` (real-clock waits held exactly) →
approach → two skeletons adjacent → retaliated down to 8/20 → replenish
(`press Digit4`, heal to full, cooldown 5 visible in the dump) → slice
landed twice — one discovery: `press Digit1` with the pointer resting on
a skeleton's tile fired slice INSTANTLY (auto-target-at-cursor — the
first slice needed no explicit target click) → walked into a 2v1 anyway →
died at 0/20 → mission-fail overlay (its restart/exit buttons were in the
`dump ui` listing — Exit Mission clickable at center 1920 1168) → pressed
Escape (≡ clicking Exit Mission) → back in the hub, 194 recorded events →
`ctrl+L` wrote the session log → `quit`.

The full-circle proof: `--data-dir <dir> --replay <session-log>` on the
console session's log reconstructed EXACTLY (hub, 194 events, 17 idle
points, world_generation 3 — replay-verification passed silently). The
design's promise — console sessions are ordinary sessions and their logs
are valid --replay fixtures — holds end to end.

Fixes that fell out of the run: the level dump's skill section originally
printed only `equipped_utility_skills` (slots 4-8); it now prints the FULL
8-slot bar via `collectSkillSlots` (weapon skills 1-3 included — slice was
invisible before). DESIGN amended.

Playtest finding (genuine, from a fresh player's run): "Beginnings 0"
with the starter loadout — two skeletons adjacent deal ~12/turn while the
starter sword's slice deals ~4-5/turn and replenish is a 5-turn cooldown;
a fresh player who walks into the 2v1 (both skeletons converge once one

at a time — the skeletons' approach was slow enough to kite), but the

## Console input — the second agent run (equip, undo-refinement, corridor war)

The user-invited return match on "Beginnings 0" from a fresh save, with two
new tools in play: inventory/equipping (the user's reminder) and undo/redo
as a strategy-refinement instrument. The mission was NOT completed — the
run ended mid-fight (11hp flanked in the corridor, reflect one tick out) —
but the difficulty the user likes held up against full game knowledge +
meta-tools, which is itself the finding.

What the run surfaced (each verified against source or the event log):

- **The drag-to-equip swap semantics**: dragging inventory/0 (Comfortable
  Boots) onto gear/boots recorded `player_equip_to_gear` and executed —
  the OLD Starter Boots survive into the inventory (the user's hint after
  my misread; the ui dump's item line proved the swap, the history's
  event 36-37 proved the drag had fired all along — my grep pattern
  matched the count line but not the item line).
- **Slot identity payloads**: the ui dump's slot lines now carry their
  payload (`gear/boots`, `inventory/0`, `skill_bar/3`) — the tag alone
  cannot distinguish same-kind slots, which drag targeting needs.
- **Auto-pickup**: walking onto a ground stack transfers it (no click); the
  level dump's ground/inventory sections drove it blind-free.
- **Momentum** (the user's reminder): every skill use — attacks AND
  cantrips — adds +1 momentum; the damage modifier is floor(log2(momentum)).
  Explains slice hitting 5 against the weapon's base 3, and the
  skeletons' hits ramping (one exchange cost 13, not the budgeted 10).
- **Enemy AI behavior pinned empirically**: enemies attack in the SAME
  turn they close into adjacency (a kited distance-2 end is not safe vs a
  2-speed chaser); they hold attack range WITHOUT moving when already in
  range (skel3 guarding the choke tile unmoved); and OCCUPIED TILES BLOCK
  PATHFINDING — a skeleton on a 1-wide corridor tile is a door (the
  flag's only route ran through (10,2), so the guard had to be killed or
  lured off).
- **Undo as strategy refinement, actually used**: when the pocket
  slugfest math turned lethal (13-damage exchange vs the budgeted 10,
  spinblade on cooldown), a 3-action rewind (each recorded player action —
  move, skip, use_skill — is an idle point, finer than per-turn) restored
  the pre-commit state, and the replan (reflect bait) ran from there.
  Redo stayed available but was never needed — deterministic replays of
  the same line.
- **The identified winning line** (for the next attempt): the reflect-bait
  rotation — heal, step to distance 2-3, cast reflect, let both chasers
  close into their own damage (verified twice: both hit themselves for
  zero cost to me), rotate replenish/reflect cooldowns while kiting at
  end-distance ≥3 from the speed-1 guard and ≥4 from the speed-2 chaser,
  kill the chaser, lure the guard off the choke tile, circle around, and
  the final dash onto the flag from (9,3) — chebyshev 2, in speed-2 reach
  (the level-end check fires before any enemy turn). The run died
  executing exactly this — at 11hp with reflect one tick late; the line
  is sound, the execution window was one turn short.
- **Speed misread, caught in review** (the user's question): the run logs
  and narrative here repeatedly said "speed 2→3" after equipping the
  Comfortable Boots — wrong. The player's base speed is 1 (no `speed`
  line in the mission's player.txt → the Entity default), Starter Boots
  have speed bonus 0, Comfortable Boots +1 → effective 1→2
  (`getEffectiveSpeed`). The error came from counting HIGHLIGHT LIST SIZE
  at (1,-1) in run 1 ((2,-2) was misread as a 2-step tile — chebyshev 1,
  a diagonal 1-step neighbor) and never re-deriving it; the direct
  observable was in every dump all along — pre-boots every move was
  exactly 1 tile, post-boots exactly 2, never 3. Lesson applied: derive
  claims from moves-per-turn (or `getEffectiveSpeed`), not highlight
  counts (sparse grids make ring-counting unreliable). The recorded
  winning line above had a downstream casualty of the same error — the
  final dash was originally written from (8,3) (chebyshev 3 to the flag,
  NOT reachable at speed 2); corrected to (9,3).
- One honestly-unexplained observation: skel2 was once seen closing
  (4,-2)→(5,0) — chebyshev 2 — in what appeared to be one enemy turn,
  while the level data says `speed 1`. Possibly a stale dump read on my
  end (I had those earlier), or a movement-mode behavior — unverified,
  worth checking against `ai_movement` before the next attempt.

Session hygiene: the fifo + sleep-holder session pattern, quit + cleanup,
and the whole second run's recorded history remains a valid --replay
fixture by construction (the first run's log was replay-verified).

## Editor select tool: drag-to-select-and-move (one gesture instead of click-then-drag)

The select tool previously required click-then-drag: a plain left press only
claimed the move drag when the press tile already hit the selection
(`editorSelectionContainsPosition`), so moving an unselected thing needed a
click (replace) followed by a second press-and-drag. Now a press on an
unselected-but-selectable thing (a nonempty click group —
`planning.editorClickGroupNonempty`, a thin wrapper over `editorClickGroup`
so the claim condition and click semantics share one source of truth) claims
the same drag: dragging it selects it and moves it in one gesture. Empty
ground still never claims — the click-to-deselect and a drag from empty
ground are unchanged.

The design decision that shaped the implementation is WHEN the select
fires. Firing the replace at press/promotion (making the selection real
during the drag, so the existing translated-outline render works untouched)
was rejected: the move pushed at release lands ON TOP of the replace's
still-draining sub-batch and pops first under LIFO — planning against a
selection that doesn't contain the dragged thing — and the leftover
`editor_select` events then land on placement indices the move just
shifted. The window is narrow (the drain loop empties a small stack within
a frame) but the failure mode is silent (a fast flick either no-ops the
move or moves the wrong things). Instead the release fires BOTH existing
actions, pushed in drain-correct order: `player_move_editor_selection`
first, `player_replace_editor_selection` on top — the LIFO drain runs the
replace's whole sub-batch (selects the grabbed group) before the move
orchestrator plans its clear phase + chained commit against the REPLACED
selection. The ordering is guaranteed by push order, not by drain timing.
Both orchestrators carry pure position/delta payloads and plan at drain
time, so replay-safety is inherited for free.

Because idle points are recorded when the stack EMPTIES (not per action),
the pair drains together and shares one idle point — a single undo step
reverts the whole drag, one fewer than the click-then-drag it replaces.
A zero-delta drop fires just the replace (grab-and-drop-in-place = the
thing ends up selected, like a click); an empty replace plan (reachable
only via a mid-drag selection change such as ctrl+A) skips the replace
and still moves.

Files:
- `src/editor/planning.zig` — `editorClickGroupNonempty` (pub for the
  `input_gestures.zig` import only).
- `src/ui/state.zig` — `EditorMoveDrag.selected_at_press`, recorded at
  press so a mid-drag selection change can't flip a claim's semantics.
- `src/input_gestures.zig` — `handleEditorMoveDrag`: the widened claim +
  the release's pair-push arm.
- `src/view.zig` — the unselected-claim preview: while such a drag is
  promoted, the grabbed click group's outline renders translated by the
  live delta (`buildEditorMoveDragOverlay` over the new
  `appendEditorClickGroupOutline`, also adopted by the cursor overlay's
  select arm — the hover-preview shape, now shared), and the OLD
  selection's outlines stay put (it is still the real selection). The
  decoration case anchors the footprint region at `placement.position +
  delta`; the plain-tile case lands at the current pointer tile.
- `src/input_handlers.zig` — the gesture test rewritten for the new
  semantics: the push-order pin (replace on top of the move), the marker
  drag landing at its target, the one-undo-step pin, zero-delta =
  replace only, unpromoted = plain click, empty ground never claims.
- `src/view.zig` — a preview test covering both claim kinds (this was
  the first view test for the move-drag translation at all, including
  the pre-existing selected-claim path).

DESIGN → Architecture → Level Editor → Active-tool model's selection-MOVE
paragraph carries the settled semantics.

## Level-end flag: the banner waves only while no active enemies remain

The level-end flag previously always rendered the wavy animated banner over
the pole, which read as "the exit is open" even while enemies remained — but
levels can only be completed when no active enemies are left. Now the level
screen renders the banner only while the level is completable; with active
enemies up, the pole stands bare. The banner is the completability signal:
it waves ⇔ stepping on the exit would end the level. Hub mission-start and
editor '=' markers keep waving (they're not levels — no enemies concept).

The rule is deliberately ONE predicate: the win condition
(`check_level_end`) and the attack-step auto-skip each carried an identical
inline "active enemies" loop (skip entity 0, `current_health > 0`,
`is_active`, `team != player team`); those two loops were extracted into
`Level.hasActiveEnemies()` (types.zig) and the flag gate uses the same
method. The flag therefore cannot drift from the actual win rule — they are
the same code. Defensive guard: an empty entities slice returns false
(levels always carry the player first, but the method must not read
`entities[0]` unguarded).

Plumbing was already in place: `LevelEndDrawable.banner_source_rectangle`
was an optional ("null when there is no banner") that both the renderer and
the occlusion-inset compositing already handle, so the change is
`levelEndDrawable` gaining a `banner_visible` parameter (nulls the rect when
false) with the level-screen call site passing `!level.hasActiveEnemies()`;
hub and editor call sites pass `true`.

Tests: `Level.hasActiveEnemies` unit test (alive+active+hostile, and the
awkward negatives — dead, inactive, same-team helper, player-only, empty);
the flag frame test gains the `banner_visible = false` → null case; a new
view() test pins the level-screen gating end-to-end (active enemy → banner
null; dead enemy / no enemies → waving; hub marker always waving).

DESIGN → Animation (the flag banner paragraph) and the win-condition prose
(`check_level_end`) carry the settled rule.

## Inventory item icons: stat numbers in the corners, colored by the equipped comparison

The item tooltip already showed each stat with its signed difference to the
equipped gear; now every item icon in the INVENTORY panel carries its stats
directly — one outlined number per stat in the icon's corners, colored by the
same comparison so the grid reads at a glance without hovering:

- single-stat items (weapons: damage; amulets: spell damage) — top-left
- armor (coat/gloves/pants/boots) — health bonus top-left, the item-specific
  stat (defense / damage / pickup radius / speed) bottom-right
- skill tomes — no stats, no numbers

The number shown is the stat VALUE (not the signed difference — the tooltip
carries that). Colors: green (`ui.positive_color`) while better than
equipped, red (`ui.negative_color`) while worse, the theme's lightest while
equal — and a weapon is green only when it beats BOTH equipped hands, red
only when worse than both; a mixed result (beats one hand, loses to the
other) is lightest, since a single number would otherwise have to make a
call the comparison can't support (the decision came out of discussion: any
per-hand rule leaves a well-defined color only under both-hands-or-neither).
An empty equipped slot compares against 0 (an item beats nothing — green),
matching the tooltip's baseline rule.

Recipe and placement reuse the material-count corner label exactly
(`material_count_font_size` 48 + `material_count_inset` 8, `outlined` for the
black outline, non-blocking so hover/click reach the slot beneath and the
slot's tooltip survives): `emitItemStatLabels` (+ `emitItemStatNumber` +
`statComparisonColor`) in src/ui/emit.zig, called from `buildInventoryPanel`
inside the item-icon block — so the numbers are suppressed on the drag source
together with the icon (the item reads as in flight). No renderer changes:
`TextLabel` already carried `color` + `outlined`. Scope: the inventory panel
only — the gear panel is its own baseline (equipped vs equipped = all equal,
meaningless) and ground items aren't the inventory.

Tests: a new `buildInventoryPanel` structure test (the panel had none): the
three weapon comparison colors (beats both / mixed / worse than both), the
boots' two stats (equal health → lightest top-left, better speed → green
bottom-right), the amulet-vs-empty-slot green, a grid-wide census (exactly
the six stat numbers, the sidebar's count labels excluded), and drag-source
suppression (the dragged slot's numbers vanish). Expected positions are
derived from the emitted slot elements' own cells, not re-derived layout
math.

DESIGN → UI Framework carries the bullet; TODO's comparison-color polish
note now lists the icon stat numbers among the shared colors' consumers.

## Inventory item stat numbers: the weapon comparison made inclusive

Follow-up to the stat-number feature above, same session: the weapon's
both-hands comparison became INCLUSIVE on both sides — green while the
weapon at least matches each equipped hand (≥ each: a weapon equal to your
best hand is still green, it upgrades the other), red while it at most
matches each hand (≤ each: equal to one hand and strictly worse than the
other is red — no hand is an upgrade), lightest only when strictly between
the two hands (beats one, strictly loses to the other). The equal-to-BOTH
hands case satisfies both inclusive checks; green wins it there (≥ each
hand is the user-facing rule — the same one that greens a weapon equal to
only the best hand). Motivation (the author's example): hands 4/5 with a
5 in inventory must read green — a strict rule would lightest it, which
says nothing useful about an obvious upgrade for the weaker hand.

The single-stat items (armor, amulets) keep the strict rule — "equal →
lightest" is well-defined there (one equipped slot, one baseline), only the
weapon's two-baseline case needed the inclusive operators. The tooltip's
signed per-hand differences are untouched.

Tests: the panel test's weapon band against hands (5,3) now walks all five
colors (7 green / 5 green-equal / 4 lightest-between / 3 red-equal / 2 red),
plus a full-tie pass (hands 5/5: weapon 5 → green, weapon 4 → red).
DESIGN → UI Framework's bullet carries the rule.

## Inventory item stat numbers: the equal-to-both-hands tie resolved to lightest

Correction to the inclusive weapon rule above, same session: green needs ≥
each hand AND strictly better than at least one hand; red mirrors it (≤ each
AND strictly worse than at least one). Equal to BOTH hands — swapping it in
changes nothing — is LIGHTEST (a pure sidegrade), not green. The rule now
reads symmetrically: green = "somewhere is a strict upgrade, nowhere is a
downgrade", red = "somewhere is a strict downgrade, nowhere is an upgrade",
lightest = "no hand changes anything" (full tie) or "one hand up, one hand
down" (strictly between). The author's verdict on the tie: a weapon
identical to what you hold says nothing useful in green.

## Inventory item stat numbers: moved to the bottom-left corner

Placement correction, same session: the first stat's number (single-stat
items' only number; armor's health bonus) moved from the icon's TOP-LEFT
to the BOTTOM-LEFT — the top-left area carries defining sprite art
(weapon silhouettes especially) that the numbers were obscuring. Both
stats now sit bottom-aligned (bottom-left health/first stat, bottom-right
item-specific stat — the material-count row), out of the art entirely.
The material-count label recipe is unchanged; only the y offset flipped
to the bottom alignment.

## Inventory skill tomes: a green outlined "!" for unlearned skills

The stat-number surface gained its one non-numeric corner mark: a skill
tome whose skill the player has NOT learned wears a green outlined "!"
in the bottom-left corner (the first-stat corner, the stat numbers'
recipe: `material_count_font_size`, black outline, non-blocking so the
slot keeps its tooltip, suppressed on the drag source) — the at-a-glance
version of the tooltip's "Activate to learn" line. A learned tome shows
nothing: its skill is known, its only remaining value is salvaging.

Baseline-independent by construction: the marker depends only on the
learned-skill set (`isSkillLearnedIn`, promoted pub in tooltip.zig for
the emit import), so it renders even while the equipped comparison is
suppressed (`equipped == null` now suppresses only the stat numbers).
The corner-position math was extracted into `statNumberPosition` so the
marker and the numbers share the bottom-left formula. `emitItemStatLabels`
gained the `learned_skills` parameter (mirroring `buildItemTooltip`'s
signature).

Tests: the panel test pins the marker (green "!" at the tome slot's
bottom-left cell corner, full recipe), the learned case (tome's skill in
the learned set → nothing reads "!"), the census (9 grid labels), and
drag-source suppression (9 → 7). DESIGN → UI Framework's bullet carries
the rule.

## Item stat numbers on the gear + entity-inspect panels

The stat numbers spread from the inventory to the other two item surfaces
(the gear panel + the entity-inspect gear mirror), each with the SAME
baseline its tooltips already use:

- **Gear panel**: the player's own equipped items — NO baseline (this gear
  IS the baseline, the same convention as the panel's suppressed tooltip
  comparisons) → every number renders plain LIGHTEST. The numbers ride the
  item icons, suppressed on the drag source together with them (the
  closure gains font_metrics + active_theme; the panel's vestigial
  `_ = font_metrics` went with it).
- **Entity inspect**: the player's equipped gear when inspecting an ENEMY
  (dropped enemy gear is directly usable — the actionable comparison its
  tooltips already make), plain lightest when inspecting the player
  itself (equipped null).

The enabler was a contract change in `emitItemStatLabels`:
`equipped == null` previously emitted NOTHING (no comparison → no
numbers); now it renders the numbers plain LIGHTEST (no comparison → no
COLOR). The baselines became `?u32` per stat (null → lightest inside
`statComparisonColor`), and the weapon's inclusive both-hands rule moved
into `weaponComparisonColor` (a null in either hand → lightest — the rule
needs both baselines live).

Tests: a new buildGearPanel structure test (the panel had none): plain
lightest numbers at the corners (positions derived from the emitted slot
elements' gear refs), full recipe, drag-source suppression. A new
entity-inspect test: the enemy's weapon green vs the player's hands, its
coat split (health red / defense green), and the player-inspect case
plain lightest (positions derived from the item-slot frames in emission
order — the inspect slots are read-only images with no refs).
DESIGN → UI Framework's bullet now scopes the numbers to all three
panels and records the per-panel baseline rule.

## Behind layers: the `behind` decoration-layer flag (grass renders behind the trunk)

Decoration layers gained a draw side: a layer sub-group may carry
`behind true` to draw BEFORE the base sprite instead of over it (the
base's transparent pixels are what let it show through). Design: DESIGN
→ Decorations & Footprint (config format + the per-piece draw order).

- **Config**: `behind true|false` (optional, default false = overlay)
  inside a layer sub-group; whitelisted in the level/hub + registry
  decoration key lists. `DecorationLayer.behind: bool = false`. The
  mission writer emits `behind true` only when set (compact). The
  shipped trees' `grass_back` layers carry it in data/decorations.txt.
- **Render**: `DecorationPieceDrawable.back_layers` —
  buildDecorationPieces splits the config layers into back + overlay
  slices (config order kept within each); draw.zig draws back layers,
  base, then overlays per bbox tile. The two composed-preview sites
  (editor palette cell, sprite-picker cell) follow the same order.
- **Editor**: the picker's ADD commit adopts a registry prefab's
  authored draw side for the picked stem (like its authored color —
  adding `tree_N_grass_back` art lands behind); a re-pick and the
  color-swatch commit keep the layer's side (a visual-identity edit,
  not a placement edit). The registry dupe, cloneDecorationOwned, and
  decorationLayersEqual all carry the flag.
- **Events**: `editor_add/set_decoration_layer` + the player mirrors
  gained `behind: bool = false`. Payload-field addition → old
  editor-session logs with those events (or with a
  player_set_editor_decoration_def layers slice — the indexed-slice
  reader requires every element field) now fail to parse: the
  re-record-until-release policy (Logging & Replay), same precedent as
  keep_original_colors. Shipped validation replays are play sessions —
  unaffected.

Tests: the registry loader pins grass_back behind=true + the rest
false; a buildDecorationPieces split test (interleaved config order,
back/overlay slices, shared position + source rect); the handler test
pins add-adoption + re-pick/color-swatch preservation end-to-end; the

color_index); the session-log pins cover the flat + indexed encodings
of the new field.

## The full color wheel: 24 gradients, programmatically extracted from the artist's asset

data/color_themes.txt regenerated from the artist's wheel graphic
(ColorPalette-01.png, 2026-09-29 delivery). The wheel decoded cleanly:
two big global squares (lightest #fffcf4, darkest #4c3f4f — the #554a58
on the light square is just its border frame) + 24 spokes at exact 15°
steps, each a 6-circle gradient ramp from light (outer ring, r≈1066) to
dark (inner, r≈522). Extraction: per-color connected regions (each circle
is a uniform fill, so every circle = one distinct high-count color with
its pixel centroid), then slot assignment per (spoke angle, ring radius)
around the wheel center — no hand color-picking. Interference handled:
the decorative dark arc + the numbers stamped on the outer circles and
the black center triangle only reduce fill counts / nudge centroids, and
two same-colored adjacent-spoke circle PAIRS merge into single blobs
(#c1cde8 on spokes 315°+330°, #d89656 on 135°+150°) — merged blobs are
assigned via bbox containment gated on the blob's own ring + angle.
Validation: 24×6 slots all filled, every spoke darkens monotonically
outward→inward, shared colors only at the two genuine artist repeats.

**Indexing** (user decision): index 0 = the gradient going straight up
(the yellow spoke), increasing CLOCKWISE — gradient i = the spoke at CCW
angle 90° − 15°·i. The old file's three gradients were spokes 45°/315°/
180° → now indices 3/9/18. With the auto-derivation rule unchanged
(enemy = wheel + N/3, player = wheel + 2N/3; N=24 → +8/+16), the DEFAULT
unthemed look (wheel 0) stays close to the old one: world = yellow
(index 0), enemy = 330° blue (index 8), player = 210° orange (index 16).

The current file's values were hand-altered per playtest feedback and
superseded by the wheel (the user confirmed the asset is the new source
of truth); the extraction also surfaced two hand-copy typos it fixes
(#969446 → #979546, #aaae56 → #aaae57). Globals: #fef9ee/#4c3f4e →
#fffcf4/#4c3f4f.

Old session logs / validation replays unaffected (theme colors ride in
color_themes.txt, re-read at reconstruction — old replays just render
with the new palette). Test updates: the loader disk test pins 24
gradients + the new lightest byte; the theme-picker test's auto-flip
derivation pins re-derived for N=24 (wheel 2 → enemy 2+8=10).

TWO REPEATED COLORS across gradients shipped as-sent, flagged for the
artist in TODO (Cross-cutting polish): #c1cde8 (color_0 of gradients 8
and 9) and #d89656 (color_3 of gradients 20 and 21). DESIGN → Level
theme records the wheel layout (24 gradients, clockwise from top).

The metadata sidebar's level-gradient picker outgrew its panel with the

(6 × 128 = 768 wide), and the list now WINDOWS to the panel:

Tests: the picker builder test pins the 128px geometry; a new overflow
