## Session-log bundle: v2 — cross-session replay over mutable content

The cross-session replay gap: a saved session log replayed against
"whatever is on disk now" — a log recorded against the autosave diverged
the moment any later session's end_hub/end_level overwrote it, custom
missions broke after an editor re-save, and mod-shadowing could change
even shipped paths. Strict verifyReplayMatch then panicked. Design
discussion settled: a folder artifact with EXACT byte copies of every
reconstruction read (readability — no escaping, the copies open as-is),
always embed (mod-shadowing means any path can change; no shipped-vs-
mutable classification), no backwards compatibility (dev-only playerbase
— v1 logs and v1 validation replays are unreadable, re-record).

- **The bundle** (`src/session_log_bundle.zig`, DESIGN → Logging &
  Replay → Session-log bundle): `session_log.txt` (the ordinary
  session-log body + a `ReconstructionCache` manifest section — one entry
  group per cached read: `event_index`, `path` (verbatim, spaces OK),
  `hash` (SHA-256 hex), `file`) + `content/` holding the copies, named
  `<first 8 hex>_<original file name>`. Dedup by hash: identical bytes
  stored once (a level file read on every re-entry); distinct bytes of
  the SAME path (the mid-session autosave write + re-load shape) are
  distinct copies. Writer: content files FIRST, session_log.txt LAST (a
  half-written bundle fails to load cleanly). Loader: the manifest
  section is REQUIRED (a bare session log — e.g. the validation replay —
  is not a bundle), every copy is verified against its recorded hash
  (missing/tampered → error.ContentMismatch, never a silent disk
  fallback), non-monotonic event_index rejects (a hand-merged manifest
  would break the replay-side binary search).
- **Read policy** (state.zig): the blanket `cross_session_replay` flag
  became an explicit `ReconstructionReadPolicy` on reconstructFromEventLog.
  `.authoritative` (bundles: `loadReconstructionCache` pre-populates the
  cache from the manifest, a miss is a broken/hand-edited bundle → panic,
  disk is never consulted) vs `.lazy_disk` (revalidate ONLY). This is the
  one deviation from the session plan: the disk fallback could NOT be
  deleted — `reconstructFromEventLogChecking` (revalidate) needs it,
  because the validation replay deliberately carries no embedded cache
  and replays against the mission's CURRENT files, hash-gated upstream.
  The fallback survives, scoped to exactly that path.
- **Writers migrated**: the ctrl+L dev dump writes
  `logs/session_<YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS>/`, the crash dump writes
  `crashes/crash_<ts>/` (a crash report now carries the embedded content
  — exactly reproducible on any machine). `--replay` takes a bundle dir
  (`session_log_bundle.loadSessionLogBundle` via
  `main.loadAndReconstructSession`). The console `history` stdout dump
  stays a bare writeEventLog projection (inspection text, not an
  artifact).
- **The regression pin** (main.zig, the loadAndReconstructSession test):
  record a real session, write its bundle, then MUTATE the file the
  session read via the mod-shadowing seam (a persistent-dir
  `data/new_player.txt` shadow, derived from the real bytes with the
  player name changed so it stays parseable) — replay stays exact
  (deepEqual) because it serves the embedded copy. Falsified the honest
  way: removing ONLY the preload (keeping .authoritative) fails the
  test with "Shadow Player" vs "New Player" — the mutation genuinely
  reaches a disk read. Side lesson: flipping .authoritative → .lazy_disk
  alone proves nothing (the preload, not the flag, serves the bytes; the
  policy only governs misses).
- Version bump fallout: session-log fixtures are all writeEventLog-
  generated (zero churn); the `file_format_version 1` literals elsewhere
  are mission/level/save files with their own per-type versions.

## Editor: the marker-overlap veto — selection moves never land '!' on '='

The bug: dragging the level-end flag onto the player-start tile (or vice
versa) moved the marker onto the other marker, leaving both on one tile
— a layout the file format cannot represent ('!' and '=' are one symbol
per cell; the save round-trip silently dropped one marker) with undefined
playtest semantics (spawn on the exit). The selection move was the SOLE
creation path (no marker placement tool exists; right-click delete never
touches markers; the file format can't carry the state in).

- `planning.editorSelectionMoveVetoed` (pure): would a selection move by
  delta land a marker on the other? Veto on FINAL positions (translated
  when selected, current when not) — moving both markers together
  preserves their offset (never vetoes; a pre-existing overlap —
  constructible only via crafted states — is only ever RESOLVED by
  moving one marker alone, never created), while moving one onto the
  stationary other vetoes the WHOLE move (not a filtered partial move:
  the flag silently staying behind while the rest moves would be easy to
  miss).
- `planning.planEditorSelectionMoveActions` (new): the move
  orchestrator's whole plan (the translated entries as the commit-chain
  worklist + the clear phase) — the entries build moved out of the
  player_input handler into the pure planner, the other tools' shape
  (the clear phase was already pure; the asymmetry is gone). Empty when
  vetoed.
- Input gate (`handleEditorMoveDrag`): a vetoed drag never pushes the
  move (no dead undo step). The wrinkle: the unselected-claim drag path
  pushes a replace-selection that drains FIRST, so the move plans against
  the POST-replace selection — the gate evaluates the veto against the
  click group at the press tile (`editorClickGroup`, made pub for it),
  not the pre-replace selection; the selected-at-press path evaluates
  the current selection. The replace still fires on its own (a
  selection change is legal even when the move isn't).
- Defensive third layer (the commit chain's marker arm): a crafted
  worklist entry targeting the STAYING other marker's cell plans empty
  (the marker simply doesn't place — it stays where it stands). A LATER
  entry may still move the other away (`markerMovesLater` — a CROSSING
  is not an overlap: '!' landing on '=''s old cell while '=' has not
  moved yet is transient mid-chain and legal). Found the honest way: the
  naive current-position check breaks the legal crossing — the lookahead
  is load-bearing, not just defensive.
- Tests, each falsified against its layer: the veto tests fail with the
  planner veto disabled; the crossing test fails with the lookahead
  stubbed; the crafted-worklist test fails with the marker arm's block
  disabled. The gesture test pins the input gate — it survived the
  planner-veto falsification BY DESIGN (the gate calls the predicate
  directly, an independent layer).

## UI surface state unification: class-1 surface state onto GameState (slices 1–5)

The UI state classification (DESIGN → UI Framework → UI state
classification) settled after the editor inspector toggle and the
in-game middle-panel toggles had drifted into two conventions — the
editor flags had moved onto GameState only because handlers needed to
mutate them, while every other surface toggle stayed a direct
`UiState` write off the undo timeline. The unification rule: class-1
SEMANTIC SURFACE state (what's open) lives on GameState behind events;
classes 2–4 (view affordances, scrolls, gesture lifecycles) stay on
`SessionState.ui_state` with direct writes.

- **Why events + GameState, not a UiState split by naming:** the
  validator (`validatePlayerAction`) sees only GameState, so gating
  "an action is legal only if the UI supplies its trigger" (the
  console/TAS/server seam) was STRUCTURALLY impossible with the
  flags off the timeline — a hand-crafted log could salvage with the
  inventory never opened and verification passed it. Also replay
  verification can't see SessionState at all, so off-timeline UI
  state silently diverged under undo/redo with nothing to catch it.
- **The migration:** `types.UiSurfaceState` on `GameState.ui_surfaces`
  (middle panels + full-screen overlays as ordered sets, the modal
  bools, the entity-inspect target) + `Editor.picker` for the
  editor's centered picker; `toggle_ui_surface` / `inspect_entity`
  meta events + `editor_open_picker` / `editor_close_picker` (open
  REPLACES a stale picker — the palette-group dropdown semantics,
  one action) + their `player_*` orchestrators. The escape chain,
  in_game keybind arms, options_action modal arms, and right-click
  inspect all push+drain via `pushPlayerActionAndDrain` (the
  `swap_weapons` interjection shape — processed inside the same
  update call so this frame's own options-menu gate sees the flipped
  state; the pre-migration direct-write ordering survives).
- **Idle points (the settled (a) choice):** toggles are ORDINARY
  player actions — fired while idle they create their own undo step
  (one click/key = one step); fired mid-drain they ride the
  surrounding subtree (no own idle point). Zero new idle-point
  machinery — the existing anytime-action recording covers both.
  The (b) alternative (UI events without idle points) was rejected
  for now: it needs action-ROOT-aware recording at two sites (the
  naive "emptying event is UI" predicate is wrong — Plan A makes
  `exit_mission`'s subtree END with a handler-pushed surface close),
  and idle points are DERIVED (virtual stack depth), not serialized,
  so downgrading later is a contained derivation-policy change with
  no log-format impact. Playtest friction decides.
- **Reset split by the same rule:** `transitionScreen` closes every
  surface (every world install routes through it — start_level /
  start_hub call it even when the screen enum stays the same), so
  replay reproduces surface closing; the classes-2–4 wholesale reset
  stays in the live loop (`gameLoop` on screen or world_generation
  change).
- **Editor picker commits keep one-action shape:** the 11
  picker-commit orchestrator handlers push `editor_close_picker` as
  a CHILD of the commit (pick+close = one undo step); a no-change
  pick (same value / unchanged draft / same definition) records the
  close ALONE (the close is a change now — "closes without
  recording" became "closes without committing"). A pick that fails
  its backstop/dims check keeps the picker OPEN, nothing recorded —
  the pick visibly didn't take (the decoration-layer arm's semantic,
  now uniform; the decoration-sprite arm used to close silently on
  backstop because the null happened at the arm top).
- **Session log v3:** the toggle events; the writer/reader gained
  OPTIONAL UNION-VARIANT payloads (tag alone = null — the
  `EditorPickerTarget.entity_layer` shape) in both the union branches
  (the struct-field optional convention already existed at
  `writeEventField`/`parseEventFieldValue`).
- **Legality (the motivation):** one hoisted gate in
  `validatePlayerAction` over the bool core
  `actionTriggerSurfaceOpen` (tested directly, the no-expectPanics
  convention): inventory family → inventory panel, the cross-panel
  drags (equip/unequip) → inventory AND gear, drag-to-bar → skills;
  everything else's trigger always renders. Surface toggles are
  scope-checked (`surfaceToggleLegal`). `player_inspect_entity` is
  level-only with a live-entity target. No existing fixture replayed
  a gated orchestrator, so the sweep was an end-to-end pin, not
  fixture repairs.
- Session-log version 2→3 (hard gate — old logs re-record, pre-release
  policy; no shipped replay fixtures existed, so the fallout was two
  hand-crafted test fixtures' version lines).

## Editor picker arms: the shared expectPickerKind gate (tech debt)

The eight picker-pick arms in `input_handlers.zig` each opened with a
hand-written "gate: the open picker must be kind X, else return" switch —
payload sites used `else => return` (a new picker kind would silently
no-op) and void sites enumerated every other variant (compile-checked,
but eight copies to re-edit in lockstep; the ui-surface session re-wrote
all eight while migrating onto `Editor.picker`). Collapsed into ONE
file-private helper:

- `expectPickerKind(editor, comptime kind) ?@FieldType(EditorPickerTarget,
  @tagName(kind))` — returns the payload when the open picker is `kind`,
  else null (no picker open, or another kind — a crafted click while the
  wrong picker is open no-ops, the pick arms' standing posture). The
  helper's switch enumerates every variant explicitly, so adding a new
  `EditorPickerTarget` kind is a compile error in ONE place instead of a
  silent no-op gap (payload sites) or eight hand-edits (void sites).
- Zig 0.16 note: `std.meta.TagPayload` doesn't exist —
  `@FieldType(T, @tagName(kind))` is the 0.16 shape for "payload type of
  this union tag".
- Per-arm gate comments dropped (the helper's doc comment carries the
  why once); behavior unchanged — the picker tests in
  `handler_tests_editor.zig` pass unmodified.

## Keybind editing: the rebuild-ownership end-to-end test (follow-up)

The keybind editor slice 4 left the mutation path untested — the arms
were thin and the steal scan + capture seam were unit-covered, but
`applyKeybindEdit`/`removeKeybindBinding`'s `rebuildInputBindings`
ownership ledger (kept strings MOVE, dropped strings + the old slice
free, appended strings dupe from the capture buffer) had no coverage.

- The test (inline in `input_handlers.zig`, next to the
  `findKeybindSteal` unit test) drives the REAL confirm seam
  (`resolveKeybindCaptureOutcome` captured → confirmed) plus
  `removeKeybindBinding` through three scenarios on one history: a
  rekey-that-steals (keep + drop + replace), a clean add, a remove
  (+ out-of-range no-op), and pins the mutate + mark-dirty discipline
  (a settings `PendingWrite` lands).
- LEAK-CHECKED per the settings-ownership convention: the harness
  arena carries only the config bootstrap; the history runs on
  `std.testing.allocator` as its backing (any allocation anywhere in
  the flow that isn't freed surfaces at test end — the flow must be
  pure settings/ui mutation), and the binding strings are SELF-OWNED
  under `testing.allocator` (an arena would mask a forgotten free).
  Teardown frees the final list via `loaders.freeSettings` — every
  remaining string is either a moved self-owned original or a
  rebuild-duped one, so any imbalance fails the leak check.
- The test's first draft asserted IN-PLACE replacement and failed:
  replace is DROP + APPEND by design — the rekeyed row moves to the
  END of the list. Harmless: the keybinds tab sorts rows by action,
  and the conflict rule leaves no co-firing same-combo pair whose
  order could matter for first-match-wins. Noted in the test comment
  (list order carries no meaning).

## Input dispatch convergence: slice 1 — the one dispatch pass

The planned convergence refactor (design settled in session, then landed
— see DESIGN → Input → Dispatch convergence): `translateInput` set the
anytime/idle flags via ~40 per-action `checkAction` lines while button
releases + console commands folded through `applyAction` — two
hand-maintained copies of the same action→flag mapping, and the
keybind-picker-vs-dispatch inconsistency that came with it.

- **The one dispatch pass:** `translateInput`'s action section is ONE
  loop over the bindings — every binding that passes `bindingFires`'
  gates (derived-context intersection, required-modifier subset, a real
  press edge or a whitelisted synthetic repeat, not suppressed) folds
  through `applyAction`. Iterating the bindings, not the actions, keeps
  the pass O(bindings) — actions with no binding are never touched
  (the rejected alternative, a comptime loop over all 175 Action
  variants, was 175×bindings of mostly-wasted enum compares). The five
  keyboard-bridge arms (editor tools/palette groups — no button carries
  them) moved INTO `applyAction` (the payload is the keyboard action's
  own identity), so keybind, click, and console share the consumption
  sites with zero residue in translateInput.
- **Behavior fix folded in (user-approved):** every action is now
  uniformly keybindable. The keybinds tab's action picker lists the
  whole enum, but the old per-action dispatch lines never checked the
  menu commands or several click actions — a binding on `new_game` (or
  `toggle_entity_inspect`, `save_game`, ...) was silently dead. The
  derived binding-context gate keeps each to its screens, so nothing
  fires where it shouldn't; a binding pinned by test
  (menu-action binding fires on the main-menu set only).
- **`actionRepeats`** — the repeat whitelist (undo/redo, skip,
  error-scroll, movement cursors) named as one function; the per-binding
  gate consults it for synthetic edges (previously each call site chose
  its `keys_repeated` slice — the whitelist lived in ~9 lines' worth of
  arg choices).
- **`action_binding_contexts_lut`** (types.zig) — the 175-way
  `actionBindingContexts` switch (the single source of truth, still
  compile-enforced exhaustive) materialized into a comptime table the
  pub fn reads; the context gate runs once per binding in the dispatch
  pass and once per competitor inside `isSuppressed`, so the switch was
  the most-executed line of the input path (the generated-lookups
  pattern).
- **Same-frame degeneracies resolve first-listed-wins** (the conflict
  rule's tiebreak): equal-specificity same-combo competitors are
  suppressed inside the pass (unchanged); the skill-slot guard keeps one
  slot selection — a same-frame double-slot press keeps the
  FIRST-LISTED binding's slot (previously lowest slot number won; the
  new tiebreak matches the conflict rule's convention). `applyAction`
  is idempotent per arm, so a same action on two inputs both firing is
  a non-event.
- Tests: the seven `checkAction` unit tests rewritten against the
  per-binding predicate (same assertions, same semantics; the
  equal-specificity test's "regardless of query order" note died with
  the query), plus two new tests — the repeat-whitelist gate inside the
  predicate, and the menu-action fix.
- Slice 1 of the convergence; slices 2–4 (fired_actions record + the
  sound choke point; the count-assertion rewrite; the input_handlers
  split evaluation) stay in TODO.

## Input dispatch convergence: slice 2 — fired_actions + the sound choke point

The `fired_actions` record + the ONE per-action sound choke point — the
"no single consumption choke point" consequence of the two-copies era.

- **`PlayerInput.fired_actions: std.EnumSet(Action)`** — recorded by
  `applyAction` itself, so all three input seams (keyboard bindings,
  button releases, console commands) report uniformly; a set, so a
  same-frame keybind + button + console command on one action records
  once.
- **`dispatchFiredActionSounds`** (input_handlers, called from
  `main.update` before the handlers): one `queueActionSound` per fired
  action. Replaced the ~25 scattered per-flag queue sites: the 9-site
  escape chain (`queueEscapeSound` deleted), dismiss_error, the
  options_action top-of-switch queue, the menu_action queue, the 4
  editor-command sites, and the 5 in_game toggle sites.
- **Fixed on the way: the `.change_setting` double-play class** — the
  options_action top-of-switch queue (added later to fix the silent
  entries) plus the arms' own queues meant `.change_setting`,
  `.edit_keybind`, and `.select_settings_tab` each queued TWO layers
  per click for months (only ears could catch it). The choke point makes
  the class structurally impossible — one queue site, one layer. Pinned
  headless by the new dispatchFiredActionSounds test (also pins both
  exclusion classes + the set-dedup property).
- **Two documented exclusions** at the choke point (the TODO's "sites
  needing more than the action stay per-site"):
  - `types.actionSoundUnwired` — moved from sound_report.zig's private
    `isUnwiredAction` to types.zig, shared by the choke point AND the
    report's shopping list (one list, two consumers): zoom/cursor keys,
    error-scroll ticks, dump_event_log, skip_level, confirm.
  - `actionLayerRidesConsumptionSite` — undo/redo (sound only when a
    step actually happened), swap_weapons (any-weapon/prepared gate),
    cancel (live preparation), the skill slots (prepare/unprepare only —
    an auto-fire cast plays the full skill cue). These keep their
    per-site queues; everything else is sound-on-fired.
- Sound-report note: the report's button-layers preamble still documents
  the unwired set (the same list, from the shared fn now).
- Slice 2 of the convergence; slices 3–4 (the count-assertion rewrite,
  the input_handlers split evaluation) stay in TODO. The Audio section's
  cue-wiring coverage item shrank accordingly (the double-play is fixed
  + pinned; the event-level cue families remain).

## Input dispatch convergence: slice 3 — what-recorded assertions replace count deltas

The picker tests in `handler_tests_editor.zig` asserted recorded-event
COUNT deltas (+2/+4) — the class that broke by hand four times during
the ui-surface migration (one fix wrong on the first try): a count
breaks whenever a commit chain grows a step, and nothing distinguishes
"the right events" from "the right number of events".

- **`expectLastEvents(history, kinds)`** (+ `RecordedEventKind`:
  outer category + inner variant tag, compared via the established
  two-level `activeTag` convention; payloads stay asserted on state,
  not re-derived) — asserts the last N recorded events ARE the expected
  chain.
- **Composable pair consts** — `open_picker_pair` /
  `close_picker_pair` (`player_open_editor_picker` +
  `editor_open_picker`, `player_close_editor_picker` +
  `editor_close_picker` — every open/close is a PAIR: the orchestrator
  + the machinery event it pushes) and their two concatenations; the
  six GROWING deltas converted:
  - the same-sprite re-pick close-only → the close pair;
  - the unchanged-draft footprint confirm → the close pair;
  - the reopen + empty-draft confirm → close pair + open pair;
  - the same-definition decoration re-pick → open pair + close pair;
  - the same-value gradient pick → open pair + close pair;
  - the inventory delete → the delete pair
    (`player_delete_editor_inventory_item` +
    `editor_delete_inventory_item`) — the crafted empty-slot +
    out-of-range deletes recording nothing is now implied by the tail
    being exactly the real delete pair.
- **The `==` no-op gates KEEP their count equality** (e.g. the
  dims-mismatch pick records nothing): they assert NOTHING was
  recorded — absence, not a growing count; no churn class.

## Input dispatch convergence: slice 4 — the split evaluation (decided: no split)

The convergence's last open item (folded in by design — "don't split as a
separate chore first"): does `input_handlers.zig` split naturally now?

- **Decision: NO SPLIT NOW.** Post-convergence the file is ~5,400 lines:
  ~1,900 in `handleAnytimeInput`'s switch, ~420 in `handleIdleInput`,
  ~360 cursor resolution, ~1,100 in cohesive per-topic helper blocks
  (the keybind-edit machinery, the text-field commit sites, the editor
  item helpers), ~1,800 tests. The dispatcher switches are intrinsically
  large — they enumerate the actions' consumption; splitting switch arms
  out is mechanical churn with no design win. The per-topic blocks are
  cohesive but heavily cross-referenced through file-private helpers
  (`pushPlayerActionAndDrain`, `expectPickerKind`, the item-action
  builders) — moving them means a pub/export shuffle for zero
  correctness gain.
- **The revisit trigger (recorded in TODO):** the hub editor + campaign
  editor add arms to this file. If the file crosses ~7k lines or the arms
  stop fitting one scan, the hub/campaign arms split out alongside the
  editor arms — a real seam (new content category), not a chore split.
- The convergence is COMPLETE (all four slices): one dispatch pass
  (`bindingFires` → `applyAction`), `fired_actions` + the sound choke
  point, what-recorded assertions, the split decision.

## Enemy AI movement: the straightness tiebreak (slice 1 — destination selection)

The observed bug: an enemy on the player's row habitually stepped a row UP
instead of walking the row toward the player. Root cause was NOT pathfinding —
A* already returned the straight row path in the same-row case. It was the
movement-destination SELECTION (`ai_movement.zig`): a basic sword enemy with
spinblade (point-blank AoE) ready moves in `point_blank_cluster` mode, where
the row tile (1,1) and the row-above tile (1,0) score identically (player
within radius 1), and the `(x, y)` `tileBefore` tiebreak always picked the
lower `y` — the top-row tile. Same tiebreak shape in `keepRangeDestination`
and in `enemyApproachTurn`'s no-path reachable-tile fallback.

- **The rule** (`functions.straighterTileBefore`): when the primary metric
  (cluster score / Chebyshev distance) ties between candidate tiles, prefer
  the STRAIGHTER line to the mover's nearest hostile — first by perpendicular
  offset from the mover→hostile line (cross product; a same-row chase stays on
  its row, a 45° chase walks the diagonal), then by squared euclidean distance
  to the hostile, then the `(x, y)` tile convention for a total deterministic
  order. Integer-only (squares and cross products — no floats in gameplay
  logic). The euclidean tier alone is NOT enough: the row tile (1,1) and the
  tile directly above the player (0,0) are euclidean-equidistant, and the
  `(x, y)` fallback would pick (0,0) again — the cross-product tier is what
  actually encodes "walk the line from where you stand".
- **Anchor semantics**: the nearest hostile to the CASTER (not per candidate
  tile — the anchor must be stable across the tie group or "straighter" is
  ill-defined). `nearestHostilePosition` mirrors `nearestHostileDistance`
  (which stays per-center: it answers "can I act from this tile").
- **Keep-range reads naturally too**: among equally-far standoff tiles, the
  kiter stays directly IN LINE with the hostle being kited (the duel line)
  rather than off to the side.
- All three selection sites swapped (`pointBlankClusterDestination`,
  `keepRangeDestination`, the approach fallback); `tileBefore` stays as the
  final fallback tier + the editor's row-major insert order. Design: DESIGN →
  Determinism & Tiebreaking (the movement-tiebreak bullet) + Architecture →
  AI movement modes.
- Behavior change → old session logs diverge under strict replay verification
  (pre-release: re-record; the policy note already lived in the TODO item).
- Tests: `straighterTileBefore` unit tests (row/diagonal/euclid/(x,y) tiers,
  antisymmetry), the bug layout pinned at speed 1 AND speed 2 (the wider tie
  field including the player's column), keep-range standoff updated to the
  in-line tile.

## Pathfinding: Chebyshev heuristic + straightness f-cost tiebreak (slice 2)

The other half of the "Enemy pathing straightness" TODO item. Two paired
changes in `shortestPath` (functions.zig) — the pairing is the point:

- **Heuristic: Manhattan → Chebyshev** (`chebyshevHeuristic`). With diagonal
  steps costing 1, Chebyshev is the EXACT remaining cost on open ground —
  it never overestimates, so A* is guaranteed to return a
  shortest-by-steps path. Manhattan overestimates up to 2x whenever the
  destination sits diagonally from a node, which could pop the goal via a
  longer route before the optimal route's nodes were ever expanded —
  empirically confirmed by fuzzing `shortestPath` against a reference BFS
  (7x7 grids, ~65% floor density: suboptimal paths within 100 seeds), and
  it stays suboptimal even under the new tiebreak (re-fuzzed with the
  Manhattan probe active: still 6-step paths where 5 is optimal). The
  seed-92 counterexample is pinned as the "heuristic admissibility" test —
  it fails if the heuristic regresses to Manhattan.
- **f-cost tiebreak: position → squared euclidean distance to the
  destination, then position** (`comparePathNodes`, via the new
  `PathNode.distance_squared`). With an exact heuristic f-ties become
  COMMON (on open ground f is constant along every monotone path), so the
  tiebreak decides the path's SHAPE — and the old x-then-y tiebreak would
  have bent same-row chases up a row (row node and row-above diagonal tie
  on f; x-then-y picks the lower y). Pinned by the same-row
  walk-the-row and diagonal walk-the-diagonal tests.
- Why slice 2 was separate from the movement-selection fix (slice 1): the
  decision sites (`ai_movement.zig`) needed the perpendicular-line key
  (cross product — euclid alone ties the row tile with the tile directly
  above the target), while A* nodes progress monotonically toward the goal
  so euclidean-to-destination alone suffices there.
- `manhattanDistance` deleted (no remaining users). Behavior change → old
  session logs diverge under strict replay verification (pre-release:
  re-record). Design: DESIGN → Determinism & Tiebreaking (the A* f-cost
  tiebreak bullet).

## Outline stripe shader (marching outlines)

The TODO's readability complaint: the theme-`lightest` outlines (the artist's
offwhite) read weakly over busy art. Fix: one fragment shader (the
spriteLodSnapBias pattern — default batch shader + one addition) flipping the
outline pixels between the incoming tint and the theme's `darkest` in
marching 45° diagonal stripes.

- **Shader** (backend.zig, GLSL 3.30 + ES 3.00 variants like both precedents):
  `s = gl_FragCoord.x + gl_FragCoord.y + phase*period` in render-target
  pixels; `mod(s, period) < band` flips the RGB to the dark color at the
  texel's own alpha (premultiplied output — the pass draws under
  BLEND_ALPHA_PREMULTIPLY). One shader covers BOTH draw shapes: untextured
  strokes (the white 1x1 texture passes the tint through) and the icon halo
  masks (the white band flips, the transparent interior stays). A compile
  failure degrades EXACTLY to the pre-shader look (solid tint), never a
  crash. The SDF text outline pass is a separate shader, untouched.
- **Covered draws**: the five world tile-outline arms in `drawTileOverlay`
  (cursor, range/radius/aggro outlines, region edges), `drawHighlightOutline`
  (the UI icon halo masks — sprite-backed highlighted buttons/images, e.g.
  the turn-step icons + its rectangle fallback), and the spriteless
  highlighted button's stroked rect (the 9-slice panel-button hover
  outline). Explicitly out: SDF text outlines, `.text_field` 9-slice frames,
  lightest-tinted panels, occlusion insets.
- **The light color rides the existing per-draw tint; the dark color +
  phase are frame-level uniforms** (set once per frame in `render` from
  `ViewState`), the band width is per-scope (`beginOutlineStripeScope(total_scale)`
  — 8 source px × the pass's whole scale so the bands match the drawn
  outline's thickness at every zoom).
- **The endShaderMode trap, caught at implementation time**: every stripe
  scope opens INSIDE an enclosing sprite pass, and raylib's endShaderMode
  restores the DEFAULT shader — the first wiring silently dropped the sprite
  LOD snap bias for the rest of the shared world-pass scope. The close
  (`endOutlineStripeScope(total_scale)`) re-opens the sprite pass. Documented
  in DESIGN → Platform Seam → Outline stripe shader + the backend method
  doc.
- **Phase**: `ViewState.outline_stripe_phase`, computed in `view()` from
  `session.animation_clock` stepped at `settings.animation_fps` — 8 steps
  per cycle, frame-quantized to match the tile-highlight sheet's cadence
  (one animation system; freezes on pause with everything else). The clock
  wraps mod the cycle IN u64 before the f32 conversion (f32 mantissa holds
  only ~16.8s of microseconds — an unwrapped clock loses phase after
  minutes). Pure view side — no game state, no replay impact.
- **Decisions**: cursor included in the march; stepped (not continuous)
  pacing; 50/50 duty (period = 2 bands). Tuning knobs, all in one place:
  band scale (`outline_thickness` × total_scale), crawl speed
  (`outline_stripe_steps` in view.zig), duty (the `2.0*` period factor in
  the shader source).
- Verified: native + test suite + web compile; the look still needs the
  eyeball pass on both targets (band size vs. outline thickness, crawl
  speed) — tuning knobs above if it reads off.

### Outline stripe shader: shared band follow-up

First eyeball pass found two issues, both fixed by one move: the world
outlines (cursor/range/radius, at the default camera_zoom 50 → 0.5) marched
at HALF the pixel speed of the UI icon outlines, and the bands read small.
Root cause of the speed mismatch: the band scaled with the pass's whole
scale (world = zoom × renderScale, UI = renderScale), and the crawl rate is
one period per cycle — a half-size band means a half-rate crawl. Fix: ONE
shared, zoom-independent band (`outline_stripe_band_multiplier` = 2.0 × the
shared outline thickness × renderScale — doubled, 16 reference px) for BOTH
families: shared band → shared period → identical size and identical speed
by construction. All stripe uniforms (dark + phase + band) are now
frame-level; the scope helpers only bind/unbind (begin takes no param; end
still takes the enclosing sprite pass's scale for the endShaderMode
restore). The world bands no longer track the outline stroke's zoom-scaled
thickness — family uniformity beats per-family thickness matching.

The phase stays a ViewState field (asked whether it could be dropped): it
already IS fully derived from the clock — a pure per-frame function of the
pause-gated `animation_clock` + `animation_fps`, nothing accumulated; the
field is the transport to the renderer, whose only input is ViewState (the
same channel the tile-highlight sheet's `source_rectangle` uses). The raw
clock cannot ride a shader time uniform directly: float mantissa loses
µs precision after ~17s, so the u64 wrap must happen before the f32 — and
the wrap/step math stays view-side, where it is headless-tested.

### Outline stripe shader: diagonal/crawl flip + the salvage drag region

Two follow-ups from the second eyeball pass. (1) The stripe diagonal family
and crawl direction flipped (`s = x - y - phase*period`, was
`x + y + phase*period`) — the two signs in the shader source are the flip
knobs, one for the diagonal family, one for the crawl direction; GLSL `mod`
returns [0, period) for negative s, so no wrap handling needed. (2) The
inventory multi-salvage drag region (a stroked `.solid_rect`,
`filled = false`, panels.zig) was the one outline-class draw still on the
plain tint — the stroked `.solid_rect` BRANCH now draws through the stripe
scope (the element doc already defined stroked = the outline class, same
primitive as the world range/radius outlines, so the branch wrap covers any
future stroked solid_rect too).

### Tile highlight: the marching-ants sheet retired, replaced by the inset outline

The clickable-tile highlight was the game's earliest-prototype art
(`world/tile_highlight.png`, a 4-frame 256x256 marching-ants sheet,
`buildHighlightOverlays` picking frames off the animation clock). Removed
entirely; the highlight is now an inset square outline in the outline class
(shared 8-source-px thickness + the marching stripe shader, theme
`lightest`), replacing the sheet's per-frame animation with the shared
stripe phase — one outline system, one animation.

- **The inset is preserved from the sheet art**: measured the sheet with a
  PIL probe — every frame's band sits at 16..239 of 256, i.e. inset 16
  source px = 1/16 of the tile. The replacement outline insets by
  `tile_highlight_inset_divisor` (16) of the tile side — shared constant in
  element.zig, used by BOTH the world highlight draw and the Select icon.
- **The editor Select tool icon** used the sheet's frame 0 as its palette
  graphic — replaced with the same inset outline: a stroked `.solid_rect`
  (the outline class by construction — it draws through the stripe shader,
  so the icon animates exactly like the world highlight), inset 1/16 of
  the fitted square with the outline-class stroke ratio (side/32 — 8 source
  px on the 256 tile).
- **Dead plumbing removed with the sheet**: `TileOverlayDrawable.source_rectangle`
  (highlight-only), `Image.source_rectangle` (the Select frame was its last
  non-null user — the emitEditorToolCell param too),
  `tile_highlight_frame_*` constants (the surviving 256 renamed
  `tool_graphic_tile_size`), the ui.zig `tile_highlight_frame_size`
  re-export (no external users), the asset itself, and the sheet-drawing +
  load-miss-fallback arm in draw.zig. The generated sprite metadata
  regenerates from the assets scan at build.

### Outline stripe shader: pure white/black pair

Eyeball experiment (user's call): the stripe flip hardcodes PURE WHITE and
PURE BLACK bands instead of theme `lightest`/`darkest` — both branches take
the texel's own alpha (premultiplied), so the halo-mask shapes and AA edges
are unchanged; only the band colors move. The per-draw `lightest` tint
plumbing stays (it is the compile-fail fallback look); the `stripeDark`
uniform + its upload + location field were dead after the hardcode and are
removed.

### Outline stripe shader: lightest + player gradient[5] pair

Third eyeball iteration on the band pair (theme darkest → pure white/black
→ this): the light branch is back to the incoming per-draw tint (theme
`lightest` at every call site — also the compile-fail fallback look), and
the dark branch uploads player gradient index 5 (the button-tint class)
per frame. No new plumbing: `ActiveColorTheme` already carries
`player_gradient`, so `render()` reads `colors[5]` straight off
`ViewState.active_color_theme`. The `stripeDark` uniform + upload +
location field return with the uniform-based pair (they were removed for
the hardcoded white/black try).

Kept — the settled pair (the user's pick after the three-way try: theme
darkest → pure white/black → lightest + player gradient[5]).

### Outline width unification: constant at every zoom and element size

The outlines were dependent on the size of the outlined thing: the world
strokes scaled with the camera zoom (4/8/16 ref px across the zoom range),
the halo masks' baked band scaled with the sprite's drawn size (e.g. the
turn-step icons at small_icon_size showed a proportionally thin halo), and
the Select icon scaled its stroke with the cell. Unified to ONE constant:
`types.outline_thickness` (8 reference px, moved to types.zig as the single
source — it was textures.zig-local, plus a duplicated local in
editor_pickers).

- World rect strokes (highlight/cursor/range/radius/aggro + region edges):
  dropped the × world_scale — the outlined thing scales with zoom, the
  stroke does not.
- Halo masks (the silhouette-hugging path): `getOutlineTexture(sprite_id,
  drawn_scale)` generates the band at `ceil(8 / drawn_scale)` SOURCE px, so
  the DRAWN band is the constant width at every element size. The outline
  cache re-keyed (sprite, band) — a flat `"{sprite}|{band}"` composite
  string (std's auto hash refuses slice-containing struct keys), one mask
  per (sprite, distinct drawn scale); keys own duped strings now freed in
  deinit (the old StringHashMap keys were never freed — a process-lifetime
  leak, fixed in passing).
- Rect strokes (Select icon, spriteless button hover, halo fallback,
  footprint picker bars, the text-field caret): all reference the shared
  constant.
- The stripe bands were already constant (16 ref px) — unchanged; the
  occlusion inset stays source-px-scaled BY DESIGN (a world-scaled shadow,
  not the outline family). Design: DESIGN → Platform Seam → Outline stripe
  shader → Constant outline width.

### Prepared-skill switch: stale targeting highlights (bug fix)

Repro: shield main hand + sword off hand; prepare sword skill 3 (flash
strike — its teleport landing tiles highlight); click shield skill 1
(bash) — ALL the flash-strike landing tiles stayed highlighted. Root
cause: the `player_prepare_skill` handler replaced `prepared_skill` and
relied on the NEW skill's prepare event to replace `highlighted_tiles` —
but a no-target prepare pushes NO event (`hostilesInRange` returns null,
not an empty slice, when nothing is in range — bash at range 1 with the
enemies at range 2+), so the previous skill's tiles lingered as stale
targeting UI. The cancel/use/skip paths all clear (clear_highlights +
clear_prepared_skill); the SWITCH path was the one hole.

Fix: the handler clears `highlighted_tiles` alongside setting the new
`prepared_skill` — switching skills resets the previous skill's targeting
UI first, then the new skill's prepare event re-highlights whatever it
has. Regression test in handler_tests_turnflow.zig pins the repro
(prepare flash strike → prepare bash with no targets → highlights empty +
prepared switched). Behavior change → old session logs that switch
prepared skills diverge on replay (pre-release: re-record).

### Reflection riders: shader-status boot probe + cache-key cleanup

Two riders from the closing reflection, one commit.

- **Cache-key leak class**: all four TextureStore caches dupe their keys at
  insert, but only the outline cache (fixed in passing earlier in the
  session) freed them in deinit — `texture_cache`, `composite_inset_cache`,
  and `sprite_bounds_cache` leaked every duped key for the process lifetime
  (invisible to the suite: `src/raylib/` is excluded from the headless test
  build). deinit now frees every cache's keys alongside its values.
- **Silent-degrade visibility**: the three fallback shaders (sprite LOD →
  plain trilinear, outline stripes → solid tint, SDF text → shadow ring)
  degrade SILENTLY on a compile failure — by design, never a crash — and
  nothing surfaced it (the SDF path prints to stderr, invisible in a
  browser). The boot section of the diagnostics log now records each one's
  compile status (compiled/FAILED + its fallback), gathered at first render
  from the backend's three shader handles. The GLSL ES web variant is the
  realistic failure case. Design: DESIGN → Platform Seam → Diagnostics.
- Remaining reflection items recorded as TODO riders (the unused-pub report
  script, the skill targeting null-vs-empty convention doc, the per-tile
  stripe-scope batch flush note); one more convention landed in AGENTS →
  Commit policy (don't split landed commits when the split costs more than
  it buys).

## Doc-symbol staleness checker (machine-walked truth for doc prose)

The drift class: DESIGN/AGENTS/TODO name code symbols in backticks, and
symbol moves/renames silently orphan the prose — every find so far was by
accident during unrelated sessions (two during the session-log bundle work,
two during dispatch convergence). Queued as "build BEFORE the campaign
editor" — that work adds a wave of new symbols + doc prose, and the
checker's value compounds from the first new line.

`scripts/doc_symbol_check.sh`: extracts every backticked dot-path from the
three living docs and checks them against a token corpus of every .zig
under src/ (raylib seam included — docs name backend symbols) + tools/ +
build.zig, comments stripped (a symbol only a comment names is stale too —
comments drift). Two advisory tiers: STALE (the member name exists in no
source file) and MOVED (the member exists but not in the file the doc's
first segment names — the recorded drift class). Allowlist for deliberate
non-symbols: external APIs (`W.STOPSIG`, `std.debug.simple_panic`,
`LazyPath.getPath`) + the `ui.X` facade meta-placeholder. `--strict` for
CI-if-ever.

First-run catches, all fixed in the same commit: DESIGN's
`parser.loadSettings`/`parser.loadDecorationRegistry`/`parser.freeSettings`
qualifiers (all three live in loaders.zig — the exact drift class the
checker exists for); the Raylib-seam paragraph rewritten from
"switches from `rl.loadTexture`" history-phrasing to the as-is
readFile → loadImageFromMemory flow; two history parentheticals naming the
removed applyVolumes machinery trimmed to DONE pointers (DESIGN carries
design, DONE carries history). Convention settled: TODO prose naming a
NOT-YET-LANDED symbol uses the bare name (`inspect_cursor`) — a backticked
dot-path is the checker's "exists today" signal. DONE.md is deliberately
not scanned: history legitimately names dead symbols.

## Unused-pub report (machine-walked truth for the minimize-pub discipline)

The discipline (AGENTS → Code Style) kept losing to human attention —
`walkingDistance` (pub, zero callers) and the dead
`ui.tile_highlight_frame_size` facade re-export survived many sessions.
The compiler flags unused file-private symbols but nothing flags an unused
pub; this script is the missing checker.

`scripts/unused_pub_report.sh`: walks `pub fn`/`pub var` + typed value
consts (`pub const name: T = ...`) under src/ — the raylib seam excluded
(backend interface, not the game's API discipline) — against a per-file
token corpus of every .zig in the tree as a reference source (comments
stripped, string literals kept: panic-message names are deliberate). One
sort+join+awk pass. Three tiers: DEAD (the declaration line is the
symbol's only occurrence anywhere — deletion candidates, the
walkingDistance class), UNUSED (internal-only — de-pub candidates:
file-private restores the compiler's dead-code check), TEST-ONLY
(cross-file references from test files only — keep pub + note why, per
AGENTS → Code Style).

Deliberate scope decisions (the false-positive classes found while
calibrating): plain `=`-form consts (types/aliases) are NOT walked — types
are consumed without ever being named cross-file (field types, enum
literals, namespace re-exports), so never-named ≠ dead and word-matching
cannot judge it; the dead-TYPE class (`DecorationId`) stays code review's.
`src/crash_dump.zig`'s struct-member pub fns are skipped — zig's
panic-namespace contract, installed wholesale as
`pub const panic = crash_dump.panic` and called by compiler-generated code
that never names them. The ui.zig facade is handled in both directions: a
src/ui symbol's re-export line is plumbing, not a use; a facade decl
(`=`-form, unwalked anyway) is only real when a file outside src/ui/ names
the symbol.

First run (the payoff — 671 decls walked): **11 DEAD** — types.zig's Rect
placement helpers (`centerX`/`centerY`/`place*`, dead since a refactor),
element.zig's `totalHeight`/`totalWidth`, loaders'
`customDecorationSpriteConforms`, `credits_header_gap` + its dead ui.zig
re-export (the tile_highlight class). **106 UNUSED** — ~60 the ui
layout-const class (pub + facade re-export + no consumer), plus
state.zig's `takeSnapshot`/`markWriteDirty`/`writeSettingsToFile`, the
skill_helpers trio, the loaders `free*` family. **3 TEST-ONLY** —
`computeMaxDamageRange`, `minimalPngHeader`, `buildAt` (keep pub, note
why). The cleanup sweep is deliberately NOT part of this landing: each
de-pub/delete is a per-symbol decision — some UNUSED are forward-looking
(`freeHub` and the loaders `free*` family become load-bearing at
campaign-editor slice 1, the self-owned-loader rider), and the
layout-const class is one mechanical sweep whenever it's taken. (The
sweep landed the next session — see "Minimize-pub sweep" below.)
