## Console input: id interning — the held-state lifetime fix (stress-test find)

First real stress test of the console channel (piped scripts driving
held-key sequences at speed) surfaced a crash class the unit suite could
not see: `press <id>` merged a key_down whose id string was DUPED INTO THE
FRAME ARENA, but `InputState.keys_held` / `key_repeat_state` RETAIN that
slice past the frame (a held key stays held until its `release`) — and
`main.frame` resets the frame arena every frame. The retained slice
dangled into reused memory: live, a piped `press ArrowRight` → later
frames segfaulted inside `isHeld` (getModifiers reads every keys_held
entry each frame); before crashing, it also produced silently wrong held
state (the "held" key vanished mid-chord, which made the first
black-box measurements self-contradictory — a rollover frame reading
dir (-1,0) instead of the correct (0,0) cancel).

- The hardware path was never affected: `input_poll.zig`'s mapping-table
  ids are static string literals, so hardware-held ids always had static
  lifetime. The console merge was the only producer of frame-arena id
  bytes.
- **Fix — intern at the merge seam**: `inputEventFor` resolves the id via
  `internedInputId` (a lookup against `types.producible_key_ids` /
  `producible_mouse_ids` — the same literals the backend uses; the parser
  already validated the id against those tables at parse time, so the
  lookup cannot miss). Merged events carry the static slice; the
  arena-dupe (`dupeEventPayload`) is deleted. The merged events ARRAY
  stays arena-owned (within-frame consumption by `translateInput`), and
  typed text stays arena-duped (within-frame consumption by the
  text-input router — it copies into the field buffer).
- **Why interning instead of a longer-lived allocator**: the id set is a
  finite, already-declared table; resolving to its canonical slice costs
  a small linear scan, allocates nothing, and makes console ids
  BY CONSTRUCTION identical (same pointer) to hardware ids.
- **Regression test** (`input_tests_console.zig`): the held-id-survives-
  the-frame-arena-reset pin — press on frame 1, `reset(.retain_capacity)`
  + scribble junk over the reused bytes, press the opposite key on frame
  2, assert the first key is STILL held (cursor_direction.x stays 0 in
  the rollover shape). Verified red on the old behavior (expected 0,
  found -1) before landing the fix. The other console tests share one
  arena for the whole script — the reason this class was invisible to
  them; the live loop's per-frame reset is the missing ingredient.
- Design updated in place: DESIGN → Input → Console input's merged-
  payload paragraph now states the static-lifetime requirement and why.
- Post-fix, the console channel is a trustworthy measurement instrument:
  the same rollover script that used to crash now runs deterministically
  and reproduces the arrow-key bug it was sent to measure (cursor stuck
  at (1,0), left press swallowed — see the next entry).

## Arrow-key cursor rollover: the press-direction fallback (snappy fast input)

The report: in a hub or level, pressing right then left in quick
succession registered only the right — the left press vanished. Root
cause (verified per-frame through the real pipeline, headless + live via
the console channel): the nudge design splits TRIGGER from DIRECTION —
the trigger is a `move_cursor_*` edge, but the vector derives from HELD
keys (`cursor_direction`, opposites cancel). A press landing while its
opposite is still held — key ROLLOVER, what fast input actually does —
fired its edge into a zero vector: no movement, edge consumed, and the
opposite's later release produces no new edge. The only rescue was the
synthetic repeat's 300ms initial delay — a quick tap (<300ms) was
swallowed whole. Timing characterization (the console channel's first
measurement job): sequential taps register at ANY speed (verified to
1-frame, ~3ms gaps); same-frame release+press works; only rollover
swallowed. Live frame period measured ≈3.2ms (uncapped loop + 0.1ms
idle yield).

- **Fix — press-direction fallback** (`cursor_press_direction` on
  InGameInput): per-tick direction derived from the REAL press edges
  only (synthetic repeats excluded — `actionPressedOnRealEdge`, which
  reuses `bindingFires` with an empty repeat set so every gate is
  identical to the dispatch pass). `resolveTileCursor` (level/hub arm +
  editor arm) uses the held vector as before, EXCEPT when it cancels to
  zero — then the press edge's own direction carries the intent. A
  rollover press now moves at its own frame, no 300ms wait.
- **Why repeats stay excluded**: deliberately holding both opposites
  freezes the cursor (the cancel is the intent there), and per-key
  repeat timers drift — a repeats-included fallback would oscillate the
  cursor on alternating 40ms repeat edges. A real press is the intent
  signal; a repeat is continuation, ambiguous under cancel.
- **Why not re-fire on the opposite's release**: movement on release is
  odd semantics, and in the fast tap-tap rollover shape the LEFT
  releases before the right — the re-fire would have to fire on a key
  that is no longer held, in the direction of a key released frames
  ago. The press frame is where the intent lives.
- **Nonzero vectors are unchanged** — diagonals still derive from held
  keys (a diagonal fires when either of the two held keys edges); the
  fallback engages only on the zero vector.
- **Tests**: derivation pins in input.zig (rollover press →
  cursor_direction (0,0) + cursor_press_direction (-1,0); repeat edge →
  press direction (0,0)); resolution pins in input_handlers.zig
  (rollover moves, repeats-only frozen, nonzero-vector diagonal
  unchanged, editor arm same); an end-to-end console pin in
  input_tests_console.zig (the reported sequence through the live seam
  — per-frame arena reset, applyFrameCommand → translateInput →
  resolveTileCursor). All verified red with the fallback disabled
  before landing.
- Design: DESIGN → Input → "Cursor nudges" bullet. The mouse-owns-the-
  frame arrow-drop (a different, intermittent signature — a jittering
  resting mouse can eat an arrow edge for a whole frame) is noted in
  TODO → Input/camera leftovers as unmeasured.

## Dump-path walker — `dump <path>` as pure reflection over the live object graph

The console channel's dumps were hand-written flat projections —
fine for the curated click-point inventories (`dump ui`, `dump level`),
drift by definition for the state mirrors (`dump state`, `dump settings`,
`dump bindings`, `dump history` duplicated typed objects by hand; a new
field needed a remembered dump line). Replaced the mirror class with a
comptime field-path walker: a path is a Zig member-access expression —
field names, union tag names, `[n]` indexes — evaluated read-only
against the FrameState the driver holds (`dump
history.current_state.hub.player.position`). Decisions settled in
discussion: full literal paths only (aliases for common roots later,
maybe); depth never limited (the path scopes the dump, not a render
rule); dot-separated single-token grammar (mirrors code syntax — union
tags are segments because `.meta_event` is what the code writes); a
100-element cap with an explicit `(+N more — address by index)` note;
`dump`/`report` verb split with the curated pair staying under `dump`
until the rename slice.

- **`src/dump_walker.zig`** (raylib-free, generic over the root): path
  parsing (segments + index suffixes, charset-validated at parse),
  resolution (structs by field, unions by active tag, optionals
  transparent, slices by bounds-checked index), and type-determined
  rendering — detail propagates through optionals/unions/slices, struct
  fields cut to one-line summaries (compact form when the value fits a
  line, else a type-name token); leaf conventions are the session-log
  writer's. Bare `dump` renders the root table of contents (one level of
  field names — the discovery entry point). Errors are truthful and
  teach: `no field 'player_name' on types.Settings — fields: ...` (this
  one fired live — the player name lives in PlayerData, not Settings,
  and the error said so).
- **Safety invariants, verified before building** (the "can a dump
  mutate or execute?" question): Zig has no name→function dispatch, so
  path segments select data only; the root is const-asserted (mutation
  is a compile error); raw pointers are never followed (`<pointer>` —
  no vtable/allocator is ever dereferenced, cycles unreachable by
  construction); NO method is ever called on a walked value (a Zig
  method is arbitrary code — the walker's contract is that walking
  executes none; this is the invariant future "convenience" additions
  must not break); union descent is active-tag-checked (the UB path
  becomes an error naming the active tag); indexes bounds-checked. A
  canary test walks a battery of deep paths over a real history and
  asserts the state bit-identical after (deepEqual).
- **The compile-time find of the slice**: `ReplayViewerEvent` is an
  EMPTY union (a "none yet" placeholder) — `@field` on an access to
  such a field cannot even lower ("expected pointer, found 'noreturn'"),
  and since the walker instantiates the whole reachable type graph from
  any path, Event's reference to it broke every dump-path compile.
  Every walker recursion site now comptime-guards with `isEmptyUnion`
  (rendering `<uninhabited>` / the no-variants error).
- **console.zig rewiring**: `DumpKind` became a union — `path` (routed
  to the walker, streamed + flushed) alongside the curated `ui`/`level`
  (arena text as before); `applyFrameCommand` gained the `frame_root`
  anytype param (main.frame passes the real FrameState; the walker
  const-asserts it — console.zig still never imports session_setup);
  the four hand-written mirrors deleted; `writers`/`session_log`
  imports went with them.
- **Tests**: walker units (compact forms + ToC, struct/slice/union/
  optional/pointer resolution + every truthful-error shape, cap + note,
  the parse errors), a console routing test through the real
  writer-level seam, and the no-mutation canary. All verified red
  against disabled pieces where applicable (the guard work was
  verified by the compile failure itself).
- Live smoke: the full vocabulary against a running game — including
  `dump history.event_history` rendering the whole session log as one
  readable compact line, and the truthful-error teaching moments.
- Design: DESIGN → Input → Console input → the `dump <path>` bullet
  (grammar, two dump classes, rendering rules, safety invariants).
  Follow-ups tracked in TODO → Console input: the per-frame
  observability stash (`previous_*` fields) and the `report` verb
  split.

## Mission sprite ids minted at the scan (the side quest before the observability stash)

While designing the per-frame observability stash, `PlayerInput`'s one
string payload (`clicked_editor_sprite` — which sprite a picker cell
picked) forced a bounded-copy plan: its bytes were minted PER FRAME by
the picker (allocPrint `custom/<dir>/<stem>` into the frame arena,
pickers:425), so a stashed copy would dangle into the reset arena —
the exact bug class the console id-interning fix addressed. Analysis
(in discussion) showed the mint was misplaced: the namespaced id is a
fact about the SCANNED FILE, not a render fact — re-derived identically
every frame the picker was open (also per-cell-per-frame allocation
churn while the modal is up).

- **Fix — mint at the source**: `MissionSprite.stored_id`
  (`custom/<mission-dir>/<stem>`), allocPrint'd once per file at scan
  time (`rescanEditorMissionSprites`) into backing_allocator, freed
  with the list (the scan's existing per-entry ownership). The picker's
  mission cells REFERENCE it (no mint); the kind-prefixed `graphic_id`
  stays view-minted — it is render-scoped (kind-dependent prefix), and
  it never leaves the frame.
- **The payload chain is now fully owned**: scan (owned, session) →
  button payload (borrow of session bytes) → `clicked_editor_sprite`
  (borrow) → handler → event push (owned deep copy). A same-frame
  borrow of session-lifetime bytes is safe indefinitely — the
  observability stash copies `PlayerInput` wholesale with NO bounded
  buffer, because there is nothing left to dangle.
- Alternatives rejected in the discussion: index payloads (the four
  pick actions span four different lists + two tabs — the stem is the
  only uniform, staleness-free key, and sprite identity is open-ended
  string space); value-carrying Action unions (breaks EnumSet
  fired_actions, bindings, settings serialization, the keybind UI).
- `missionDirectoryName` moved to types.zig (pub — the id-convention's
  own helper, next to `customSpriteDimsPassGate` which parses the same
  ids); the picker's private copy deleted.
- Tests: the scan test pins the minted id at the source
  (`custom/artists_den/boss`); the picker test pins POINTER IDENTITY —
  the built button's payload IS the session list's string (the
  structural no-re-mint property, not just content equality).
- Design updated in place: DESIGN → Architecture → Level Editor → the
  sprite picker's Mission bullet (the scan-mint + why).
- Also flagged in discussion, recorded as a TODO candidate: the
  28-field `clicked_*` payload explosion on AnytimeInput (one
  hand-wired sibling field per payload kind, ~25 copy-paste lines in
  main.zig's dispatch relay) — the clean shape is one tagged-union
  payload field (the SlotRef pattern), a 30–50-site refactor for
  another session.

## The observability stash — previous_player_input / previous_delta / last_taken_command

The gap that closed the dump-path discussion: the console channel could
not see its own subject matter — the per-frame input TRANSLATION (fired
actions, edges, cursor vectors) and the frame DELTA existed only during
`frame()` (the delta previously measured by timing two whole process
runs against each other: 500-frame vs 1500-frame scripts, ~3.2ms/frame).

- **FrameState stash**: `previous_player_input: ?input.PlayerInput` +
  `previous_delta_microseconds: u64`, written once per frame in
  `main.frame` right after translateInput + the console action fold
  (verified: everything below that point only reads player_input).
  The `previous_` naming follows `previous_view_state`. Read order is
  assertion-shaped for free: dumps execute at the START of frame N+1
  (applyFrameCommand), so `press X` then `dump
  previous_player_input...` shows the press frame's translation.
- **`console_queue.last_taken_command`**: recorded at pop in
  takeFrameCommand (any kind — input, dump, quit, WAITS included: a
  wait consumes a frame, so it is the truthful "what took this frame");
  a by-value copy taken before the reader can reuse the slot; an empty
  drain keeps the last record.
- **No bounded buffer needed**: the original plan had a 128-byte copy
  buffer for PlayerInput's one string payload — the side quest
  (mission sprite ids minted at the scan, previous entry) dissolved
  the hazard at the source, so the stash is a plain wholesale copy.
- **Tests**: the taken-command record (press / wait / empty-drain
  keeps-last); the stash dump paths against the real root shape
  (cursor_direction, delta, the sprite payload reads back verbatim).
  Live verification: a script asserting the press frame's edge, the
  held-derived direction on later frames, and the frame delta in one
  command — the exact diagnostics that were impossible before.
- Design: DESIGN → Input → Console input → the observability-stash
  bullet. The `report ui`/`report level` verb split remains in TODO
  (dump-path slice 3), as does the `clicked_*` payload-consolidation
  candidate.

## The `report` verb split — dump is purely the mirror

Dump-path slice 3, closing the set: the curated projections moved off
the `dump` verb — `report ui` / `report level` — so the two dump
classes have two verbs and two visible semantics (`dump <path>` =
pure reflection; `report` = interpretation of derived facts).
`ConsoleCommand.dump` became a plain `PathText` (always a path; the
DumpKind union dissolved) alongside `report: ReportKind` ({ui, level}).
The pre-split spellings (`dump ui`) PARSE as paths and error truthfully
against the root — `no field 'ui' on session_setup.FrameState —
fields: ...` — the redirect itself teaches the new verb. Rider caught
while reshaping: the walker landing had accidentally dropped the
curated dumps' trailing newline (consecutive dumps concatenated);
restored. Design updated in place (DESIGN → Input → Console input →
the dump-paths bullet's class paragraph + the command-set list).

## Input: clicked_* payload consolidation (the ButtonPayload union)

The 28 `clicked_*` payload fields (27 on `AnytimeInput` +
`IdleInput.clicked_save_row`, set by ~25 hand-wired relay lines in
main.zig, each field FOUR touch points — element field, input field,
dispatch line, handler read — with zero compiler help for forgetting
one) collapsed into ONE tagged union, `types.ButtonPayload`, riding
`PlayerInput.clicked_payload`. The design conversation that settled the
shape (the interesting part):

- **The category-error insight (where the blur came from).** Asking
  "does the payload belong to AnytimeInput or IdleInput?" was asking
  data to participate in an action classification. The boundary
  classifies ACTIONS by when they may consume; the payload never
  consumes anything by itself, so it has no consumption timing to
  classify — it inherits its action's. `PlayerInput` already had the
  family for frame-level facts transcending the classification
  (`pointer`, `modifiers`, the two outcomes, `fired_actions` — itself
  action-LAYER data correctly living above the split); the payload
  joined it. This retroactively names why `fired_actions` lives where
  it lives, and gives every future input datum a placement test.
  Recorded as DESIGN → Input → the PlayerInput placement rule.
- **Two near-misses the rule flags and explains (both stay):**
  `IdleInput.tile_clicked` fails the INERT half (handleIdleInput
  mutates it mid-consumption — Enter folds the cursor into it — a
  resolution value, not a frame fact); `IdleInput.skill_slot_selected`
  is not click identity (the `.skill_slot_N` action itself encodes it;
  the payload channel exists only when the action does NOT encode the
  identity, which is also why the Digit bridges differ — they map a
  different keyboard action onto the click action + payload).
- **SlotRef purity.** `SlotRef.save_file` existed in the drag-domain
  union purely to carry the save-row click payload ("Save rows are
  never drag sources" was an explicit dead guard arm in
  dragToOrchestrator) — a fit by SlotRef's own doc comment. Save rows
  now ride `.save_row`; `SlotRef` is back to exactly its four drag
  domains, and `slotContentSize`/`slotContentIcon`/view's drag-ghost
  switch dropped their save_file arms.
- **Compound identities are one struct variant, not two fields**: a
  weapon-type cell is `{ gear_slot, weapon_type }` (the five
  two-payload consumption sites forced this); item-kind cells carry
  `{ kind, weapon_type: ?WeaponType = null }` (non-weapon cells leave
  it null — the old separate-field defaulting, inside the variant).
  Null-MEANINGFUL identities keep the optional inside the variant
  (`.editor_layer` null = the picker's add mode, `.editor_skill` null
  = the picker's None cell — `payloadAs` flattens the inner optional so
  call sites read exactly like the old per-field optionals).
- **The table + fail-fast + no-orphan walk.** `types.actionButtonPayload`
  is the `actionBindingContexts` pattern applied to payloads: an
  exhaustive switch (payload-less actions NAMED in grouped null arms, no
  else — a new Action is a compile error until its payload story is
  decided) mapping each action to its one variant; main.zig's relay (now
  ONE line) checks the button's payload against it and panics on a
  mismatch — the exact silent-eat class (`orelse return` eating a
  wrong/missing payload) this whole seam exists to kill. A comptime
  walk makes a variant no action names a compile error (dead union
  members, the minimize-pub/dead-code ethos applied to variants).
  Console `action` commands still carry no payload — a payload-needing
  action fired that way no-ops at the arm by design (the payload IS
  the click); `payloadAs` is the belt-and-suspenders behind the relay.

Numbers: element.zig's `Button` lost 23 optional payload fields for
one `payload: ?ButtonPayload`; input.zig lost 27+1 fields for one on
`PlayerInput`; main.zig's ~25 relay lines became one;
input_handlers.zig gained the `payloadAs`/`PayloadAsType` consumption
seam (its `@setEvalBranchQuota` — the comptime field walk crosses the
default eval-branch quota once instantiated for many variants); the
five `applyAction` Digit bridges construct variants. No event-log,
file-format, or version impact — the payload is input-side transient
and never crosses the input→event seam.

The test sweep (109 sites in handler_tests_editor.zig) validated the
dry-run discipline's own warning: a naive per-call regex block
(`.*?\},`) broke on `.clicked_editor_tool = .{ .entity_type = 1 }`
(inner braces end the "block" early) — the inventory pass surfaced it
before any write (the `select_editor_tool` tuple was missing). The
real sweep is a brace-depth state machine driven by the ACTION in the
call (the action names the variant, compounds collect their two fields,
anything unexpected asserts). The no-payload call sites (the other
argument-count class) were swept shape-by-shape with the compiler as
the checklist. 824/824 pass.

Rider: the Action enum's doc comments carried 41
`AnytimeInput.clicked_X` references — all swept to the
payload-variant phrasing in the same change (a doc naming a dead
field reads as truth). DESIGN → Input gained the two bullets (Button
payloads + the placement rule); the load-save / level-editor /
settings / console sections' payload references updated to the union
spelling.

## Console: the console-ready prompt (TTY-gated, game-thread printed)

The interactive half of the console channel's missing discoverability
surface (the other half — `help`/`inputs` — lands next): a `> ` prompt
marking "the channel can take the next line."

- **The game thread prints it, never the reader.** stdout already had
  exactly one writer (the game thread, via the queue's output — the
  reader writes only stderr); a reader-side "print before each blocking
  read" would add a second stdout writer and a guaranteed cosmetic
  race — the reader prints the next `> ` immediately after push, and
  the next frame's dump output lands glued to the stale prompt. The
  game thread's version is naturally ordered (a `dump`'s output writes
  first, then the prompt — same thread, sequential). gdb's architecture
  lesson, applied.
- **Printed at boot + after each processed command when the frame drain
  left the queue empty** — pasted multi-line input prompts once, after
  the last command, not per line; a mid-script backlog never prompts;
  `quit` prints none; mid-hold frames print none by construction
  (`wait`/`wait idle` arm inside `takeFrameCommand`, never reaching the
  caller's switch).
- **TTY-gated** (`isTty(stdin)` at native wiring →
  `ConsoleQueue.interactive`): the gate silences only the prompt — the
  channel itself stays always-on by design (a piped script drives
  identically, just unprompted: a prompt over a pipe is a lie, it
  invites typing the pipe can never receive; console transcripts are
  first-class artifacts — replay fixtures, TAS logs — that prompts
  would pollute). An stdin-less launch (double-click, the mac bundle)
  prints nothing — the zero-cost property preserved.

`promptDue` (the bool predicate — quit/interactive/drained) is the
unit-tested core; `printPrompt` is the thin best-effort writer (pub for
the native driver's boot prompt). applyFrameCommand's switch was
restructured to compute-then-prompt-then-return (labeled blocks — an
unlabeled prong block's trailing value is a 0.16 parse quirk).

## Console: help + inputs — one verb table owns the vocabulary

The discoverability half of the console channel (the prompt landed
first): `help` (the command list) + `inputs` (the input-id vocabulary) +
the boot hint, built on the structural decision that one table owns
everything.

- **The verb table (the both-ways machine-walk).** The parser's if-chain
  over hand-compared verb strings became ONE comptime declaration,
  `verb_table` in console.zig: name, argument shape, description, real
  example lines, and a per-verb parse fn. The parser dispatches on
  `name`; `help` prints the entries (column width comptime-derived from
  the table's own widest usage pair, so added verbs realign
  automatically); the both-ways test parses every example (everything
  the printed help shows is a tested-working command line) and requires
  every `ConsoleCommand` variant to be covered by ≥1 example (a new
  variant is a test failure until the help table covers it). Three
  hand-written lists died with it: the parser arms, the unknown-verb
  error's inline verb list, and the would-be help table. The
  unknown-verb error now points at `help`; the unknown-id error points
  at `inputs`.
- **`inputs` — the id vocabulary, derived.** Prints
  `producible_key_ids` + `producible_mouse_ids` straight from the
  arrays the parser validates against (and the same ids the settings
  bindings name): it cannot lie, and new ids appear automatically. The
  category grouping (modifiers → letters → digits → punctuation →
  navigation → F-keys → numpad → media) emerges from the tables'
  existing order wrapped at 80 columns — no hand-maintained grouping.
- **Ids stay strict exact-match — discoverable instead of forgiving.**
  The `press Key1` trap (digits are `Digit1`) is solved by the list,
  not by aliases: one canonical spelling is shared by command lines,
  session logs, and bindings files, and an accepted alias would beg the
  reverse question of which spelling a dumped binding uses.
- **The boot hint** (interactive only): "console input on stdin — type
  help for the command list" + the first prompt at wiring; the prompt
  says a console exists, the hint says how to learn it.
  (`announceConsoleInput` also fixed a commit-1 gap the smoke test
  caught: the boot prompt printed unconditionally — piped runs got a
  stray `> ` — before the gate moved into the announcement.)

Verified by driving the real binary both ways: piped (`help` prints,
no prompts anywhere, `quit` silent) and interactive via a pty
(`script -qec`): boot hint + prompt, the post-drain prompt after a
sole command, none after `quit` or mid-backlog.

## Session reflection: ButtonPayload + the console's discoverability

Three commits (each carries its own entry above): the `clicked_*`
payload consolidation, the console-ready prompt, and `help`/`inputs` on
one verb table. The durable lessons beyond the per-commit records,
now in their homes:

- **A sweep script's own asserts can lose its applied work** — the
  assert-then-write-all shape rolled back applied fixes twice in one
  session before the shape changed to write-per-step. AGENTS → Build &
  Test → the sweep-script bullet carries the rule now (and a stray `d`
  typo on that very bullet — the one that had been garbling "full diff"
  — is fixed with it).
- **Compiles ≠ runs generalizes beyond the platform seams.** The
  console channel's stdout/TTY behavior is invisible to the headless
  suite (a prompt, a boot hint, output interleaving); the console
  prompt's FIRST commit shipped an ungated boot prompt with 824 tests
  passing, caught in seconds by a piped smoke run against the real
  binary. AGENTS → Build & Test now carries CONSOLE COMPILES ≠ CONSOLE
  RUNS with both smoke shapes (piped + pty — the pty exercises the TTY
  gate, which a plain pipe cannot).
- **The 0.16 labeled-block prong quirk** (verified by minimal repro, not
  just encountered): a switch prong with a result type needs
  `blk: { ... break :blk value; }` to yield; an unlabeled block's
  trailing value is a parse error. In AGENTS → Zig 0.16 Gotchas.
- **handler_tests_editor's 181 identical call shapes** noted in TODO →
  Tech Debt as fold-into-next-touch polish (the payload argument change
  rippled ~200 sites across five test files — the cost of no shared
  call helper).

The session also validated the doc system end to end: every design
question resolved by pointing at an existing settled rule (the
PlayerInput placement rule was *articulated from* the existing shape,
SlotRef's own doc convicted `save_file`, strict-exact-match settled the
alias question), and the TODO's `clicked_*` candidate note from a prior
reflection seeded the session's whole first task — the open-question →
design → done loop doing exactly what AGENTS.md says it does.

## Gradient index surfacing — the theme picker's number column + the metadata sidebar's swatch numbers

The theme picker showed bare swatch strips (no labels — "the colors ARE
the content"), and the metadata sidebar's gradient rows showed the
effective colors with no index — an author picking gradients had no way
to see WHICH gradient (the 0-based index that `color_themes.txt`'s
`gradient_index` lines and the level's stored keys
`color_wheel_index` / `enemy_gradient_index` / `player_gradient_index`
use). Both surfaces now show the number:

- **Theme picker** (`src/ui/editor_pickers.zig`): a number column left
  of each strip — right-aligned digits (columns line up), vertically
  centered in the 128px row, sized to the WIDEST row number; the
  index-column + strip + scrollbar cluster stays centered as a unit.
- **Metadata sidebar** (`src/ui/editor_inspector.zig`): the role's
  EFFECTIVE gradient index flush right on the gradient row's label
  line (the control line's Auto + swatch geometry untouched); null
  level (defensive path) shows no number, mirroring the picker's
  stale-level no-highlight.
- **`loaders.effectiveGradientIndex`** — the new single source for the
  effective index (the role's override while manual, the auto-derived
  one otherwise), normalized by the SAME modulo
  `deriveActiveColorTheme` applies. Both surfaces call it, so the
  sidebar number, the picker's current-row highlight, and the active
  theme's actual colors can never disagree. This also fixed a latent
  quirk: the picker previously compared the RAW level indices, so a
  hand-edited out-of-range `color_wheel_index` (e.g. 30 of 24
  gradients) displayed the modded colors but highlighted no row.

0-based by decision (matches the config value — the point of showing
it). Tests: the picker's census gains per-row index-label assertions
(one per gradient, right edges aligned); the sidebar's census content
list gains the three numbers, and the semantic walk asserts each
visible gradient row's number by line association (world 0, enemy
auto-derived 1, player manual 2). DESIGN → Level Editor updated at the
two surfaces' descriptions.

## Gradient spacing rule + report — the "too close" colors made measurable

The gradient wheel's 1→2 steps were too small across the yellow corner of
the wheel — gradient 0 (the default theme everywhere) rendered its even
tiles at color 1 against a color 2 background at WCAG contrast 1.03:
effectively the same color. Root cause structural: the renderer places the
ramp's WEAK pair (the small 1→2 step of the artist's 6-step ramps) in the
most contrast-critical adjacent roles (even tiles at 1, background at 2).

- **`src/gradient_report.zig`** (`zig build gradient-report`, wrapped by
  `scripts/gradient_report.sh` — the sound_report pattern): reads
  `data/color_themes.txt` through the game's own parser + loader and writes
  `gradient_report.md` — ΔE76 per adjacent ramp step, the three structural
  seams (tiles-vs-background, checkerboard, odd-tile-vs-background) with
  WCAG contrast ratios, flags, and computed slide repairs (the violating
  step's darker color slides along its own ramp toward its darker neighbor
  until it clears the floor + 0.5 headroom; the repair for the
  tiles-vs-background class moves only the background color). Run-at-will
  reference, NOT a build step (unlike the SDF atlas) and NOT a test gate —
  the thresholds may become a gate later once calibrated against what
  reads well in play.
- **The rule** (settled in DESIGN → Level Editor → Level theme): any two
  renderer-adjacent colors ≥ ΔE 6 apart; structural seams keep WCAG
  contrast ≥ 1.06. Calibrated on the shipped wheel: broken seams at
  ΔE 5.4–5.6, fine seams start ~6.8.
- **The artist's original wheel is preserved at commit `a4148d5`** — the
  report snapshot committed BEFORE any color change. The fix commit
  regenerates the report, so the two commits' `gradient_report.md` diff
  shows exactly what the fix changed.
- **The fix**: three single-hex color_2 edits (the slide repairs): gradient
  0 `#f2eb82`→`#e8df7b`, gradient 3 `#bec761`→`#b9c05e`, gradient 22
  `#f0bb6e`→`#eab66b` — all three 1-2 seams move from ΔE ~5.5 to ~6.5, the
  2-3 steps keep ≥ 7.9 slack, and the report reads CLEAN. Gradients 1, 2,
  23 sit just above the floor (ΔE 6.0–6.2, legal) — left as-is for now;
  the report shows them as the weakest legal, an artist call whether to
  widen the yellow corner consistently later.

## Font migration: FreeZilla → Cause (SIL OFL 1.1) + license texts embedded in the exe

The unfinished FreeZilla handwriting face (76 of 95 ASCII glyphs; the
0.5em fallback in `measureSpanWidth` papered over the gaps) is replaced by
Cause Medium (`assets/fonts/cause-medium.ttf` from
https://github.com/xconsau/Cause — Saurabh Sharma / intothedesign, © The
Cause Project Authors). Weight chosen by in-game comparison: Regular
shipped first for parity, Medium read better against the 8px black
outline (a face flip is a two-path change — build.zig's generator input +
text.zig's fallback read — so iterating on weights is cheap). The
migration surface was tiny by construction: the
font's identity lived in exactly two sites — `build.zig`'s SDF-generator
input (dependency-tracked, so the build-time SDF atlas regenerated
automatically) and `src/raylib/text.zig`'s runtime fallback read. All other
machinery (base size 128, SDF encoding constants, shader, runtime-derived
`FontMetrics`) is font-agnostic and survived untouched; the headless suite
never touches the font.

Why static, not the variable font: the whole pipeline (generator + fallback)
is stb_truetype via raylib, which has no variable-font support — it renders
the default instance (wght 400 = Regular) and ignores fvar/gvar. The
variable file would render identically to the static Regular while
embedding ~110 KB instead of ~56 KB. The remaining statics slot in later as
second faces if the bold/italic TODO item lands (Cause has no italic —
fake-italic or drop, decided then).

**Licensing (OFL 1.1, read before bundling):** no Reserved Font Name is
declared; we ship unmodified (Original Version), so all conditions are
satisfied trivially — bundling with software is explicitly permitted. Two
new obligations handled:
- `LICENSE-FONT.txt` (root, matching LICENSE-CODE/GRAPHICS/AUDIO) + a README
  "## Licenses" bullet crediting "The Cause Project Authors" (the copyright
  line in the OFL and the TTF name table) and Saurabh Sharma (designer,
  nameID 9 in the font's own metadata — the Google Fonts convention of
  copyright line + designer credit).
- **The binary gap:** root licenses never reached the shipped artifact —
  `generateAssetsFile` embeds only `data/` and `assets/`, so the single-file
  exe (and the web build, same shape) carried the font TTF + its SDF-derived
  atlas blob with no license text anywhere. OFL condition 2 requires each
  copy to carry the copyright notice + license ("stand-alone text files …
  or machine-readable metadata fields within text or binary files"); a bare
  exe has no "alongside". Fixed structurally: `collectLicenseFiles` (in
  build.zig, the `collectContentFiles` pattern) scans the project root for
  `LICENSE-*.txt` and adds them to the embedded map — so ALL license texts
  (MIT code, CC-BY-SA graphics + audio, OFL font) now ride inside every
  distributed copy, closing the same latent CC-BY-SA "license text must
  accompany distributions" gap for the art and audio too. Scanned, not
  hardcoded: a new root LICENSE-*.txt lands embedded automatically. Found
  one bug on the way: `entry.name` from dir iteration dies at the next
  `iter.next()` — the first version passed it un-copied and emitted garbage
  bytes as embed keys; `b.dupe` fixes it.

OFL nuance noted: the build-time SDF atlas is a format-converted derivative
of the font (OFL's Modified Version definition includes "changing
formats"), so condition 5 (derivatives stay under OFL) applies to it —
satisfied by shipping TTF + blob + license text together inside the exe,
no relicensing of anything.

## 9-slice small panels: the smeared border (run-axis LOD minification)

The header-only tooltips (undo/redo/gear/skills — a single 64px row:
`lineHeight(64)=76 + 2*24 padding = 124` tall, ~212-270 wide) rendered their
top/bottom border lines as a vertical gray-gradient smear while large panels
stayed crisp — at EVERY `render_resolution` preset, with the corners always
correct. That last fact was the decisive clue: the mechanism had to be
aspect-driven, not resolution-driven.

Root cause (found via a temporary raylib host tool — `tools/
nine_slice_probe.zig`, the `sdf_atlas_generator` pattern: same texture load
pipeline incl. premultiply + generated mips + trilinear, same
`beginTextureMode` + `beginMode2D(zoom = renderScale)` pass shape, same piece
math + the sprite-pass LOD-bias shader, GPU readback exported as PNGs): a
NARROW panel's top/bottom edge pieces span the whole source width
(`texture_width - 2*corner` = 260 texels for the 124-tall tooltip) but land
in a destination only ~88 reference px wide — the piece minifies ~3-6x
along its RUN axis, dragging the texture LOD 2+ mip levels down where the
10px border stroke is box-averaged to 1-2px; trilinear ghost-blends those
thin levels into the sample → the smear. Large panels' edge pieces MAGNIFY
along the run axis, so the LOD stays pinned by the cross axis's exact 2:1
(clean mip1) → crisp. Corners are square 1:1 in both — always correct. The
sprite-pass `spriteLodSnapBias` (renderScale term) can't fix it — the bias
snaps the renderScale LOD term, not the piece's own aspect term (probe
`current` vs `current_nobias` at 720p: the bias helps, the smear stays).

The fix: `ui.nineSlicePiecesAtScale` (pure, unit-tested — element.zig)
crops each edge/center piece's source span on its RUN axis to the
destination's span in TARGET pixels (dest ref px × renderScale), window
centered — the run-axis LOD term collapses to 0 and the border samples at
its true thickness. Piece roles: top/bottom edges crop width, left/right
crop height, center both, corners never (square 1:1 by construction); the
CROSS axis is never cropped (already 1:1 in reference space — cropping it
cuts into the border; the probe's first crop version did exactly that and
the border vanished). `drawNineSlice` (draw.zig) now calls it with
`backend.renderScale()`; `nineSlicePieces` de-pub'd (internal to element.zig
now), the ui.zig facade swaps the re-export. Probe validation (undo-tooltip
top border profile, `K`=border, digits=gray): current
`KKKKK814www` (smeared) → crop `KKKKKK17www` — PIXEL-IDENTICAL to the large
panel at 1080p, equal at every preset.

The centered crop window is invisible in today's edge art (uniform along
the run axis); when patterned panel art ships, the TODO 9-slice tiling
refinement supersedes the window choice for narrow panels. The probe (tool
+ `zig build nine-slice-probe` wiring + PNGs) was temporary by agreement and
is fully reverted — this entry carries the method + findings.

## Art report — the machine-derived sprite inventory (scripts/art_report.sh)

`src/art_report.zig` (`zig build art-report`, wrapped by `scripts/
art_report.sh` — the sound_report.sh pattern) enumerates every sprite id the
game can consume and writes `art_report.md`: per-id status (shipped /
shadowed / MISSING-draws-magenta — no fallbacks, so the status column is
the whole truth) plus the shipped sprites no shipped content references. Three
machine-walked sources, no hand-maintained list:

- **Engine enums + derivation shapes:** skills via `ui.skillIconSpriteId`
  (called per SkillId — zero drift), effect overlays via each definition's
  `effect_sprite` (via `generated_lookups`), items via the Item-union tags +
  WeaponType subtags (a mirror of `ui.itemIconSpriteId`'s closed set), and
  weapons via WeaponType (a mirror of view.zig's
  `weapons/{enemy_}?<type>` derivation). The effect ICON ids are not walked
  separately: `ui.effectIconSpriteId` resolves to the skill icon, the
  effects/<x> overlay, or the display name (not a sprite id) — the first two
  are already covered, the third is not id-shaped.
- **Every sprite-id string literal in shipped code under src/** (the
  tool's own file excluded — its manual notes would self-report; test
  blocks excluded — fixture ids are structure-asserted, never loaded, and
  would put phantom assets on the shopping list). This is the truth for
  the UI/world icon set — no enum to walk.
- **Every `sprite <stem>` reference in shipped data** (levels, hubs,
  decorations.txt, editor_defaults.txt), mapped by section header:
  Entities -> entities/, Decorations -> decorations/, NPCs -> npcs/ (the
  loaders' namespace derivation mirrored).

Two hand-maintained notes live IN the tool (`manual_notes`, each retires
when its condition lands): the redo-button `ui/icon_undo` double duty
(icon_redo is not code-referenced — the TODO wrinkle, resolved by the
note), and the `npcs/` palette being future stock for the campaign
editor's npc_type model.

First-run findings: **6 MISSING** (ui/icon_swap, ui/momentum,
ui/icon_undo, ui/icon_playtest, ui/icon_validate — plus the
report-discovered ui/close_button from element.zig), and **9 unreferenced** —
the six new enemies (frog/ghoul/mushroom/snake/specter + raider — shipped
art no official content spawns yet), plain skeleton, and the two NPC
sprites. The
'orphan' framing was corrected on review: entity + decoration sprites
are editor palette stock BY DESIGN — every shipped sprite is
player-placeable, so unreferenced-by-shipped-content is NOT unused; the
report's section + row wording now says palette stock instead of
'nothing consumes it'. The first cut of the literal scanner INCLUDED test blocks
("conservative"), which put six phantom ids on the shopping list (the
editor-shell palette-composition test's fixtures — custom_fighter,
skeleton_armor, moss_vine etc. — never loaded, never drawn); the user
caught it asking what custom_fighter was, and the scanner now excludes
test blocks exactly (zig-fmt'd test declarations are top-level and close
with a lone `}` at column 0). The TODO's hand-maintained
missing-art notes (Cross-cutting polish, Platform Layer's Missing-art
audit, the View section's placeholder-id list) now point at the report
instead; the NEXT-UP art-report item is checked off. AGENTS' machine-walked
-truth pattern list gained `art_report.zig`.
